abstract.haxe_doc:
`Any` is a type that is compatible with any other in both ways.
This means that a value of any type can be assigned to `Any`, and vice-versa, a value of `Any` type can be assigned to any other type.
It's a more type-safe alternative to `Dynamic`, because it doesn't support field access or operators and it's bound to monomorphs. So, to work with the actual value, it needs to be explicitly promoted to another type.

length.haxe_doc: The length of `this` Array.

concat.haxe_doc:
Returns a new Array by appending the elements of `a` to the elements of `this` Array.
This operation does not modify `this` Array.
If `a` is the empty Array `[]`, a copy of `this` Array is returned.
The length of the returned Array is equal to the sum of `this.length` and `a.length`.
If `a` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

join.haxe_doc:
Returns a string representation of `this` Array, with `sep` separating each element.
The result of this operation is equal to `Std.string(this[0]) + sep + Std.string(this[1]) + sep + ... + sep + Std.string(this[this.length-1])`
If `this` is the empty Array `[]`, the result is the empty String `""`. If `this` has exactly one element, the result is equal to a call to `Std.string(this[0])`.
If `sep` is null, the result is unspecified.

pop.haxe_doc:
Removes the last element of `this` Array and returns it.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
If `this` has at least one element, `this.length` will decrease by 1.
If `this` is the empty Array `[]`, null is returned and the length remains 0.

push.haxe_doc:
Adds the element `x` at the end of `this` Array and returns the new length of `this` Array.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
`this.length` increases by 1.

reverse.haxe_doc:
Reverse the order of elements of `this` Array.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
If `this.length < 2`, `this` remains unchanged.

shift.haxe_doc:
Removes the first element of `this` Array and returns it.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
If `this` has at least one element, `this`.length and the index of each remaining element is decreased by 1.
If `this` is the empty Array `[]`, `null` is returned and the length remains 0.

slice.haxe_doc:
Creates a shallow copy of the range of `this` Array, starting at and including `pos`, up to but not including `end`.
This operation does not modify `this` Array.
The elements are not copied and retain their identity.
If `end` is omitted or exceeds `this.length`, it defaults to the end of `this` Array.
If `pos` or `end` are negative, their offsets are calculated from the end of `this` Array by `this.length + pos` and `this.length + end` respectively. If this yields a negative value, 0 is used instead.
If `pos` exceeds `this.length` or if `end` is less than or equals `pos`, the result is `[]`.

sort.haxe_doc:
Sorts `this` Array according to the comparison function `f`, where `f(x,y)` returns 0 if x == y, a positive Int if x > y and a negative Int if x < y.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
The sort operation is not guaranteed to be stable, which means that the order of equal elements may not be retained. For a stable Array sorting algorithm, `haxe.ds.ArraySort.sort()` can be used instead.
If `f` is null, the result is unspecified.

splice.haxe_doc:
Removes `len` elements from `this` Array, starting at and including `pos`, an returns them.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
If `len` is < 0 or `pos` exceeds `this`.length, an empty Array [] is returned and `this` Array is unchanged.
If `pos` is negative, its value is calculated from the end of `this` Array by `this.length + pos`. If this yields a negative value, 0 is used instead.
If the sum of the resulting values for `len` and `pos` exceed `this.length`, this operation will affect the elements from `pos` to the end of `this` Array.
The length of the returned Array is equal to the new length of `this` Array subtracted from the original length of `this` Array. In other words, each element of the original `this` Array either remains in `this` Array or becomes an element of the returned Array.

toString.haxe_doc:
Returns a string representation of `this` Array.
The result will include the individual elements' String representations separated by comma. The enclosing [ ] may be missing on some platforms, use `Std.string()` to get a String representation that is consistent across platforms.

unshift.haxe_doc:
Adds the element `x` at the start of `this` Array.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
`this.length` and the index of each Array element increases by 1.

insert.haxe_doc:
Inserts the element `x` at the position `pos`.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
The offset is calculated like so:
- If `pos` exceeds `this.length`, the offset is `this.length`. - If `pos` is negative, the offset is calculated from the end of `this` Array, i.e. `this.length + pos`. If this yields a negative value, the offset is 0. - Otherwise, the offset is `pos`.
If the resulting offset does not exceed `this.length`, all elements from and including that offset to the end of `this` Array are moved one index ahead.

remove.haxe_doc:
Removes the first occurrence of `x` in `this` Array.
This operation modifies `this` Array in place.
If `x` is found by checking standard equality, it is removed from `this` Array and all following elements are reindexed accordingly. The function then returns true.
If `x` is not found, `this` Array is not changed and the function returns false.

contains.haxe_doc:
Returns whether `this` Array contains `x`.
If `x` is found by checking standard equality, the function returns `true`, otherwise the function returns `false`.

indexOf.haxe_doc:
Returns position of the first occurrence of `x` in `this` Array, searching front to back.
If `x` is found by checking standard equality, the function returns its index.
If `x` is not found, the function returns -1.
If `fromIndex` is specified, it will be used as the starting index to search from, otherwise search starts with zero index. If it is negative, it will be taken as the offset from the end of `this` Array to compute the starting index. If given or computed starting index is less than 0, the whole array will be searched, if it is greater than or equal to the length of `this` Array, the function returns -1.

lastIndexOf.haxe_doc:
Returns position of the last occurrence of `x` in `this` Array, searching back to front.
If `x` is found by checking standard equality, the function returns its index.
If `x` is not found, the function returns -1.
If `fromIndex` is specified, it will be used as the starting index to search from, otherwise search starts with the last element index. If it is negative, it will be taken as the offset from the end of `this` Array to compute the starting index. If given or computed starting index is greater than or equal to the length of `this` Array, the whole array will be searched, if it is less than 0, the function returns -1.

copy.haxe_doc:
Returns a shallow copy of `this` Array.
The elements are not copied and retain their identity, so `a[i] == a.copy()[i]` is true for any valid `i`. However, `a == a.copy()` is always false.

iterator.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of the Array values.

keyValueIterator.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of the Array indices and values.

map.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Array by applying function `f` to all elements of `this`.
The order of elements is preserved.
If `f` is null, the result is unspecified.

filter.haxe_doc:
Returns an Array containing those elements of `this` for which `f` returned true.
The individual elements are not duplicated and retain their identity.
If `f` is null, the result is unspecified.

resize.haxe_doc:
Set the length of the Array.
If `len` is shorter than the array's current size, the last `length - len` elements will be removed. If `len` is longer, the Array will be extended, with new elements set to a target-specific default value:
- always null on dynamic targets - 0, 0.0 or false for Int, Float and Bool respectively on static targets - null for other types on static targets

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new Array.

now.haxe_doc: Returns a Date representing the current local time.

fromTime.haxe_doc: Creates a Date from the timestamp (in milliseconds) `t`.

fromString.haxe_doc:
Creates a Date from the formatted string `s`. The following formats are accepted by the function:
- `"YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss"` - `"YYYY-MM-DD"` - `"hh:mm:ss"`
The first two formats expressed a date in local time. The third is a time relative to the UTC epoch.

getTime.haxe_doc:
Returns the timestamp (in milliseconds) of `this` date. On cpp and neko, this function only has a second resolution, so the result will always be a multiple of `1000.0`, e.g. `1454698271000.0`. To obtain the current timestamp with better precision on cpp and neko, see the `Sys.time` API.
For measuring time differences with millisecond accuracy on all platforms, see `haxe.Timer.stamp`.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a string representation of `this` Date in the local timezone using the standard format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. See `DateTools.format` for other formatting rules.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new date object from the given arguments.
The behaviour of a Date instance is only consistent across platforms if the the arguments describe a valid date.
- month: 0 to 11 (note that this is zero-based) - day: 1 to 31 - hour: 0 to 23 - min: 0 to 59 - sec: 0 to 59

class.haxe_doc:
The Date class provides a basic structure for date and time related information. Date instances can be created by
- `new Date()` for a specific date, - `Date.now()` to obtain information about the current time, - `Date.fromTime()` with a given timestamp or - `Date.fromString()` by parsing from a String.
There are some extra functions available in the `DateTools` class.
In the context of Haxe dates, a timestamp is defined as the number of milliseconds elapsed since 1st January 1970 UTC.
## Supported range
Due to platform limitations, only dates in the range 1970 through 2038 are supported consistently. Some targets may support dates outside this range, depending on the OS at runtime. The `Date.fromTime` method will not work with timestamps outside the range on any target.

match.haxe_doc:
Tells if `this` regular expression matches String `s`.
This method modifies the internal state.
If `s` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

matched.haxe_doc:
Returns the matched sub-group `n` of `this` EReg.
This method should only be called after `this.match` or `this.matchSub`, and then operates on the String of that operation.
The index `n` corresponds to the n-th set of parentheses in the pattern of `this` EReg. If no such sub-group exists, the result is unspecified.
If `n` equals 0, the whole matched substring is returned.

matchedPos.haxe_doc:
Returns the position and length of the last matched substring, within the String which was last used as argument to `this.match` or `this.matchSub`.
If the most recent call to `this.match` or `this.matchSub` did not match anything, the result is unspecified.
If the global g modifier was in place for the matching, the position and length of the leftmost substring is returned.

matchSub.haxe_doc:
Tells if `this` regular expression matches a substring of String `s`.
This function expects `pos` and `len` to describe a valid substring of `s`, or else the result is unspecified. To get more robust behavior, `this.match(s.substr(pos,len))` can be used instead.
This method modifies the internal state.
If `s` is null, the result is unspecified.

split.haxe_doc:
Splits String `s` at all substrings `this` EReg matches.
If a match is found at the start of `s`, the result contains a leading empty String "" entry.
If a match is found at the end of `s`, the result contains a trailing empty String "" entry.
If two matching substrings appear next to each other, the result contains the empty String `""` between them.
By default, this method splits `s` into two parts at the first matched substring. If the global g modifier is in place, `s` is split at each matched substring.
If `s` is null, the result is unspecified.

replace.haxe_doc:
Replaces the first substring of `s` which `this` EReg matches with `by`.
If `this` EReg does not match any substring, the result is `s`.
By default, this method replaces only the first matched substring. If the global g modifier is in place, all matched substrings are replaced.
If `by` contains `$1` to `$9`, the digit corresponds to number of a matched sub-group and its value is used instead. If no such sub-group exists, the replacement is unspecified. The string `$$` becomes `$`.
If `s` or `by` are null, the result is unspecified.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new regular expression with pattern `r` and modifiers `opt`.
This is equivalent to the shorthand syntax `~/r/opt`
If `r` or `opt` are null, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
The EReg class represents regular expressions.
While basic usage and patterns consistently work across platforms, some more complex operations may yield different results. This is a necessary trade- off to retain a certain level of performance.
EReg instances can be created by calling the constructor, or with the special syntax `~/pattern/modifier`
EReg instances maintain an internal state, which is affected by several of its methods.
A detailed explanation of the supported operations is available at <https://haxe.org/manual/std-regex.html>

abstract.haxe_doc:
An abstract type that represents an Enum type.
The corresponding enum instance type is `EnumValue`.
See `Type` for the Haxe Reflection API.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/types-enum-instance.html

hasNext.haxe_doc: Returns true if the iterator has other items, false otherwise.

next.haxe_doc:
Moves to the next item of the iterator.
If this is called while hasNext() is false, the result is unspecified.

new.haxe_doc:
Iterates from `min` (inclusive) to `max` (exclusive).
If `max <= min`, the iterator will not act as a countdown.

class.haxe_doc:
IntIterator is used for implementing interval iterations.
It is usually not used explicitly, but through its special syntax: `min...max`
While it is possible to assign an instance of IntIterator to a variable or field, it is worth noting that IntIterator does not reset after being used in a for-loop. Subsequent uses of the same instance will then have no effect.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/lf-iterators.html

array.haxe_doc:
Creates an Array from Iterable `it`.
If `it` is an Array, this function returns a copy of it.

list.haxe_doc:
Creates a List form Iterable `it`.
If `it` is a List, this function returns a copy of it.

has.haxe_doc:
Tells if `it` contains `elt`.
This function returns true as soon as an element is found which is equal to `elt` according to the `==` operator.
If no such element is found, the result is false.

exists.haxe_doc:
Tells if `it` contains an element for which `f` is true.
This function returns true as soon as an element is found for which a call to `f` returns true.
If no such element is found, the result is false.
If `f` is null, the result is unspecified.

fold.haxe_doc:
Functional fold on Iterable `it`, using function `f` with start argument `first`.
If `it` has no elements, the result is `first`.
Otherwise the first element of `it` is passed to `f` alongside `first`. The result of that call is then passed to `f` with the next element of `it`, and so on until `it` has no more elements.
If `it` or `f` are null, the result is unspecified.

indexOf.haxe_doc:
Returns the index of the first element `v` within Iterable `it`.
This function uses operator `==` to check for equality.
If `v` does not exist in `it`, the result is -1.

find.haxe_doc:
Returns the first element of `it` for which `f` is true.
This function returns as soon as an element is found for which a call to `f` returns true.
If no such element is found, the result is null.
If `f` is null, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Lambda` class is a collection of methods to support functional programming. It is ideally used with `using Lambda` and then acts as an extension to Iterable types.
On static platforms, working with the Iterable structure might be slower than performing the operations directly on known types, such as Array and List.
If the first argument to any of the methods is null, the result is unspecified.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-Lambda.html

sqrt.haxe_doc:
Returns the square root of `v`.
- If `v` is negative (including `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`) or `NaN`, the result is `NaN`. - If `v` is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`. - If `v` is `0.0`, the result is `0.0`.

abs.haxe_doc:
Returns the absolute value of `v`.
- If `v` is positive or `0`, the result is unchanged. Otherwise the result is `-v`. - If `v` is `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`. - If `v` is `NaN`, the result is `NaN`.

floor.haxe_doc:
Returns the largest integer value that is not greater than `v`.
If `v` is outside of the signed `Int32` range, or is `NaN`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is unspecified.

round.haxe_doc:
Rounds `v` to the nearest integer value.
Ties are rounded up, so that `0.5` becomes `1` and `-0.5` becomes `0`.
If `v` is outside of the signed `Int32` range, or is `NaN`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is unspecified.

ceil.haxe_doc:
Returns the smallest integer value that is not less than `v`.
If `v` is outside of the signed `Int32` range, or is `NaN`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is unspecified.

isFinite.haxe_doc:
Tells if `f` is a finite number.
If `f` is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `NaN`, the result is `false`, otherwise the result is `true`.

isNaN.haxe_doc:
Tells if `f` is `Math.NaN`.
If `f` is `NaN`, the result is `true`, otherwise the result is `false`. In particular, `null`, `POSITIVE_INFINITY` and `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` are not considered `NaN`.

cos.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric cosine of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

sin.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric sine of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

exp.haxe_doc:
Returns Euler's number, raised to the power of `v`.
`exp(1.0)` is approximately `2.718281828459`.
- If `v` is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`. - If `v` is `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `0.0`. - If `v` is `NaN`, the result is `NaN`.

log.haxe_doc:
Returns the natural logarithm of `v`.
This is the mathematical inverse operation of exp, i.e. `log(exp(v)) == v` always holds.
- If `v` is negative (including `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`) or `NaN`, the result is `NaN`. - If `v` is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`. - If `v` is `0.0`, the result is `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`.

tan.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric tangent of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

atan.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric arc tangent of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

acos.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric arc cosine of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

asin.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric arc of the specified angle `v`, in radians.
If `v` is `NaN` or infinite, the result is `NaN`.

pow.haxe_doc: Returns a specified base `v` raised to the specified power `exp`.

atan2.haxe_doc:
Returns the trigonometric arc tangent whose tangent is the quotient of two specified numbers, in radians.
If parameter `x` or `y` is `NaN`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `NaN`.

random.haxe_doc: Returns a pseudo-random number which is greater than or equal to `0.0`, and less than `1.0`.

min.haxe_doc:
Returns the smaller of values `a` and `b`.
- If `a` or `b` are `NaN`, the result is `NaN`. - If `a` or `b` are `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`. - If `a` and `b` are `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`.

max.haxe_doc:
Returns the greater of values `a` and `b`.
- If `a` or `b` are `NaN`, the result is `NaN`. - If `a` or `b` are `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `POSITIVE_INFINITY`. - If `a` and `b` are `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, the result is `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`.

PI.haxe_doc: Represents the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, specified by the constant, π. `PI` is approximately `3.141592653589793`.

NaN.haxe_doc:
A special `Float` constant which denotes an invalid number.
`NaN` stands for "Not a Number". It occurs when a mathematically incorrect operation is executed, such as taking the square root of a negative number: `Math.sqrt(-1)`.
All further operations with `NaN` as an operand will result in `NaN`.
If this constant is converted to an `Int`, e.g. through `Std.int()`, the result is unspecified.
In order to test if a value is `NaN`, you should use `Math.isNaN()` function.

POSITIVE_INFINITY.haxe_doc:
A special `Float` constant which denotes positive infinity.
For example, this is the result of `1.0 / 0.0`.
Operations with `POSITIVE_INFINITY` as an operand may result in `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, `POSITIVE_INFINITY` or `NaN`.
If this constant is converted to an `Int`, e.g. through `Std.int()`, the result is unspecified.

NEGATIVE_INFINITY.haxe_doc:
A special `Float` constant which denotes negative infinity.
For example, this is the result of `-1.0 / 0.0`.
Operations with `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` as an operand may result in `NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, `POSITIVE_INFINITY` or `NaN`.
If this constant is converted to an `Int`, e.g. through `Std.int()`, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
This class defines mathematical functions and constants.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-math.html

hasField.haxe_doc:
Tells if structure `o` has a field named `field`.
This is only guaranteed to work for anonymous structures. Refer to `Type.getInstanceFields` for a function supporting class instances.
If `o` or `field` are null, the result is unspecified.

field.haxe_doc:
Returns the value of the field named `field` on object `o`.
If `o` is not an object or has no field named `field`, the result is null.
If the field is defined as a property, its accessors are ignored. Refer to `Reflect.getProperty` for a function supporting property accessors.
If `field` is null, the result is unspecified.

setField.haxe_doc:
Sets the field named `field` of object `o` to value `value`.
If `o` has no field named `field`, this function is only guaranteed to work for anonymous structures.
If `o` or `field` are null, the result is unspecified.

getProperty.haxe_doc:
Returns the value of the field named `field` on object `o`, taking property getter functions into account.
If the field is not a property, this function behaves like `Reflect.field`, but might be slower.
If `o` or `field` are null, the result is unspecified.

setProperty.haxe_doc:
Sets the field named `field` of object `o` to value `value`, taking property setter functions into account.
If the field is not a property, this function behaves like `Reflect.setField`, but might be slower.
If `field` is null, the result is unspecified.

callMethod.haxe_doc:
Call a method `func` with the given arguments `args`.
The object `o` is ignored in most cases. It serves as the `this`-context in the following situations:
* (neko) Allows switching the context to `o` in all cases. * (macro) Same as neko for Haxe 3. No context switching in Haxe 4. * (js, lua) Require the `o` argument if `func` does not, but should have a context. This can occur by accessing a function field natively, e.g. through `Reflect.field` or by using `(object : Dynamic).field`. However, if `func` has a context, `o` is ignored like on other targets.

fields.haxe_doc:
Returns the fields of structure `o`.
This method is only guaranteed to work on anonymous structures. Refer to `Type.getInstanceFields` for a function supporting class instances.
If `o` is null, the result is unspecified.

compare.haxe_doc:
Compares `a` and `b`.
If `a` is less than `b`, the result is negative. If `b` is less than `a`, the result is positive. If `a` and `b` are equal, the result is 0.
This function is only defined if `a` and `b` are of the same type.
If that type is a function, the result is unspecified and `Reflect.compareMethods` should be used instead.
For all other types, the result is 0 if `a` and `b` are equal. If they are not equal, the result depends on the type and is negative if:
- Numeric types: a is less than b - String: a is lexicographically less than b - Other: unspecified
If `a` and `b` are null, the result is 0. If only one of them is null, the result is unspecified.

compareMethods.haxe_doc:
Compares the functions `f1` and `f2`.
If `f1` or `f2` are null, the result is false. If `f1` or `f2` are not functions, the result is unspecified.
Otherwise the result is true if `f1` and the `f2` are physically equal, false otherwise.
If `f1` or `f2` are member method closures, the result is true if they are closures of the same method on the same object value, false otherwise.

isObject.haxe_doc:
Tells if `v` is an object.
The result is true if `v` is one of the following:
- class instance - structure - `Class<T>` - `Enum<T>`
Otherwise, including if `v` is null, the result is false.

isEnumValue.haxe_doc:
Tells if `v` is an enum value.
The result is true if `v` is of type EnumValue, i.e. an enum constructor.
Otherwise, including if `v` is null, the result is false.

deleteField.haxe_doc:
Removes the field named `field` from structure `o`.
This method is only guaranteed to work on anonymous structures.
If `o` or `field` are null, the result is unspecified.

copy.haxe_doc:
Copies the fields of structure `o`.
This is only guaranteed to work on anonymous structures.
If `o` is null, the result is `null`.

makeVarArgs.haxe_doc: Transform a function taking an array of arguments into a function that can be called with any number of arguments.

random.haxe_doc:
Return a random integer between 0 included and `x` excluded.
If `x <= 1`, the result is always 0.

isOfType.haxe_doc:
Tells if a value `v` is of the type `t`. Returns `false` if `v` or `t` are null.
If `t` is a class or interface with `@:generic` meta, the result is `false`.

downcast.haxe_doc:
Checks if object `value` is an instance of class or interface `c`.
Compiles only if the type specified by `c` can be assigned to the type of `value`.
This method checks if a downcast is possible. That is, if the runtime type of `value` is assignable to the type specified by `c`, `value` is returned. Otherwise null is returned.
This method is not guaranteed to work with core types such as `String`, `Array` and `Date`.
If `value` is null, the result is null. If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.

int.haxe_doc:
Converts a `Float` to an `Int`, rounded towards 0.
If `x` is outside of the signed Int32 range, or is `NaN`, `NEGATIVE_INFINITY` or `POSITIVE_INFINITY`, the result is unspecified.

string.haxe_doc:
Converts any value to a String.
If `s` is of `String`, `Int`, `Float` or `Bool`, its value is returned.
If `s` is an instance of a class and that class or one of its parent classes has a `toString` method, that method is called. If no such method is present, the result is unspecified.
If `s` is an enum constructor without argument, the constructor's name is returned. If arguments exists, the constructor's name followed by the String representations of the arguments is returned.
If `s` is a structure, the field names along with their values are returned. The field order and the operator separating field names and values are unspecified.
If s is null, "null" is returned.

parseInt.haxe_doc:
Converts a `String` to an `Int`.
Leading whitespaces are ignored.
`x` may optionally start with a + or - to denote a postive or negative value respectively.
If the optional sign is followed 0x or 0X, hexadecimal notation is recognized where the following digits may contain 0-9 and A-F. Both the prefix and digits are case insensitive.
Otherwise `x` is read as decimal number with 0-9 being allowed characters. Octal and binary notations are not supported.
Parsing continues until an invalid character is detected, in which case the result up to that point is returned. Scientific notation is not supported. That is `Std.parseInt('10e2')` produces `10`.
If `x` is `null`, the result is `null`. If `x` cannot be parsed as integer or is empty, the result is `null`.
If `x` starts with a hexadecimal prefix which is not followed by at least one valid hexadecimal digit, the result is unspecified.

parseFloat.haxe_doc:
Converts a `String` to a `Float`.
The parsing rules for `parseInt` apply here as well, with the exception of invalid input resulting in a `NaN` value instead of `null`. Also, hexadecimal support is **not** specified.
Additionally, decimal notation may contain a single `.` to denote the start of the fractions.
It may also end with `e` or `E` followed by optional minus or plus sign and a sequence of digits (defines exponent to base 10).

class.haxe_doc: The Std class provides standard methods for manipulating basic types.

abstract.haxe_doc:
The standard `Void` type. Only `null` values can be of the type `Void`.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/types-void.html

The standard `Float` type, this is a double-precision IEEE 64bit float.
On static targets, `null` cannot be assigned to Float. If this is necessary, `Null<Float>` can be used instead.
`Std.int` converts a `Float` to an `Int`, rounded towards 0. `Std.parseFloat` converts a `String` to a `Float`.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/types-basic-types.html @see https://haxe.org/manual/types-nullability.html
Single-precision IEEE 32bit float (4-byte).

`Null<T>` is a wrapper that can be used to make the basic types `Int`, `Float` and `Bool` nullable on static targets.
If null safety is enabled, only types wrapped in `Null<T>` are nullable.
Otherwise, it has no effect on non-basic-types, but it can be useful as a way to document that `null` is an acceptable value for a method argument, return value or variable.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/types-nullability.html

next.haxe_doc:
Returns the current item of the `Iterator` and advances to the next one.
This method is not required to check `hasNext()` first. A call to this method while `hasNext()` is `false` yields unspecified behavior.
On the other hand, iterators should not require a call to `hasNext()` before the first call to `next()` if an element is available.

hasNext.haxe_doc:
Returns `false` if the iteration is complete, `true` otherwise.
Usually iteration is considered to be complete if all elements of the underlying data structure were handled through calls to `next()`. However, in custom iterators any logic may be used to determine the completion state.

typedef.haxe_doc: A `KeyValueIterator` is an `Iterator` that has a key and a value.
A `KeyValueIterable` is a data structure which has a `keyValueIterator()` method to iterate over key-value-pairs.

fromCharCode.haxe_doc:
Returns the String corresponding to the character code `code`.
If `code` is negative or has another invalid value, the result is unspecified.

length.haxe_doc: The number of characters in `this` String.

toUpperCase.haxe_doc: Returns a String where all characters of `this` String are upper case.

toLowerCase.haxe_doc: Returns a String where all characters of `this` String are lower case.

charAt.haxe_doc:
Returns the character at position `index` of `this` String.
If `index` is negative or exceeds `this.length`, the empty String `""` is returned.

charCodeAt.haxe_doc:
Returns the character code at position `index` of `this` String.
If `index` is negative or exceeds `this.length`, `null` is returned.
To obtain the character code of a single character, `"x".code` can be used instead to inline the character code at compile time. Note that this only works on String literals of length 1.

indexOf.haxe_doc:
Returns the position of the leftmost occurrence of `str` within `this` String.
If `startIndex` is given, the search is performed within the substring of `this` String starting from `startIndex`.
If `startIndex` exceeds `this.length`, -1 is returned.
If `startIndex` is negative, the result is unspecifed.
Otherwise the search is performed within `this` String. In either case, the returned position is relative to the beginning of `this` String.
If `str` cannot be found, -1 is returned.

lastIndexOf.haxe_doc:
Returns the position of the rightmost occurrence of `str` within `this` String.
If `startIndex` is given, the search is performed within the substring of `this` String from 0 to `startIndex + str.length`. Otherwise the search is performed within `this` String. In either case, the returned position is relative to the beginning of `this` String.
If `startIndex` is negative, the result is unspecifed.
If `str` cannot be found, -1 is returned.

split.haxe_doc:
Splits `this` String at each occurrence of `delimiter`.
If `this` String is the empty String `""`, the result is not consistent across targets and may either be `[]` (on Js, Cpp) or `[""]`.
If `delimiter` is the empty String `""`, `this` String is split into an Array of `this.length` elements, where the elements correspond to the characters of `this` String.
If `delimiter` is not found within `this` String, the result is an Array with one element, which equals `this` String.
If `delimiter` is null, the result is unspecified.
Otherwise, `this` String is split into parts at each occurrence of `delimiter`. If `this` String starts (or ends) with `delimiter`, the result `Array` contains a leading (or trailing) empty String `""` element. Two subsequent delimiters also result in an empty String `""` element.

substr.haxe_doc:
Returns `len` characters of `this` String, starting at position `pos`.
If `len` is omitted, all characters from position `pos` to the end of `this` String are included.
If `pos` is negative, its value is calculated from the end of `this` String by `this.length + pos`. If this yields a negative value, 0 is used instead.
If the calculated position + `len` exceeds `this.length`, the characters from that position to the end of `this` String are returned.
If `len` is negative, the result is unspecified.

substring.haxe_doc:
Returns the part of `this` String from `startIndex` to but not including `endIndex`.
If `startIndex` or `endIndex` are negative, 0 is used instead.
If `startIndex` exceeds `endIndex`, they are swapped.
If the (possibly swapped) `endIndex` is omitted or exceeds `this.length`, `this.length` is used instead.
If the (possibly swapped) `startIndex` exceeds `this.length`, the empty String `""` is returned.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the String itself.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a copy from a given String.

class.haxe_doc:
The basic String class.
A Haxe String is immutable, it is not possible to modify individual characters. No method of this class changes the state of `this` String.
Strings can be constructed using the String literal syntax `"string value"`.
String can be concatenated by using the `+` operator. If an operand is not a String, it is passed through `Std.string()` first.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-String.html

add.haxe_doc:
Appends the representation of `x` to `this` StringBuf.
The exact representation of `x` may vary per platform. To get more consistent behavior, this function should be called with Std.string(x).
If `x` is null, the String "null" is appended.

addSub.haxe_doc:
Appends a substring of `s` to `this` StringBuf.
This function expects `pos` and `len` to describe a valid substring of `s`, or else the result is unspecified. To get more robust behavior, `this.add(s.substr(pos,len))` can be used instead.
If `s` or `pos` are null, the result is unspecified.
If `len` is omitted or null, the substring ranges from `pos` to the end of `s`.

addChar.haxe_doc:
Appends the character identified by `c` to `this` StringBuf.
If `c` is negative or has another invalid value, the result is unspecified.

toString.haxe_doc:
Returns the content of `this` StringBuf as String.
The buffer is not emptied by this operation.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new StringBuf instance.
This may involve initialization of the internal buffer.

class.haxe_doc:
A String buffer is an efficient way to build a big string by appending small elements together.
Unlike String, an instance of StringBuf is not immutable in the sense that it can be passed as argument to functions which modify it by appending more values.

winMetaCharacters.haxe_doc: Character codes of the characters that will be escaped by `quoteWinArg(_, true)`.

quoteUnixArg.haxe_doc: Returns a String that can be used as a single command line argument on Unix. The input will be quoted, or escaped if necessary.

quoteWinArg.haxe_doc:
Returns a String that can be used as a single command line argument on Windows. The input will be quoted, or escaped if necessary, such that the output will be parsed as a single argument using the rule specified in http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms880421
Examples: ```haxe quoteWinArg("abc") == "abc"; quoteWinArg("ab c") == '"ab c"'; ```

startsWith.haxe_doc:
Tells if the string `s` starts with the string `start`.
If `start` is `null`, the result is unspecified.
If `start` is the empty String `""`, the result is true.

endsWith.haxe_doc:
Tells if the string `s` ends with the string `end`.
If `end` is `null`, the result is unspecified.
If `end` is the empty String `""`, the result is true.

isSpace.haxe_doc:
Tells if the character in the string `s` at position `pos` is a space.
A character is considered to be a space character if its character code is 9,10,11,12,13 or 32.
If `s` is the empty String `""`, or if pos is not a valid position within `s`, the result is false.

ltrim.haxe_doc:
Removes leading space characters of `s`.
This function internally calls `isSpace()` to decide which characters to remove.
If `s` is the empty String `""` or consists only of space characters, the result is the empty String `""`.

rtrim.haxe_doc:
Removes trailing space characters of `s`.
This function internally calls `isSpace()` to decide which characters to remove.
If `s` is the empty String `""` or consists only of space characters, the result is the empty String `""`.

trim.haxe_doc:
Removes leading and trailing space characters of `s`.
This is a convenience function for `ltrim(rtrim(s))`.

lpad.haxe_doc:
Concatenates `c` to `s` until `s.length` is at least `l`.
If `c` is the empty String `""` or if `l` does not exceed `s.length`, `s` is returned unchanged.
If `c.length` is 1, the resulting String length is exactly `l`.
Otherwise the length may exceed `l`.
If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.

replace.haxe_doc:
Replace all occurrences of the String `sub` in the String `s` by the String `by`.
If `sub` is the empty String `""`, `by` is inserted after each character of `s` except the last one. If `by` is also the empty String `""`, `s` remains unchanged.
If `sub` or `by` are null, the result is unspecified.

hex.haxe_doc:
Encodes `n` into a hexadecimal representation.
If `digits` is specified, the resulting String is padded with "0" until its `length` equals `digits`.

class.haxe_doc:
This class provides advanced methods on Strings. It is ideally used with `using StringTools` and then acts as an [extension](https://haxe.org/manual/lf-static-extension.html) to the `String` class.
If the first argument to any of the methods is null, the result is unspecified.

offset.haxe_doc: Please note that you need to retain the original unoffset'ed Bytes so it does not get garbage collected, unless the pointer was not GC allocated.

getArray.haxe_doc: Get the bytes reference from an array of basic types (no copy occurs)

exists.haxe_doc: Returns `true` if the file or directory specified by `path` exists.

rename.haxe_doc:
Renames/moves the file or directory specified by `path` to `newPath`.
If `path` is not a valid file system entry, or if it is not accessible, or if `newPath` is not accessible, an exception is thrown.

stat.haxe_doc: Returns `FileStat` information for the file or directory specified by `path`.

fullPath.haxe_doc: Returns the full path of the file or directory specified by `relPath`, which is relative to the current working directory. Symlinks will be followed and the path will be normalized.

absolutePath.haxe_doc: Returns the full path of the file or directory specified by `relPath`, which is relative to the current working directory. The path doesn't have to exist.

isDirectory.haxe_doc:
Returns `true` if the file or directory specified by `path` is a directory.
If `path` is not a valid file system entry or if its destination is not accessible, an exception is thrown.

createDirectory.haxe_doc:
Creates a directory specified by `path`.
This method is recursive: The parent directories don't have to exist.
If the directory cannot be created, an exception is thrown.

deleteFile.haxe_doc:
Deletes the file specified by `path`.
If `path` does not denote a valid file, or if that file cannot be deleted, an exception is thrown.

deleteDirectory.haxe_doc:
Deletes the directory specified by `path`. Only empty directories can be deleted.
If `path` does not denote a valid directory, or if that directory cannot be deleted, an exception is thrown.

readDirectory.haxe_doc:
Returns the names of all files and directories in the directory specified by `path`. `"."` and `".."` are not included in the output.
If `path` does not denote a valid directory, an exception is thrown.

class.haxe_doc:
This class provides information about files and directories.
If `null` is passed as a file path to any function in this class, the result is unspecified, and may differ from target to target.
See `sys.io.File` for the complementary file API.

println.haxe_doc: Prints any value to the standard output, followed by a newline. On Windows, this function outputs a CRLF newline. LF newlines are printed on all other platforms.

args.haxe_doc:
Returns all the arguments that were passed in the command line. This does not include the interpreter or the name of the program file.
(java)(eval) On Windows, non-ASCII Unicode arguments will not work correctly.
(cs) Non-ASCII Unicode arguments will not work correctly.

stderr.haxe_doc: Returns the standard error of the process, to which program errors can be written.

getEnv.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the given environment variable, or `null` if it doesn't exist.

sleep.haxe_doc: Suspends execution for the given length of time (in seconds).

getCwd.haxe_doc: Gets the current working directory (usually the one in which the program was started).

systemName.haxe_doc: Returns the type of the current system. Possible values are: - `"Windows"` - `"Linux"` - `"BSD"` - `"Mac"`

command.haxe_doc:
Runs the given command. The command output will be printed to the same output as the current process. The current process will block until the command terminates. The return value is the exit code of the command (usually `0` indicates no error).
Command arguments can be passed in two ways:
1. Using `args` to pass command arguments. Each argument will be automatically quoted and shell meta-characters will be escaped if needed. `cmd` should be an executable name that can be located in the `PATH` environment variable, or a full path to an executable.
2. When `args` is not given or is `null`, command arguments can be appended to `cmd`. No automatic quoting/escaping will be performed. `cmd` should be formatted exactly as it would be when typed at the command line. It can run executables, as well as shell commands that are not executables (e.g. on Windows: `dir`, `cd`, `echo` etc).
Use the `sys.io.Process` API for more complex tasks, such as background processes, or providing input to the command.

programPath.haxe_doc: Returns the absolute path to the current program file that we are running. Concretely, for an executable binary, it returns the path to the binary. For a script (e.g. a PHP file), it returns the path to the script.

time.haxe_doc: Gives the most precise timestamp value available (in seconds).

exit.haxe_doc:
Exits the current process with the given exit code.
(macro)(eval) Being invoked in a macro or eval context (e.g. with `-x` or `--run`) immediately terminates the compilation process, which also prevents the execution of any `--next` sections of compilation arguments.

class.haxe_doc: This class provides access to various base functions of system platforms. Look in the `sys` package for more system APIs.

getClass.haxe_doc:
Returns the class of `o`, if `o` is a class instance.
If `o` is null or of a different type, null is returned.
In general, type parameter information cannot be obtained at runtime.

getEnum.haxe_doc:
Returns the enum of enum instance `o`.
An enum instance is the result of using an enum constructor. Given an `enum Color { Red; }`, `getEnum(Red)` returns `Enum<Color>`.
If `o` is null, null is returned.
In general, type parameter information cannot be obtained at runtime.

getSuperClass.haxe_doc:
Returns the super-class of class `c`.
If `c` has no super class, null is returned.
If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.
In general, type parameter information cannot be obtained at runtime.

getClassName.haxe_doc:
Returns the name of class `c`, including its path.
If `c` is inside a package, the package structure is returned dot- separated, with another dot separating the class name: `pack1.pack2.(...).packN.ClassName` If `c` is a sub-type of a Haxe module, that module is not part of the package structure.
If `c` has no package, the class name is returned.
If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.
The class name does not include any type parameters.

getEnumName.haxe_doc:
Returns the name of enum `e`, including its path.
If `e` is inside a package, the package structure is returned dot- separated, with another dot separating the enum name: `pack1.pack2.(...).packN.EnumName` If `e` is a sub-type of a Haxe module, that module is not part of the package structure.
If `e` has no package, the enum name is returned.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.
The enum name does not include any type parameters.

resolveClass.haxe_doc:
Resolves a class by name.
If `name` is the path of an existing class, that class is returned.
Otherwise null is returned.
If `name` is null or the path to a different type, the result is unspecified.
The class name must not include any type parameters.

resolveEnum.haxe_doc:
Resolves an enum by name.
If `name` is the path of an existing enum, that enum is returned.
Otherwise null is returned.
If `name` is null the result is unspecified.
If `name` is the path to a different type, null is returned.
The enum name must not include any type parameters.

createInstance.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of class `cl`, using `args` as arguments to the class constructor.
This function guarantees that the class constructor is called.
Default values of constructors arguments are not guaranteed to be taken into account.
If `cl` or `args` are null, or if the number of elements in `args` does not match the expected number of constructor arguments, or if any argument has an invalid type, or if `cl` has no own constructor, the result is unspecified.
In particular, default values of constructor arguments are not guaranteed to be taken into account.

createEmptyInstance.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of class `cl`.
This function guarantees that the class constructor is not called.
If `cl` is null, the result is unspecified.

createEnum.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of enum `e` by calling its constructor `constr` with arguments `params`.
If `e` or `constr` is null, or if enum `e` has no constructor named `constr`, or if the number of elements in `params` does not match the expected number of constructor arguments, or if any argument has an invalid type, the result is unspecified.

createEnumIndex.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of enum `e` by calling its constructor number `index` with arguments `params`.
The constructor indices are preserved from Haxe syntax, so the first declared is index 0, the next index 1 etc.
If `e` or `constr` is null, or if enum `e` has no constructor named `constr`, or if the number of elements in `params` does not match the expected number of constructor arguments, or if any argument has an invalid type, the result is unspecified.

getInstanceFields.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of the instance fields of class `c`, including inherited fields.
This only includes fields which are known at compile-time. In particular, using `getInstanceFields(getClass(obj))` will not include any fields which were added to `obj` at runtime.
The order of the fields in the returned Array is unspecified.
If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.

getClassFields.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of static fields of class `c`.
This does not include static fields of parent classes.
The order of the fields in the returned Array is unspecified.
If `c` is null, the result is unspecified.

getEnumConstructs.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of the names of all constructors of enum `e`.
The order of the constructor names in the returned Array is preserved from the original syntax.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.

typeof.haxe_doc:
Returns the runtime type of value `v`.
The result corresponds to the type `v` has at runtime, which may vary per platform. Assumptions regarding this should be minimized to avoid surprises.

enumEq.haxe_doc:
Recursively compares two enum instances `a` and `b` by value.
Unlike `a == b`, this function performs a deep equality check on the arguments of the constructors, if exists.
If `a` or `b` are null, the result is unspecified.

enumConstructor.haxe_doc:
Returns the constructor name of enum instance `e`.
The result String does not contain any constructor arguments.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.

enumParameters.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of the constructor arguments of enum instance `e`.
If `e` has no arguments, the result is [].
Otherwise the result are the values that were used as arguments to `e`, in the order of their declaration.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.

enumIndex.haxe_doc:
Returns the index of enum instance `e`.
This corresponds to the original syntactic position of `e`. The index of the first declared constructor is 0, the next one is 1 etc.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.

allEnums.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of all constructors of enum `e` that require no arguments.
This may return the empty Array `[]` if all constructors of `e` require arguments.
Otherwise an instance of `e` constructed through each of its non- argument constructors is returned, in the order of the constructor declaration.
If `e` is null, the result is unspecified.

abstract.haxe_doc:
Xml node types.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-Xml.html

parse.haxe_doc: Parses the String into an Xml document.

createElement.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createPCData.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createCData.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createComment.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createDocType.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createProcessingInstruction.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

createDocument.haxe_doc: Creates a node of the given type.

nodeType.haxe_doc: Returns the type of the Xml Node. This should be used before accessing other functions since some might raise an exception if the node type is not correct.

nodeName.haxe_doc: Returns the node name of an Element.

nodeValue.haxe_doc: Returns the node value. Only works if the Xml node is not an Element or a Document.

parent.haxe_doc: Returns the parent object in the Xml hierarchy. The parent can be `null`, an Element or a Document.

get.haxe_doc: Get the given attribute of an Element node. Returns `null` if not found. Attributes are case-sensitive.

set.haxe_doc: Set the given attribute value for an Element node. Attributes are case-sensitive.

exists.haxe_doc: Tells if the Element node has a given attribute. Attributes are case-sensitive.

attributes.haxe_doc: Returns an `Iterator` on all the attribute names.

iterator.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of all child nodes. Only works if the current node is an Element or a Document.

elements.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of all child nodes which are Elements. Only works if the current node is an Element or a Document.

elementsNamed.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of all child nodes which are Elements with the given nodeName. Only works if the current node is an Element or a Document.

firstElement.haxe_doc: Returns the first child node which is an Element.

addChild.haxe_doc: Adds a child node to the Document or Element. A child node can only be inside one given parent node, which is indicated by the `parent` property. If the child is already inside this Document or Element, it will be moved to the last position among the Document or Element's children. If the child node was previously inside a different node, it will be moved to this Document or Element.

removeChild.haxe_doc: Removes a child from the Document or Element. Returns true if the child was successfuly removed.

insertChild.haxe_doc: Inserts a child at the given position among the other childs. A child node can only be inside one given parent node, which is indicated by the [parent] property. If the child is already inside this Document or Element, it will be moved to the new position among the Document or Element's children. If the child node was previously inside a different node, it will be moved to this Document or Element.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a String representation of the Xml node.

class.haxe_doc:
Cross-platform Xml API.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-Xml.html

_new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Map.
This becomes a constructor call to one of the specialization types in the output. The rules for that are as follows:
1. if `K` is a `String`, `haxe.ds.StringMap` is used 2. if `K` is an `Int`, `haxe.ds.IntMap` is used 3. if `K` is an `EnumValue`, `haxe.ds.EnumValueMap` is used 4. if `K` is any other class or structure, `haxe.ds.ObjectMap` is used 5. if `K` is any other type, it causes a compile-time error
(Cpp) Map does not use weak keys on `ObjectMap` by default.

PRIORITIES.expr: [[OOr], [OAnd], [OEq, ONotEq, OLt, OLte, OGt, OGte], [OAdd, OSub], [OMul, ODiv, OMod]]

m.e: [[OOr], [OAnd], [OEq, ONotEq, OLt, OLte, OGt, OGte], [OAdd, OSub], [OMul, ODiv, OMod]]

version.haxe_doc: * Gif version. There is only 2 Gif version exists. 87a and 89a. * 87a have less features and does not support any extensions. * Unknown version is adviced to be interpreted as newest (89a) official version.

logicalScreenDescriptor.haxe_doc: * Information about logical screen of Gif that provides basic information about Gif.

globalColorTable.haxe_doc: * Global color table used for Gif. Present only if Logical Screen Descriptor contained global color table flag. * Note that this color table not always present since frames can contain local color tables that overrides global color table.

typedef.haxe_doc: * Gif data.

BFrame.haxe_doc: * Gif frame block. * Note that this block does not contain link to graphic control extension of Frame even if it is present. GraphicControl extension Block commonly present right before frame Block.

BExtension.haxe_doc: * Additional extension block. This Block does not supported in 87a Gif specification version.

BEOF.haxe_doc: * End of File block. Represents end of Gif data.

enum.haxe_doc: * Gif data block. Custom blocks are not supported.

EGraphicControl.haxe_doc: * Graphic Control extension gives additional control over next frame, like frame delay, disposal method, alpha channel and other information.

EComment.haxe_doc: * Commentary extension. Not show up as any visual, just a text in file.

EText.haxe_doc: * Text extension. Must work as text rendering on the image, but ignored by all major Gif decoders.

EApplicationExtension.haxe_doc: * Application extension allow to insert additional application data into Gif. Mostly used app extension is NETSCAPE2.0 looping extension, used to set up amount of loops in frame.

enum.haxe_doc: * Extension block contains additional data about Gif image. This block does not supported by 87a version.

AENetscapeLooping.haxe_doc: * NETSCAPE2.0 looping extension. Contains only amount of animation repeats. * Note that there is two NETSCAPE2.0 app extensions for Gif format and the type of extension is stored in first byte of data. Looping extension have ID 1.

enum.haxe_doc: * Application extension. Mostly used only for one reason - setting up loops count. There is exist other app extensions but they are really rare.

typedef.haxe_doc: * Typical color table for Gif image. * Can contain 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 or 256 colors. * Data stored in RGB format. Information about alpha channel provided by Graohic Control Extension.

y.haxe_doc: * Y position of image on the Logical Screen

x.haxe_doc: * X position of image on the Logical Screen

width.haxe_doc: * Width of image in pixels

sorted.haxe_doc: * Is local color table sorted in order of decreasing priority?

pixels.haxe_doc: * Pixel data of frame. Stored as Indexed colors, 1 byte per pixel.

localColorTable.haxe_doc: * Is this image uses local color table?

interlaced.haxe_doc: * Is this image written in interlace mode? * Note: The pixel data already deinterlaced and this flag presented only for information purpose (and for Writer when there is one).

height.haxe_doc: * Height of image in pixels

colorTable.haxe_doc: * Local color table used by frame. Stored as 3-byte RGB colors. If value is null, must be used global color table.

typedef.haxe_doc: * Single frame of the image. * Actually it's a merge of 3 consequent blocks: * 1. Image Descriptor. * Contains frame informations like position, size, existing of local color table and interlaced flag. * 2. [Local color table]. * Only present if Image Descriptor contains local color table flag. Overrides global color table. * 3. Pixel data blocks. * LZW compressed pixel data.

userInput.haxe_doc: * Is image must wait for user input, before dispose? * This flag may be used by user-defined program but absolutely ignored by any Gif players.

transparentIndex.haxe_doc: * Index in color table that used as transparent.

delay.haxe_doc: * Delay, before next image appears. Delay is in centiseconds (1 centisecond = 1/100 seconds). * Note: Some players (like FastStone) cut fraction of elapsed time when progressing to next frame which results in small timing error. * Recommended to use `time -= delay` instead of `time = 0`.

typedef.haxe_doc: * Graphic Control Extension block, used for setting up disposal method, transparency, delay and user input.

textGridY.haxe_doc: * Y position of text grid on Logical Screen.

textGridX.haxe_doc: * X position of text grid on Logical Screen.

textGridWidth.haxe_doc: * Width of text grid in pixels.

textGridHeight.haxe_doc: * Height of text grid in pixels.

charCellWidth.haxe_doc: * Width of character cell in text grid.

charCellHeight.haxe_doc: * Height of character cell in text grid.

typedef.haxe_doc: * Extension for rendering text on Gif logical screen. It does not supported by major Gif decoders. * Font and text size decision is left to decoder. (recommended to decide based on grid/cell size) * Text must be rendered with one character at cell. * It's recommended to replace any characters less than 0x20 and greater than 0xf7 to be rendered as Space (0x20)

width.haxe_doc: * Width of GIF image in pixels

sorted.haxe_doc: * Specification: * Indicates whether the Global Color Table is sorted. If the flag is set, the Global Color Table is sorted, in order of decreasing importance. Typically, the order would be decreasing frequency, with most frequent color first. This assists a decoder, with fewer available colors, in choosing the best subset of colors; the decoder may use an initial segment of the table to render the graphic.

pixelAspectRatio.haxe_doc: * Factor used to compute an approximation of the aspect ratio of the pixel in the original image.

height.haxe_doc: * Height of GIF image in pixels

hasGlobalColorTable.haxe_doc: * Is this file uses global color table?

colorResolution.haxe_doc: * Specification: * Number of bits per primary color available to the original image, minus 1. This value represents the size of the entire palette from which the colors in the graphic were selected, not the number of colors actually used in the graphic. For example, if the value in this field is 3, then the palette of the original image had 4 bits per primary color available to create the image. This value should be set to indicate the richness of the original palette, even if not every color from the whole palette is available on the source machine.

backgroundColorIndex.haxe_doc: * Background color index in global color table

typedef.haxe_doc: * Logical screen descriptor of GIF file. * Contains very basic information about Gif.

GIF87a.haxe_doc: * First version of Gif file format from May 1987. * * Note: The checking of unsupported blocks disabled by default to save some time. To enable supported blocks check set `yagp_strict_version_check` debug variable.

GIF89a.haxe_doc: * Second and actual version of Gif file format from July 1989.

enum.haxe_doc: * Version of Gif file. * The only 2 official versions is GIF87a and GIF89a.

UNSPECIFIED.haxe_doc: * The disposal method is unspecified. Action on demand of viewer. * * Mostly interpreted as NO_ACTION.

FILL_BACKGROUND.haxe_doc: * Fill frame rectangle with background color. * * Usage note: * Most renderers clears to transparency instead of filling background color, when frame's transparent color index not equals to background color index.

RENDER_PREVIOUS.haxe_doc: * Render previous state of gif as it before rendering disposing frame.

enum.haxe_doc: * Disposal method of GIF frame.

class.haxe_doc: * ... * @author Yanrishatum

framesCount.haxe_doc: * Returns amount of frames in Gif data.

frame.haxe_doc: * Returns frame at given index. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Index of frame. * @return Frame at given index or null, if there is no frame at that index.

graphicControl.haxe_doc: * Returns Graphic Control extension for frame at given index. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Index of frame. * @return GCE extension if it is exists for given frame, null otherwise.

extractBGRA.haxe_doc: * Extracts frame pixel data in Blue-Green-Red-Alpha pixel format. * This function extracts only exact frame and does put previous frame pixel data into resulting Bytes. Note that frame size may not equal to Gif logical screen size. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Frame index. * @return BGRA pixel data with dimensions equals to specified Frame size. If frame does not present in Gif data returns null.

extractRGBA.haxe_doc: * Extracts frame pixel data in Red-Green-Blue-Alpha pixel format. * This function extracts only exact frame and does put previous frame pixel data into resulting Bytes. Note that frame size may not equal to Gif logical screen size. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Frame index. * @return RGBA pixel data with dimensions equals to specified Frame size. If frame does not present in Gif data returns null.

extractFullBGRA.haxe_doc: * Extracts full Gif pixel data to specified frame in Blue-Green-Red-Alpha pixel format. * This functions returns full representation of frame including rendering of all other frames before. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Frame index. * @return BGRA pixel data with dimensions equals to Gif logical screen with full pixel data of Gif image at specified frame.

extractFullRGBA.haxe_doc: * Extracts full Gif pixel data to specified frame in Red-Green-Blue-Alpha pixel format. * This functions returns full representation of frame including rendering of all other frames before. * @param data Gif data. * @param frameIndex Frame index. * @return RGBA pixel data with dimensions equals to Gif logical screen with full pixel data of Gif image at specified frame.

loopCount.haxe_doc: * Returns amount of animation repeats stored in Gif data. * This is link to Netscape Looping application extension. If this extension does not present amount of loops equals to 1. * @param data Gif data. * @return Amount of animation repeats. Zero equals to infinite amount of repeats.

class.haxe_doc: * Tools for gif data. * @author Yanrishatum

decodeJPG.haxe_doc: Decode JPG data into the target buffer.

decodePNG.haxe_doc: Decode PNG data into the target buffer.

decodeDXT.haxe_doc: Decode any image data into ARGB pixels

scaleImage.haxe_doc: Upscale/downscale an image. Currently supported flag bits: 1 = bilinear filtering

class.haxe_doc: * MPEG Version * * sored on 2 bits in the file, * values represent bit values
* Layer * * stored on 2 bits in the file, * values represent bit values
* Sound channel mode * * stored on 2 bits in the file, * values represent bit values
* Emphasis * * 2 bits

enum.haxe_doc: * Used by seekFrame to retrun the type * of frame (possibly) found.

skipID3v2.haxe_doc: * Called after found 'ID3' signature * at the beginning of the file. * * Records the raw tag data.

seekFrame.haxe_doc: * Winds the input stream until the 11-bit * syncword is found. * * @returns Bool false if not found (this should happen at eof).

readFrames.haxe_doc: * Returns all valid frames. Invalid frames * are discarded.

readFrameHeader.haxe_doc: * Returns null if header proves to be invalid.

readFrame.haxe_doc: * Reads a frame from the input. * * The input position should already be just past the * 11 bit syncword. * * Returns null if the header is invalid or the frame was incomplete.

read.haxe_doc: * Reads the MP3 data. * * Currently returns all valid frames.

isInvalidFrameHeader.haxe_doc: * Tells whether the header is invalid.

getSampleDataSize.haxe_doc: * Return sample data size. Note that * the 4 bytes subtracted is the size of the header, * so this 4 bytes less the frame size. * * Also, 2 bytes are subtracted for CRC too, if present

getSampleCount.haxe_doc: * Returns the number of samples in the frame.

getFrameInfo.haxe_doc: * Displays frame info in human-readable format. * Subject to change, do not use for programmatical parsing!

getHeader.haxe_doc: Returns the PNG header informations. Throws an exception if no header found.

getPalette.haxe_doc: Return the PNG palette colors, or null if no palette chunk was found

reverseBytes.haxe_doc: Converts from BGRA to ARGB and the other way by reversing bytes.

extractGrey.haxe_doc: Decode the greyscale PNG data and apply filters, extracting only the grey channel if alpha is present.

extract32.haxe_doc: Decode the PNG data and apply filters. By default this will output BGRA low-endian format. You can use the [reverseBytes] function to inverse the bytes to ARGB big-endian format.

buildGrey.haxe_doc: Creates PNG data from bytes that contains one bytes (grey values) for each pixel.

buildIndexed.haxe_doc: Creates PNG data from bytes that contains a one byte palette index for each pixel and a separate palette with 3 RGB bytes per color.

buildRGB.haxe_doc: Creates PNG data from bytes that contains three bytes (R,G and B values) for each pixel.

build32ARGB.haxe_doc: Creates PNG data from bytes that contains four bytes in ARGB format for each pixel.

build32BGRA.haxe_doc: Creates PNG data from bytes that contains four bytes in BGRA format for each pixel.

yOrigin.haxe_doc: * These bytes specify the absolute vertical coordinate for the lower left * corner of the image as it is positioned on a display device having an * origin at the lower left of the screen (e.g., the TARGA series).

xOrigin.haxe_doc: * These bytes specify the absolute horizontal coordinate for the lower left * corner of the image as it is positioned on a display device having an * origin at the lower left of the screen (e.g., the TARGA series).

width.haxe_doc: This field specifies the width of the image in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: This field specifies the height of the image in pixels.

colorMapType.haxe_doc: * Indicated type of color map. * 0 = no color map present. * 1 = color map included. * 2-127 is reserved by Truevision * 128-255 may be used by app developers.

colorMapLength.haxe_doc: Total number of color map entries included.

colorMapFirstIndex.haxe_doc: * Index of the first color map entry. Index refers to the starting entry in * loading the color map.

colorMapEntrySize.haxe_doc: * Establishes the number of bits per entry. Typically 15, 16, 24 or 32-bit * values are used.

bitsPerPixel.haxe_doc: * This field indicates the number of bits per pixel. This number includes * the Attribute or Alpha channel bits. Common values are 8, 16, 24 and * 32 but other pixel depths could be used.

alphaChannelBits.haxe_doc: * the number of attribute bits per * pixel. In the case of the TrueVista, these bits * indicate the number of bits per pixel which are * designated as Alpha Channel bits. For the ICB * and TARGA products, these bits indicate the * number of overlay bits available per pixel.

NoImage.haxe_doc: There is no image data present

RunLengthColorMapped.haxe_doc: Run-length encoded image with color-map usage

class.haxe_doc: * ... * @author Yanrishatum

x.haxe_doc: The horizontal position of the point.

y.haxe_doc: The vertical position of the point.

distanceSq.haxe_doc: Returns squared distance between this Point and given Point `p`.

distance.haxe_doc: Returns a distance between this Point and given Point `p`.

sub.haxe_doc: Substracts Point `p` from this Point and returns new Point with the result.

add.haxe_doc: Adds Point `p` to this Point and returns new Point with the result.

scaled.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with the position of this Point multiplied by a given scalar `v`.

equals.haxe_doc: Tests if this Point position equals to `other` Point position.

dot.haxe_doc: Returns a dot product between this Point and given Point `p`.

lengthSq.haxe_doc: Returns squared length of this Point.

length.haxe_doc: Returns length (distance to `0,0`) of this Point.

normalized.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with the normalized values of this Point.

set.haxe_doc: Sets the Point `x,y` with given values.

load.haxe_doc: Copies `x,y` from given Point `p` to this Point.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of this Point.

cross.haxe_doc: Returns a cross product between this Point and a given Point `p`.

lerp.haxe_doc: Sets this Point position to a result of linear interpolation between Points `p1` and `p2` at the interpolant position `k`.

transform.haxe_doc: Applies a given Matrix `m` transformation to this Point position.

transformed.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with a result of applying a Matrix `m` to this Point position.

transform2x2.haxe_doc: Applies a given 2x2 Matrix `m` transformation to this Point position.

transformed2x2.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with a result of applying a 2x2 Matrix `m` to this Point position.

toIPoint.haxe_doc: Converts this point to integer point scaled by provided scalar `scale` (rounded).

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotates this Point around `0,0` by a given `angle`.

getRotation.haxe_doc: Get the angle in radians between the vector (1, 0) and this Point. The angle returned is [-π, π]

class.haxe_doc: A simple 2D position/vector container. @see `h2d.col.IPoint`

parentContainer.haxe_doc: The parent container of this object. See `Object.contentChanged` for more details.

parent.haxe_doc: The parent object in the scene tree.

numChildren.haxe_doc: How many immediate children this object has.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the object. Can be used to retrieve an object within a tree by using `Object.getObjectByName`.

x.haxe_doc: The x position (in pixels) of the object relative to its parent.

y.haxe_doc: The y position (in pixels) of the object relative to its parent.

scaleX.haxe_doc: The amount of horizontal scaling of this object.

scaleY.haxe_doc: The amount of vertical scaling of this object.

rotation.haxe_doc: The rotation angle of this object, in radians.

visible.haxe_doc: Is the object and its children are displayed on screen.

alpha.haxe_doc: The amount of transparency of the Object.

filter.haxe_doc:
The post process filter for this object.
When set, `Object.alpha` value affects both filter and object transparency (use `Drawable.color.a` to set transparency only for the object).

blendMode.haxe_doc:
The blending mode of the object.
If there is no `Object.filter` active, only applies to the current object (not inherited by children). Otherwise tells how the filter is blended with background.

posChanged.haxe_doc:
A flag that indicates that the object transform was modified and absolute position recalculation is required.
Automatically cleared on `Object.sync` and can be manually synced with the `Object.syncPos`.

allocated.haxe_doc:
A flag that indicates whether the object was allocated or not.
When adding children to allocated objects, `onAdd` is being called immediately, otherwise it's delayed until the whole tree is added to a currently active `Scene`.

getSize.haxe_doc: Similar to `getBounds(parent)`, but instead of the full content, it will return the size based on the alignment of the object. For instance for a text, `Object.getBounds` will return the full glyphs size whereas `getSize` will ignore the pixels under the baseline. @param out An optional bounds instance to fill. Allocates new Bounds instance and returns it if not set.

getAbsPos.haxe_doc: Returns the updated absolute position matrix. See `Object.getMatrix` for current matrix values.

contains.haxe_doc: Tells if the object is contained into this object children, recursively.

find.haxe_doc: Find a single object in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning the first not-null value returned, or null if not found.

findAll.haxe_doc: Find several objects in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning all the not-null values returned. @param arr An optional array instance to fill results with. Allocates a new array if not set.

getObjectsCount.haxe_doc: Return the total number of children in the whole tree, recursively.

localToGlobal.haxe_doc: Convert a local position (or `[0,0]` if `pt` is null) relative to the object origin into an absolute screen position, applying all the inherited transforms. @param pt An optional position to convert and return. Allocates new Point at 0,0 position if not set. Modifies the Point instance as is.

globalToLocal.haxe_doc: Convert an absolute screen position into a local position relative to the object origin, applying all the inherited transforms. @param pt A position to convert and return. Modifies the Point instance as is.

getScene.haxe_doc: Returns an `h2d.Scene` down the hierarchy tree or `null` if object is not added to Scene.

addChild.haxe_doc: Add a child object at the end of the children list.

addChildAt.haxe_doc: Insert a child object at the specified position of the children list.

onContentChanged.haxe_doc: Should be called when Object content was changed in order to notify parent container. See `Object.contentChanged`.

onAdd.haxe_doc:
Sent when object is being added to an allocated scene.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

onRemove.haxe_doc:
Sent when object is removed from the allocated scene.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

getMatrix.haxe_doc: Populates `m` with current absolute object transform values. See `Object.getAbsPos` for up-to-date values.

removeChild.haxe_doc: Remove the given object from the immediate children list of the object if it's part of it.

setParentContainer.haxe_doc: Sets the parent container for this Object and it's children. See `Object.contentChanged` for more details.

removeChildren.haxe_doc: Remove all children from the immediate children list.

remove.haxe_doc: Same as `parent.removeChild(this)`, but does nothing if parent is null.

drawTo.haxe_doc: Draw the object and all its children into the given Texture.

drawToTextures.haxe_doc: Draw the object and all its children into the given Textures.

draw.haxe_doc: Override this method in order to add custom graphics rendering to your Object. `draw` is invoked before rendering of the object children.

sync.haxe_doc:
Performs a sync of data for rendering (such as absolute position recalculation). While this method can be used as a substitute to an update loop, it's primary purpose it to prepare the Object to be rendered.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

syncPos.haxe_doc: Ensures that object has an up-to-date position transform.

calcAbsPos.haxe_doc: Internal usage Calculates the absolute object position transform. See `Object.syncPos` for a safe position sync method. This method does not ensure that object parents also have up-to-date transform nor does it clear the `Object.posChanged` flag.

emitTile.haxe_doc: Draws single Tile instance with this Object transform.

clipBounds.haxe_doc: Internal usage Clip the local bounds with our global viewport. Used during filter rendering in order to clip out areas that are off-screen and should not be rendered. `h2d.Scene` note: `clipBounds` will always output bounds equivalent to entire window. This is done in order for scene to never clip out cameras as they may render virtually any area of the Scene.

move.haxe_doc: Move the object by the specified amount along its current direction (`Object.rotation` angle).

setPosition.haxe_doc: Set the position of the object relative to its parent.

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotate the object by the given angle (in radians)

scale.haxe_doc: Scale uniformly the object by the given factor.

setScale.haxe_doc: Set the uniform scale for the object.

getChildAt.haxe_doc: Return the `n`th element among the immediate children list of this object, or `null` if there is no Object at this position.

getChildIndex.haxe_doc: Return the index of the object `o` within the immediate children list of this object, or `-1` if it is not part of the children list.

getObjectByName.haxe_doc: Search for an object recursively by name, return `null` if not found.

iterator.haxe_doc: Return an iterator over this object immediate children

contentChanged.haxe_doc: Advanced usage Called by the children of a container object if they have `parentContainer` defined in them. Primary use-case is when the child size got changed, requiring content to reevaluate positioning such as `Flow` layouts, but also can be used for other purposes.

constraintSize.haxe_doc: Advanced usage This can be called by a parent container to constraint the size of its children. Negative value mean that constraint is to be disabled. For example, `Text` constraints it's maximum width, causing word-wrap to occur within constrained area. @see `FlowProperties.constraint`

new.haxe_doc: Create a new empty object. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Object adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A base 2D class that all scene tree elements inherit from.
Serves as a virtual container that does not display anything but can contain other objects so the various transforms are inherited to its children.
Private events `Object.onAdd`, `Object.onRemove` and `Object.onHierarchyMoved` can be used to capture when Object is added/removed from the currently active scene as well as being moved withing the object tree.
Object exposes a number of properties to control position, scale and rotation of the Object relative to its parent, but they are used indirectly during rendering. Instead, they are being used to calculate the absolute matrix transform relative to the Scene. As optimization, it's not recalculated as soon as properties are modified and delayed until `Object.sync`. Absolute object position can be accessed through private variables `Object.matA`, `Object.matB`, `Object.matC`, `Object.matD`, `Object.absX` and `Object.absY`.
