But it should be noted that in order to ensure up-to-date values, it's advised to call `Object.syncPos` before accessing them.

color.haxe_doc: The color multiplier for the drawable. Can be used to adjust individually each of the four channels R,G,B,A (default [1,1,1,1])

smooth.haxe_doc:
By enabling smoothing, scaling the object up or down will use hardware bilinear filtering resulting in a less crisp aspect.
By default smooth is `null` in which case `Scene.defaultSmooth` value is used.

tileWrap.haxe_doc:
Enables texture uv wrap for this Drawable, causing tiles with uv exceeding the texture size to repeat instead of clamping on edges.
Note that `tileWrap` does not use the `Tile` region as a wrapping area but instead uses underlying `h3d.mat.Texture` size. This is due to implementation specifics, as it just sets the `Texture.wrap` to either `Repeat` or `Clamp`. Because of that, proper Tile tiling can be expected only when the tile covers an entire Texture area.

colorKey.haxe_doc: Setting a colorKey color value will discard all pixels that have this exact color in the tile.

colorMatrix.haxe_doc: Setting a colorMatrix will apply a color transformation. See also `adjustColor`.

colorAdd.haxe_doc: Setting colorAdd will add the amount of color of each channel R,G,B,A to the object pixels.

adjustColor.haxe_doc: Set the `Drawable.colorMatrix` value by specifying which effects to apply. Calling `adjustColor()` without arguments will reset the colorMatrix to `null`.

getShader.haxe_doc: Returns the first shader of the given shader class among the drawable shaders. @param stype The class of the shader to look up.

getShaders.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of all drawable shaders

addShader.haxe_doc:
Add a shader to the drawable shaders.
Keep in mind, that as stated before, drawable children do not inherit Drawable properties, which includes shaders.

removeShader.haxe_doc: Remove a shader from the drawable shaders, returns true if found or false if it was not part of our shaders.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Drawable instance with given parent. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Drawable adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A base class for all 2D objects that will draw something on the screen.
Unlike Object base class, all properties of Drawable only apply to the current object and are not inherited by its children.

frames.haxe_doc: The current animation, as a list of tile frames to display. If the frames are empty or if a tile is frames is null, a pink 5x5 bitmap will be displayed instead.

currentFrame.haxe_doc:
The current frame the animation is currently playing. Always in `[0,frames.length]` range. Use `Std.int(anim.currentFrame)` in order to obtain current frame index. Fractional value represents the progress of current frame and increases according to `Anim.speed` value.
Setting frame to a negative value will wrap it around from the end of the animation. Setting negative value smaller than `-frames.length` lead to undefined behavior. Setting frame to a value greater than `frames.length` would cause to wrap around.

speed.haxe_doc:
The speed (in frames per second) at which the animation is playing.
Settings speed to a negative value is not supported and leads to undefined behavior.

pause.haxe_doc: Setting pause will suspend the animation, preventing automatic accumulation of `Anim.currentFrame` over time.

loop.haxe_doc: Disabling loop will stop the animation at the last frame.

fading.haxe_doc: When enabled, fading will draw two consecutive frames with alpha transition between them instead of directly switching from one to another when it reaches the next frame. This can be used to have smoother animation on some effects.

onAnimEnd.haxe_doc:
Sent each time the animation reaches past the last frame.
If `loop` is enabled, callback is sent every time the animation loops. During the call, `currentFrame` is already wrapped around and represent new frame position so it's safe to modify it.
If `loop` is disabled, callback is sent only once when the animation reaches `currentFrame == frames.length`. During the call, `currentFrame` is always equals to `frames.length`.

getFrame.haxe_doc: Returns the Tile at current frame.

class.haxe_doc:
Displays an animated sequence of bitmap Tiles on the screen.
Anim does not provide animation sequence management and it's up to user on how to implement it. Another limitation is framerate. Anim runs at a fixed framerate dictated by `Anim.speed`. Switching animations can be done through `Anim.play` method.
Note that animation playback happens regardless of Anim visibility and only can be paused by `Anim.pause` flag. Anim should be added to an active `h2d.Scene` in order to function.

tile.haxe_doc: The tile to display. See `h2d.Tile` documentation for details. If the tile is null, a pink 5x5 bitmap will be displayed instead.

width.haxe_doc:
If set, rescale the tile to match the given width, keeping the aspect ratio unless `height` is also set.
Note that both `width` and `height` are `null` by default and in order to retrieve bitmap dimensions with scaling accurately, call `getSize` method or address `tile.width/height` to get unscaled dimensions.

height.haxe_doc:
If set, rescale the tile to match the given height, keeping the aspect ratio unless `width` is also set.
Note that both `width` and `height` are `null` by default and in order to retrieve bitmap dimensions with scaling accurately, call `getSize` method or address `tile.width/height` to get unscaled dimensions.

class.haxe_doc:
Displays a single bitmap Tile on the screen.
It is a most primitive Drawable and easiest to use, but vastly inferior to others in terms of performance when used for rendering of many tiles. When dealing with many images at once, it is recommended to use batched renderers, like `h2d.SpriteBatch` or `h2d.TileGroup`.

Max.haxe_doc: The output color is the max of the source and dest colors. The blend parameters Src and Dst are ignored for this equation. `Out = MAX( Src, Dst )`

Min.haxe_doc: The output color is the min of the source and dest colors. The blend parameters Src and Dst are ignored for this equation. `Out = MAX( Src, Dst )`

enum.haxe_doc: The blending rules when rendering a Tile/Material.

x.haxe_doc: X position of the camera in world space based on anchorX.

y.haxe_doc: Y position of the camera in world space based on anchorY.

scaleX.haxe_doc: Horizontal scale factor of the camera. Scaling applied, using anchored position as pivot.

scaleY.haxe_doc: Vertical scale factor of the camera. Scaling applied, using anchored position as pivot.

rotation.haxe_doc: Rotation of the camera in radians. Camera is rotated around anchored position.

clipViewport.haxe_doc:
Enables viewport clipping. Allow to restrict rendering area of the camera to the viewport boundaries.
Does not affect the user input when Camera is set as interactive camera.

viewportX.haxe_doc: Horizontal viewport offset of the camera relative to internal scene viewport (see `h2d.Scene.scaleMode`) in scene coordinates. ( default : 0 ) Automatically scales on scene resize.

viewportY.haxe_doc: Vertical viewport offset of the camera relative to internal scene viewport (see `h2d.Scene.scaleMode`) in scene coordinates. ( default : 0 ) Automatically scales on scene resize.

viewportWidth.haxe_doc: Camera viewport width in scene coordinates. ( default : scene.width ) Automatically scales on scene resize.

viewportHeight.haxe_doc: Camera viewport height in scene coordinates. ( default: scene.height ) Automatically scales on scene resize.

anchorX.haxe_doc: Horizontal anchor position inside viewport boundaries used for positioning and resize compensation. ( default : 0 ) Value is a percentile (0..1) from left viewport edge to right viewport edge with 0.5 being center.

anchorY.haxe_doc: Vertical anchor position inside viewport boundaries used for positioning and resize compensation. ( default : 0 ) Value is a percentile (0..1) from top viewport edge to bottom viewport edge with 0.5 being center.

visible.haxe_doc:
Camera visibility.
Does not affect the user input when Camera is set as interactive camera.

follow.haxe_doc: Makes camera to follow the referenced Object position.

followRotation.haxe_doc: Enables `h2d.Object.rotation` sync between `Camera.follow` object and Camera.

remove.haxe_doc: Detaches Camera from the Scene it currently attached to.

enter.haxe_doc: Internal usage Prepares RenderContext to render the camera contents and clips viewport if necessary. Should call `Camera.exit` afterwards.

exit.haxe_doc: Internal usage Causes RenderContext to restore the state prior to camera rendering. Should be called after `Camera.enter` when rendering is finished.

sync.haxe_doc: Internal usage Synchronizes the camera transform matrix.

setScale.haxe_doc: Sets the `Camera.scaleX` and `Camera.scaleY` to given `x` and `y`.

setPosition.haxe_doc: Sets the camera position to given `x` and `y`.

move.haxe_doc: Moves the camera position by given `dx` and `dy`.

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotates the camera relative to current rotation by given `angle` in radians.

setAnchor.haxe_doc: Sets the `Camera.anchorX` and `Camera.anchorY` to given `x` and `y`.

setViewport.haxe_doc:
Sets camera viewport dimensions. If `w` or `h` arguments are 0 - scene size is used (width or height respectively).
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

setRawViewport.haxe_doc: Sets camera viewport dimensions in raw format of 0..1 percentiles.

screenXToCamera.haxe_doc:
Convert screen position into a local camera position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

screenYToCamera.haxe_doc:
Convert screen position into a local camera position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

cameraXToScreen.haxe_doc:
Convert local camera position to absolute screen position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

cameraYToScreen.haxe_doc:
Convert local camera position to absolute screen position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

sceneXToCamera.haxe_doc: Convert an absolute scene position into a local camera position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.screenXToCamera` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.

sceneYToCamera.haxe_doc: Convert an absolute scene position into a local camera position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.screenYToCamera` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.

cameraXToScene.haxe_doc: Convert local camera position into absolute scene position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.cameraXToScreen` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.

cameraYToScene.haxe_doc: Convert local camera position into absolute scene position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.cameraYToScreen` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.

eventToCamera.haxe_doc: Internal usage Convert `Event.relX` and `Event.relY` to local camera position.

screenToCamera.haxe_doc:
Convert screen position into a local camera position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

cameraToScreen.haxe_doc:
Convert local camera position to absolute screen position.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

sceneToCamera.haxe_doc:
Convert an absolute scene position into a local camera position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.screenToCamera` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

cameraToScene.haxe_doc:
Convert local camera position into absolute scene position. Does not represent screen position, see `Camera.cameraToScreen` to convert position with accounting of `scaleMode`.
Requires Camera being attached to a Scene.

class.haxe_doc:
A 2D camera representation attached to `h2d.Scene`.
Enables ability to move, scale and rotate the scene viewport.
Scene supports usage of multiple Camera instances. To configure which layers each Camera renders - `Camera.layerVisible` method should be overridden. By default, camera does not clip out the contents that are outside camera bounding box, which can be enabled through `Camera.clipViewport`.
Due to Heaps event handling structure, only one Camera instance can handle the mouse/touch input, and can be set through `h2d.Scene.interactiveCamera` variable. Note that during even handing, interactive camera does not check if the Camera itself is visible nor the layers filters as well as `clipViewport` is not applied.

Top.haxe_doc:
Aligns children to the top edge of the `Flow`.
Only applicable to the `Flow.verticalAlign`.

Left.haxe_doc:
Aligns children to the left edge of the `Flow`.
Only applicable to the `Flow.horizontalAlign`.

Right.haxe_doc:
Aligns children to the right edge of the `Flow`.
Only applicable to the `Flow.horizontalAlign`.

Middle.haxe_doc: Aligns children to the center of the `Flow`.

Bottom.haxe_doc:
Aligns children to the bottom edge of the `Flow`.
Only applicable to the `Flow.verticalAlign`.

enum.haxe_doc: `Flow` content alignment rules.

Horizontal.haxe_doc:
Children are aligned horizontally from left to right (or right to left when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).
If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next row if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.
`Flow.lineHeight` can be used to set a fixed row height when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`. Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.verticalAlign` value vertically with `null` being treated as `Bottom`.

Vertical.haxe_doc:
Children are aligned vertically from top to bottom (or bottom to top when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).
If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next column if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.
`Flow.colWidth` can be used to set a fixed column width when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`. Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.horizontalAlign` value horizontally with `null` being treated as `Left`.

Stack.haxe_doc: Children are aligned independently (`Flow.reverse` has no effect).

enum.haxe_doc: The `Flow.layout` type.

Expand.haxe_doc: Children larger than `Flow.maxWidth` / `Flow.maxHeight` will expand the flow size.

Limit.haxe_doc:
Limits the bounds reported by the flow using `Flow.maxWidth` or `Flow.maxHeight`, if set.
Children larger than max size will draw outside of the Flow bounds or overflow if `Flow.multiline` is enabled.

Hidden.haxe_doc:
Limits the bounds reported by the flow using `Flow.maxWidth` or `Flow.maxHeight`, if set.
Compared to `Limit` - Flow will mask out the content that is outside of Flow bounds.

Scroll.haxe_doc: Similar to `Hidden` but allows to scroll using `Flow.scroll*` properties for control.

enum.haxe_doc: The `Flow.overflow` rules.

paddingLeft.haxe_doc: An extra padding to the left of the flow element.

paddingTop.haxe_doc: An extra padding to the top of the flow element.

paddingRight.haxe_doc: An extra padding to the right of the flow element.

paddingBottom.haxe_doc: An extra padding to the bottom of the flow element.

isAbsolute.haxe_doc: When enabled, element won't be automatically positioned during `Flow.reflow` and instead treated as an absolute element relative to the Flow.

horizontalAlign.haxe_doc:
The `Flow.horizontalAlign` override.
If `FlowProperties.isAbsolute` is enabled - aligns the element within the Flow boundaries. Otherwise affects the element alignment within the Flow. Does not affect the alignment if `Flow.layout` is `Horizontal`.

verticalAlign.haxe_doc:
The `Flow.verticalAlign` override.
If `FlowProperties.isAbsolute` is enabled - aligns the element within the Flow boundaries. Otherwise affects the element alignment within the Flow. Does not affect the alignment if `Flow.layout` is `Vertical`.

offsetX.haxe_doc:
A visual offset of the element along the X axis.
Offset does not affect the occupied space by the element, and can lead to overlapping with other elements.

offsetY.haxe_doc:
A visual offset of the element along the Y axis.
Offset does not affect the occupied space by the element, and can lead to overlapping with other elements.

minWidth.haxe_doc: The minimum occupied width of the element within the flow.

minHeight.haxe_doc: The minimum occupied height of the element within the flow.

calculatedWidth.haxe_doc: The calculated element width since last element reflow.

calculatedHeight.haxe_doc: The calculated element height since last element reflow.

isBreak.haxe_doc: Whether this element is the last on its current row/column, and the next flow element being on the next row/column after overflow.

lineBreak.haxe_doc: Forces this element to break the line and flow onto the next row/column. `Flow.multiline` is not required to be enabled.

autoSize.haxe_doc: When set, element will use the maximum size of non-autoSize elements as size constraint instead of current constraint on the parent flow.

autoSizeWidth.haxe_doc: The horizontal part of `autoSize`: the share of the available width given to the element, or `null` to disable it.

autoSizeHeight.haxe_doc: The vertical part of `autoSize`: the share of the available height given to the element, or `null` to disable it.

class.haxe_doc:
An individual `Flow` element properties.
Can be obtained after adding the element to the Flow and calling `Flow.getProperties`. Contains configuration unique of each Flow element.

PADDING_IGNORE_PARENT.haxe_doc: A special padding value for the properties of a child (`FlowProperties.paddingLeft` and others): the child ignores the padding of the flow on this side and extends to its border.

needReflow.haxe_doc:
If some sub element gets resized, you need to set reflow to true in order to force the reflow of elements. You can also directly call `Flow.reflow` which will immediately update all elements positions.
If a reflow is needed, `Flow.reflow` will be called before rendering the flow. Each change in one of the flow properties or addition/removal of elements will set needReflow to true.

horizontalAlign.haxe_doc: Horizontal alignment of elements inside the flow. See `FlowAlign` for more details.

verticalAlign.haxe_doc: Vertical alignment of elements inside the flow. See `FlowAlign` for more details.

minWidth.haxe_doc: Ensures that Flow is at least the specified outer width at all times when not null.

minHeight.haxe_doc: Ensures that Flow is at least the specified outer height at all times when not null.

maxWidth.haxe_doc: Attempts to limit the Flow outer width to the specified width. Used as a baseline for overflow when `Flow.multiline` is enabled and `Flow.layout` is `Horizontal`.

maxHeight.haxe_doc: Attempts to limit the Flow outer height to the specified height. Used as a baseline for overflow when `Flow.multiline` is enabled and `Flow.layout` is `Vertical`.

lineHeight.haxe_doc: Sets the minimum row height when `Flow.layout` is `Horizontal`.

colWidth.haxe_doc: Sets the minimum colum width when `Flow.layout` is `Vertical`.

overflow.haxe_doc: Enabling overflow will treat maxWidth/maxHeight and lineHeight/colWidth constraints as absolute : bigger elements will overflow instead of expanding the limit. See respective `FlowOverflow` values for more details.

paddingHorizontal.haxe_doc:
Will set `Flow.paddingLeft` and `Flow.paddingRight` to the given value.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingVertical.haxe_doc:
Will set `Flow.paddingTop` and `Flow.paddingBottom` to the given value.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingLeft.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the left edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingRight.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the right edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingTop.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the top edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingBottom.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the bottom edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

horizontalSpacing.haxe_doc: The horizontal separation spacing between two flowed elements.

verticalSpacing.haxe_doc: The vertical separation spacing between two flowed elements.

enableInteractive.haxe_doc:
Adds an `h2d.Interactive` to the Flow that is accessible through `Flow.interactive` field. This Interactive is automatically resized to cover the whole Flow area.
Flow is added as a bottom-most (after the `Flow.backgroundTile`) child as to not impede flow elements with Interactives.

backgroundTile.haxe_doc:
Setting a background tile will create an `h2d.ScaleGrid` background which uses the `Flow.borderWidth`/`Flow.borderHeigh` values for its borders.
It will automatically resize when the reflow is done to cover the whole Flow area.

innerWidth.haxe_doc:
Calculate the client width, which is the inner size of the flow without the borders and padding.
@see `Flow.padding`

innerHeight.haxe_doc:
Calculate the client height, which is the inner size of the flow without the borders and padding.
@see `Flow.padding`

outerWidth.haxe_doc:
Flow total width. Compared to `Flow.innerWidth`, it also includes paddings and, if enabled, borders (see `Flow.borderWidth`).
@see `Flow.padding`

outerHeight.haxe_doc:
Flow total height Compared to `Flow.innerHeight`, it also includes paddings and, if enabled, borders (see `Flow.borderHeight`).
@see `Flow.padding`

layout.haxe_doc: The Flow item layout rules. See `FlowLayout` for specific details on each mode.

isInline.haxe_doc: When isInline is set to false, the flow size will be reported based on its bounds instead of its calculated size. @see `Object.getSize`

debug.haxe_doc: When set to true, the Flow will display a debug overlay. * Red box around the flow * Green box for the client space. * Blue boxes for each element. When set to false, this will disable the ability to debug the flow.

multiline.haxe_doc: When set to true, uses specified lineHeight/colWidth instead of maxWidth/maxHeight for alignment.

reverse.haxe_doc:
When set to true, children are aligned in reverse order.
Note that it does not affect render ordering, and may cause overlap of elements due to them positioned in reverse order.

fillWidth.haxe_doc: When set to true, if a width constraint is present and `minWidth` is null - Flow will expand to fill all the available horizontal space

fillHeight.haxe_doc: When set to true, if a height constraint is present and `minHeight` is null - Flow will expand to fill all the available vertical space

scrollBar.haxe_doc: The scroll bar component created when `overflow` is set to `Scroll`

scrollBarCursor.haxe_doc: The scroll bar cursor component created when `overflow` is set to `Scroll`

scrollWheelSpeed.haxe_doc: The amount of scrolling that is done when using mouse wheel (in pixels).

scrollPosY.haxe_doc: The current scrolling position for the flow content (in pixels). Only applies when overflow is Scroll or Hidden.

getProperties.haxe_doc:
Get the per-element properties. Returns null if the element is not currently part of the Flow.
Requesting the properties will cause a reflow regardless if properties values were changed or not.

addSpacing.haxe_doc:
Adds some spacing by either increasing the padding of the latest non-absolute element or the padding of the flow if there are no elements in it.
The padding affected depends on the `Flow.layout` mode. It's impossible to add spacing with a `Stack` Flow layout.

scrollIntoView.haxe_doc: Scrolls the flow vertically so that the element is visible. Returns `false` if the flow is not scrollable (see `overflow`).

makeBackground.haxe_doc: Creates the background of the flow for the tile, a `ScaleGrid` using the borders of the flow. Can be overridden to use another kind of background.

reflow.haxe_doc: Call to force all flowed elements position to be updated. See `Flow.needReflow` for more information.

onBeforeReflow.haxe_doc: Sent at the start of the `Flow.reflow`.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Flow instance. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Flow adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc: An automatic layout system.

prevChar.haxe_doc: A character that should precede current character in order to apply this kerning.

offset.haxe_doc: A kerning offset between the character pair in pixels.

class.haxe_doc: A `FontChar` kerning information as well as linked list of kernings. See `FontChar.kerning`.

t.haxe_doc: A Tile representing position of a character on the texture.

width.haxe_doc:
Horizontal advance value of the character.
On top of advance, letter spacing is affected by `FontChar.kerning` matches and `Text.letterSpacing`.

kerning.haxe_doc:
Linked list of kerning values.
In order to add new kerning values use `FontChar.addKerning` and `FontChar.getKerningOffset` to retrieve kerning offsets.

addKerning.haxe_doc: Adds a new kerning to the character with specified `prevChar` and `offset`.

getKerningOffset.haxe_doc: Returns kerning offset for a pair `[prevChar, currentChar]` or `0` if there was no paired kerning value.

clone.haxe_doc: Clones the character instance.

class.haxe_doc: A single `Font` character descriptor.

abstract.haxe_doc: Channel reading method for `FontType.SignedDistanceField`.

Red.haxe_doc: Use red channel of a texture to determine distance.

Green.haxe_doc: Use green channel of a texture to determine distance.

Blue.haxe_doc: Use blue channel of a texture to determine distance.

Alpha.haxe_doc: Use alpha channel of a texture to determine distance.

MultiChannel.haxe_doc: Use RGB channels of a texture to determine distance. See here for details: https://github.com/Chlumsky/msdfgen

Red.haxe_doc: Use red channel of a texture to determine distance.

Green.haxe_doc: Use green channel of a texture to determine distance.

Blue.haxe_doc: Use blue channel of a texture to determine distance.

Alpha.haxe_doc: Use alpha channel of a texture to determine distance.

MultiChannel.haxe_doc: Use RGB channels of a texture to determine distance. See here for details: https://github.com/Chlumsky/msdfgen

FontGroup.haxe_doc: A font group is a virtual font that contains one or several sub fonts that can be selected with h2d.Text.resolveSubFont.

enum.haxe_doc: The rendering type of the of the `Font` instance.

name.haxe_doc: The font name. Assigned on font creation and can be used to identify font instances.

size.haxe_doc: Current font size. Font can be resized with `resizeTo`.

baseLine.haxe_doc:
The baseline value of the font represents the base on which characters will sit.
Used primarily with `HtmlText` to sit multiple fonts and images at the same line.

lineHeight.haxe_doc: Font line height provides vertical offset for each new line of the text.

tile.haxe_doc: Reference to the source Tile containing all glyphs of the Font.

tilePath.haxe_doc: The resource path of the source Tile. Either relative to .fnt or to resources root.

type.haxe_doc: The font type. BitmapFonts rendered as-is, but SDF fonts will use an extra shader to produce scalable smooth fonts. See `FontType.SignedDistanceField` for more details.

charset.haxe_doc: Font charset allows to resolve specific char codes that are not directly present in glyph map as well as detect spaces. Defaults to `hxd.Charset.getDefault()`.

subFonts.haxe_doc: Subfonts will be selected when assigned with the `h2d.Text.resolveSubFont` method.

getChar.haxe_doc: Returns a `FontChar` instance corresponding to the `code`. If font char is not present in glyph list, `charset.resolveChar` is called. Returns `null` if glyph under specified charcode does not exist. @param code The charcode to search for.

clone.haxe_doc: Creates a copy of the font instance.

dispose.haxe_doc: Disposes of the Font instance. Equivalent to `Tile.dispose`.

calcBaseLine.haxe_doc: Calculate a baseLine default value based on available glyphs.

class.haxe_doc:
An instance of a text font.
Heaps comes with a default Font that covers basic ASCII characters, and can be retrieved via `hxd.res.DefaultFont.get()`.

buffer.haxe_doc: The primitive vertex buffer, holding its vertexes data.

indexes.haxe_doc: The primitive indexes buffer, holding its triangles indices.

refCount.haxe_doc: Current amount of references to this Primitive. Use `incref` and `decref` methods to affect this value. If it reaches 0, it will be automatically disposed.

triCount.haxe_doc: The number of triangles the primitive has.

vertexCount.haxe_doc: The number of vertexes the primitive has.

getCollider.haxe_doc: Return a local collider for the primitive

getBounds.haxe_doc: Return the bounds for the primitive

incref.haxe_doc: Increase reference count of the Primitive.

decref.haxe_doc: Decrease reference count of the Primitive. If recount reaches zero, Primitive is automatically disposed when last referencing mesh is removed from scene.

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocate the primitive on GPU. Used for internal usage.

selectMaterial.haxe_doc: Select the specified sub material before drawin. Used for internal usage.

getMaterialIndexes.haxe_doc: Returns the number and offset of indexes for the specified material

getMaterialIndexStart.haxe_doc: Returns the first index of the given material group and level of detail.

getMaterialIndexCount.haxe_doc: Returns the number of indexes of the given material group and level of detail.

render.haxe_doc: Render the primitive. Used for internal usage.

dispose.haxe_doc: Dispose the primitive, freeing the GPU memory it uses.

toString.haxe_doc: Return the primitive type.

screenRatioToLod.haxe_doc: Returns the level of detail to use for an object covering `screenRatio` of the screen (see `h3d.scene.Mesh.screenRatio`).

getCullingScreenRatio.haxe_doc: Returns the screen ratio under which the meshes using this primitive are not drawn at all (`0` to always draw them).

class.haxe_doc: h3d.prim.Primitive is the base class for all 3D primitives. You can't create an instance of it and need to use one of its subclasses.

tile.haxe_doc: The Tile used as source of Texture to render.

bevel.haxe_doc:
Adds bevel cut-off at line corners.
The value is a percentile in range of 0...1, dictating at which point edges get beveled based on their angle. Value of 0 being not beveled and 1 being always beveled.

clear.haxe_doc: Clears the Graphics contents.

moveTo.haxe_doc: Ends the current line and starts new one at given position.

curveTo.haxe_doc: * Draws a quadratic Bezier curve using the current line style from the current drawing position to (cx, cy) and using the control point that (bx, by) specifies. * IvanK Lib port ( http://lib.ivank.net )

cubicCurveTo.haxe_doc: * Draws a cubic Bezier curve from the current drawing position to the specified anchor point. * IvanK Lib port ( http://lib.ivank.net ) * @param bx control X for start point * @param by control Y for start point * @param cx control X for end point * @param cy control Y for end point * @param dx end X * @param dy end Y * @param nsegments = 40

lineTo.haxe_doc: Draws a straight line from the current drawing position to the given position.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Graphics instance. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Graphics adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple interface to draw arbitrary 2D geometry.
Usage notes: * While Graphics allows for multiple unique textures, each texture swap causes a new drawcall, and due to that it's recommended to minimize the amount of used textures per Graphics instance, ideally limiting to only one texture. * Due to how Graphics operate, removing them from the active `h2d.Scene` will cause a loss of all data.

Accurate.haxe_doc: Accurate line height calculations. Each line will adjust it's height according to it's contents.

TextOnly.haxe_doc: Only text adjusts line heights, and `` tags do not affect it (partial legacy behavior).

Constant.haxe_doc: Legacy line height mode. When used, line heights remain constant based on `Text.font` variable.

enum.haxe_doc: The `HtmlText` line height calculation rules.

Top.haxe_doc: Align images along the top of the text line.

Bottom.haxe_doc: Align images to sit on the base line of the text.

Middle.haxe_doc: Align images to the middle between the top of the text line its base line.

enum.haxe_doc: `HtmlText` img tag vertical alignment rules.

resolveSubFont.haxe_doc: Returns the font used by the text when its font is a group of fonts (`FontGroup`). Returns the first sub font by default: it can be replaced to select another one, such as the one of the current language.

font.haxe_doc: The font used to render text.

textColor.haxe_doc: Text RGB color. Alpha value is ignored.

maxWidth.haxe_doc:
When set, limits maximum line width and causes word-wrap. Affects positioning of the text depending on `textAlign` value.
When Text is affected by size constraints (see `Object.constraintSize`), smallest of the two is used for word-wrap.

dropShadow.haxe_doc: Adds simple drop shadow to the Text with specified offset, color and alpha. Causes text to be rendered twice (first drop shadow and then the text itself).

textWidth.haxe_doc: Calculated text width. Can exceed maxWidth in certain cases.

textHeight.haxe_doc:
Calculated text height.
Not a completely precise text metric and increments in the `Font.lineHeight` steps. In `HtmlText`, can be increased by various values depending on the active line font and `HtmlText.lineHeightMode` value.

textAlign.haxe_doc: Text align rules dictate how the text lines are positioned. See `Align` for specific details on each alignment mode.

wordBreak.haxe_doc: When `lineBreak` is enabled, allow breaking inside a word if it does not fit on a single line. Without it, a word longer than `maxWidth` overflows the text bounds.

validateText.haxe_doc:
Extra validation of the `text` variable when it's changed. Override to add custom validation.
Only validation of the text is allowed, and attempting to change the text value will lead to undefined behavior.

calcTextWidth.haxe_doc: Calculates and returns width of the provided `text` with settings this Text instance.

splitText.haxe_doc: Perform a word-wrap of the `text` based on this Text settings.

splitRawText.haxe_doc: Advanced usage Perform a word-wrap of the text based on this Text settings. @param text String to word-wrap. @param leftMargin Starting x offset of the first line. @param afterData Minimum remaining space required at the end of the line. @param font Optional overriding font to use instead of currently set. @param sizes Optional line width array. Will be populated with sizes of split lines if present. Sizes will include both `leftMargin` in it's first line entry. @param prevChar Optional character code for concatenation purposes (proper kernings).

getTextProgress.haxe_doc: Returns cut `text` based on `progress` percentile. Can be used to gradually show appearing text. (Especially useful when using `HtmlText`)

setColorSegments.haxe_doc: Set the text color segments. This is an Array containing a pair of (position,color). Each time the text display will reach the given position, the color will be set. The segment color is multiplied by the global textColor.

class.haxe_doc:
A basic text renderer with multiline support.
See [Text](https://github.com/HeapsIO/heaps/wiki/Text) section of the manual for more details.

defaultLoadImage.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to load images for `` tag. See `HtmlText.loadImage` for details.

defaultLoadFont.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to load fonts for `<font>` tags with `face` attribute. See `HtmlText.loadFont` for details.

defaultFormatText.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to format assigned text. See `HtmlText.formatText` for details.

defineDefaultHtmlTag.haxe_doc: Associate a custom html tag to a specific font and color.

condenseWhite.haxe_doc: When enabled, condenses extra spaces (carriage-return, line-feed, tabulation and space character) to one space. If not set, uncondensed whitespace is left as is, as well as line-breaks.

propagateInteractiveNode.haxe_doc: When enabled, nodes that create interactives will propagate events

imageSpacing.haxe_doc: The spacing after `` tags in pixels.

lineHeightMode.haxe_doc: Line height calculation mode controls how much space lines take up vertically. Changing mode to `Constant` restores the legacy behavior of HtmlText.

imageVerticalAlign.haxe_doc: Vertical alignment of the images in `` tag relative to the text.

loadImage.haxe_doc: Method that should return an `h2d.Tile` instance for `` tags. By default calls `HtmlText.defaultLoadImage` method. HtmlText does not cache tile instances. Due to internal structure, method should be deterministic and always return same Tile on consequent calls with same `url` input. @param url A value contained in `src` attribute.

formatText.haxe_doc: Called when text is assigned, allowing to process arbitrary text to a valid XHTML.

defineHtmlTag.haxe_doc: Define a custom html tag to be displayed with specific font and color.

defineHtmlTags.haxe_doc: Define or reset a set of custom html tags to be displayed with specific font and color.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple HTML text renderer.
See the [Text](https://github.com/HeapsIO/heaps/wiki/Text) section of the manual for more details and a list of the supported HTML tags.

propagateEvents.haxe_doc: If set, events are also sent to the interactives below this one.

cursor.haxe_doc: The cursor displayed when the mouse is over the interactive.

handleEvent.haxe_doc: Handles an event sent to the interactive.

getInteractiveScene.haxe_doc: Returns the scene of the interactive.

class.haxe_doc: An object which can receive events from `SceneEvents`, such as `h2d.Interactive` and `h3d.scene.Interactive`.

width.haxe_doc: Width of the Interactive. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

height.haxe_doc: Height of the Interactive. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

cursor.haxe_doc: Cursor used when Interactive is under mouse cursor.

isEllipse.haxe_doc: Performs an elliptic hit-test instead of rectangular one based on `Interactive.width` and `height`. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

enableRightButton.haxe_doc: When enabled, interacting with secondary mouse buttons (right button/wheel) will cause `onPush`, `onClick`, `onRelease` and `onReleaseOutside` callbacks. Otherwise those callbacks will only be triggered with primary mouse button (left button).

allowMultiClick.haxe_doc: When enabled, allows to receive several onClick events the same frame.

backgroundColor.haxe_doc: If set, Interactive will draw a `Tile` with `[width, height]` dimensions of specified color (including alpha).

shape.haxe_doc: Detailed shape collider for Interactive. If set, `width` and `height` properties are ignored for collision checks.

shapeX.haxe_doc: Detailed shape X offset from Interactive.

shapeY.haxe_doc: Detailed shape Y offset from Interactive.

preventClick.haxe_doc: Reset current pressed state of the Interactive, preventing the `onClick` or `onReleaseOutside` being triggered when user releases mouse button.

focus.haxe_doc: Sets focus on this `Interactive`. If Interactive was not already focused and it receives focus - `onFocus` event is sent. Interactive won't become focused if during `onFocus` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes focus from interactive if it's focused. If Interactive is currently focused - `onFocusLost` event will be sent. Interactive won't lose focus if during `onFocusLost` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

isOver.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently hovered by the mouse.

hasFocus.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently focused.

onOver.haxe_doc:
Sent when mouse enters Interactive hitbox area.
`Event.propagate` and `Event.cancel` are ignored during `onOver`. Propagation can be set with `onMove` event, as well as cancelling `onMove` will prevent `onOver`.

onOut.haxe_doc: Sent when mouse exits Interactive hitbox area. `Event.propagate` and `Event.cancel` are ignored during `onOut`.

onPush.haxe_doc: Sent when Interactive is pressed by the user.

onRelease.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive is unpressed under multiple circumstances. * Always sent if user releases mouse while it is inside Interactive hitbox area. This happens regardless if that Interactive was pressed prior or not, and due to that it's not guaranteed that `Interactive.onPush` would precede this event. `Event.kind` is set to `ERelease` during this event. * Sent before `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` if this Interactive was pressed, but released outside its hitbox area. `Event.kind` is set to `EReleaseOutside` during this event.
See `Interactive.onClick` and `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` methods for separate events that trigger only when user interacts with this particular Interactive.

onReleaseOutside.haxe_doc:
Sent when user presses the Interactive, moves the mouse outside its hitbox area and releases the mouse button.
Can be prevented to fire by calling `Interactive.preventClick` during or after `Interactive.onPush` event.
`Interactive.onRelease` is sent with `Event.kind` being `EReleaseOutside` just before this event.

onClick.haxe_doc:
Sent when the Interactive is clicked by the user.
Can be prevented to fire by calling `Interactive.preventClick` during or after `Interactive.onPush` event.
`Interactive.onRelease` is sent with `Event.kind` being `ERelease` just before this event.

onMove.haxe_doc:
Sent when user moves within the Interactive hitbox area. See `Interactive.onCheck` for event when user does not move the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onWheel.haxe_doc: Sent when user scrolls mouse wheel above the Interactive. Wheel delta can be obtained through the `Event.wheelDelta`.

onFocus.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive receives focus during `Interactive.focus` call.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from becoming focused.

onFocusLost.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive lost focus either via `Interactive.blur` call or when user clicks on another Interactive/outside this Interactive hitbox area.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from losing focus.

onKeyUp.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user unpressed a keyboard key. Unpressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onKeyDown.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user pressed a keyboard key. Pressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onCheck.haxe_doc:
Sent every frame when user hovers an Interactive but does not move the mouse. See `Interactive.onMove` for event when user moves the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onTextInput.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user inputs text. Character added can be accessed through `Event.charCode`.

class.haxe_doc:
A user input handler.
Hitbox area can be a rectangle, an ellipse or an arbitrary shape (`h2d.col.Collider`).
Note that Interactive does not reports its hitbox bounds in `Object.getBounds` unless `Interactive.backgroundColor` is set, in which case `width` and `height` are reported.
By default, Interactive only reacts to primary (left) mouse button for actions, see `Interactive.enableRightButton` for details.

addChild.haxe_doc: Adds a child object `s` at the end of the topmost layer. @param s An object to be added.

add.haxe_doc: * Adds a child object `s` at the end of the given `layer`. * @param s An object to be added. * @param layer An index of the layer the object should be added at with 0 being the bottom-most layer. Pass -1 to use topmost layer. * @param index An optional index at which the object should be inserted inside the layer. Pass -1 to append to the end.

getChildAtLayer.haxe_doc: Return the `n`th element among the immediate children list on the `layer`, or null if there is none. @param layer The layer children of which are used. Pass -1 to use the topmost layer.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Layers instance. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Layers adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A layer-based container for Objects.
Hierarchically organizes objects based on their layer. Supports per-layer Y-sorting through `Layers.ysort`.

unmask.haxe_doc: Unmasks the previously masked area from `Mask.maskWith`. @param ctx The render context to unmask.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the masked area.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the masked area.

scrollX.haxe_doc: Horizontal scroll offset of the Mask content in pixels. Can be clamped by `Mask.scrollBounds`.

scrollY.haxe_doc: Vertical scroll offset of the Mask content in pixels. Can be clamped by `Mask.scrollBounds`.

scrollBounds.haxe_doc: Optional scroll boundaries that prevent content from overscroll.

scrollTo.haxe_doc: Scroll the Mask content to the specified offset.

scrollBy.haxe_doc: Scroll the Mask content by the specified offset relative to the current scroll offset.

class.haxe_doc:
Restricts rendering area within the `[width, height]` rectangle. For more advanced masking, see `h2d.filter.AbstractMask`.
Rotation of the mask does not rotate the masked area and instead causes it to cover the bounding box of the mask.
The `Mask.maskWidth` and `Mask.unmask` can be used to mask out rendering area without direct usage of Mask instance in-between.

follow.haxe_doc: Reference to target 3D object to follow.

pixelSnap.haxe_doc: Rounds the resulting 2d position of follower aligning it to s2d pixel grid.

followVisibility.haxe_doc: If enabled, follower will mirror visibility of target object.

offsetX.haxe_doc: Extra camera projection offset along X-axis to which follower will attach to.

offsetY.haxe_doc: Extra camera projection offset along Y-axis to which follower will attach to.

offsetZ.haxe_doc: Extra camera projection offset along Z-axis to which follower will attach to.

horizontalAlign.haxe_doc: Horizontal object alignment relative to anchoring point.

verticalAlign.haxe_doc: Vertical object alignment relative to anchoring point.

depthBias.haxe_doc: Calculate the depth for masking with the given bias in 3D position units, relative to current camera.

cameraRelative.haxe_doc: Express the offset in terms of the current camera direction.

autoRemove.haxe_doc: If enabled, the ObjectFollower will remove itself if the object followed is null or removed.

class.haxe_doc: Follows the 3D object position in current 3D camera, synchronizing the follower position to projected 2D position of the followed object.

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Particles are sorted back-to-front every frame based on their current position.

enum.haxe_doc: See `ParticleGroup.sortMode` - not used anywhere.

Point.haxe_doc: A single Point, that emits in all directions.

enum.haxe_doc: The particle emission pattern modes. See `ParticleGroup.emitMode`.

priority.haxe_doc: The priority of the shader in the shader list: the shaders are sorted by ascending priority. See `setPriority`.

setPriority.haxe_doc: Shader priority should only be changed *before* the shader is added to a material.

getParamValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the parameter of the given index. Generated by the macro.

getParamFloatValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the float parameter of the given index. Generated by the macro.

setParamIndexValue.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the parameter of the given index. Generated by the macro.

setParamIndexFloatValue.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the float parameter of the given index. Generated by the macro.

writeParam.haxe_doc: Writes the value of the parameter of the given index in the buffer, at the float position `pos`.

updateConstants.haxe_doc: Computes the shader variant from the values of the constant parameters (and globals). Generated by the macro.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the shader with the same parameter values. Generated by the macro.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the class name of the shader.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the shader.

class.haxe_doc: The base class of the shaders, written in HxSL in their `SRC` static variable. The `hxsl.Macros.buildShader` macro compiles the source and generates a property for each parameter. Shaders are added to materials or passes, and linked together into a `RuntimeShader`.

x.haxe_doc: Element X position.

y.haxe_doc: Element Y position.

scale.haxe_doc:
Shortcut to set both `BatchElement.scaleX` and `BatchElement.scaleY` at the same time.
Equivalent to `el.scaleX = el.scaleY = scale`.

scaleX.haxe_doc:
X-axis scaling factor of the element.
This variable is used only if `SpriteBatch.hasRotationScale` is set to `true`.

scaleY.haxe_doc:
Y-axis scaling factor of the element.
This variable is used only if `SpriteBatch.hasRotationScale` is set to `true`.

rotation.haxe_doc:
Element rotation in radians.
This variable is used only if `SpriteBatch.hasRotationScale` is set to `true`.

r.haxe_doc: Red tint value (0...1 range) of the element.

g.haxe_doc: Green tint value (0...1 range) of the element.

b.haxe_doc: Blue tint value (0...1 range) of the element.

t.haxe_doc:
The Tile this element renders.
Due to implementation specifics, this Tile instance is used only to provide rendering area, not the Texture itself, as `SpriteBatch.tile` used as a source of rendered texture.

alpha.haxe_doc: Alpha value of the element. Alias of `BatchElement.a`.

visible.haxe_doc: If set to `false`, element will not be rendered.

remove.haxe_doc: Remove this BatchElement from the parent SpriteBatch instance.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new BatchElement instance with provided Tile. @param t The tile used to render this BatchElement.

class.haxe_doc:
A base class for `SpriteBatch` elements which can be extended with custom logic.
See `BasicElement` as an example of custom element logic.

enable.haxe_doc: Disabling the group immediately removes it from rendering and resets it's state.

blendMode.haxe_doc: Configures blending mode for this group.

nparts.haxe_doc: Maximum number of particles alive at a time.

emitLoop.haxe_doc: If enabled, group will emit new particles indefinitely maintaining number of particles at `ParticleGroup.nparts`.

emitMode.haxe_doc: The pattern in which particles are emitted. See individual `PartEmitMode` values for more details.

emitStartDist.haxe_doc: Initial particle position distance from emission point.

emitDist.haxe_doc: Additional random particle position distance from emission point.

emitDistY.haxe_doc: Secondary random position distance modifier (used by `Box` emitMode)

emitDirectionAsAngle.haxe_doc: When enabled, particle rotation will match the particle movement direction angle.

emitSync.haxe_doc:
Randomized synchronization delay before particle appears after being emitted.
Usage note for non-relative mode: Particle will use configuration that was happened at time of emission, not when delay timer runs out.

emitDelay.haxe_doc:
Fixed delay before particle appears after being emitted.
Usage note for non-relative mode: Particle will use configuration that was happened at time of emission, not when delay timer runs out.

sizeIncr.haxe_doc: If set, particle will change it's size with time.

incrX.haxe_doc: If enabled, particle will increase on X-axis with `sizeIncr`.

incrY.haxe_doc: If enabled, particle will increase on Y-axis with `sizeIncr`.

sizeRand.haxe_doc: Additional random size increase when particle is created.

lifeRand.haxe_doc: Additional random lifetime increase when particle is created.

speedRand.haxe_doc: Additional random velocity increase when particle is created.

speedIncr.haxe_doc: If set, particle velocity will change over time.

gravityAngle.haxe_doc: The gravity angle in radians. `0` points down.

rotSpeed.haxe_doc: Initial rotation speed of the particle.

rotSpeedRand.haxe_doc: Additional random rotation speed when particle is created.

rotAuto.haxe_doc: If enabled, particles will be automatically rotated in the direction of particle velocity.

fadeIn.haxe_doc: The time in seconds during which particle alpha fades in after being emitted.

fadeOut.haxe_doc: The time in seconds at which particle will start to fade out before dying. Fade out time can be calculated with `lifetime - fadeOut`.

fadePower.haxe_doc: The exponent of the alpha transition speed on fade in and fade out.

frameCount.haxe_doc:
Total count of frames used by the group.
When 0, amount of frames in a group calculated by `frameDivisionX * frameDivisionY`.
Otherwise it's `min(frameDivisionX * frameDivisionY, frameCount)`.

animationRepeat.haxe_doc: The amount of times the animations will loop during lifetime. Settings it to 0 will stop the animation playback and each particle will have a random frame assigned at emission time.

texture.haxe_doc: The texture used to render particles.

colorGradient.haxe_doc: Optional color gradient texture for tinting.

isRelative.haxe_doc:
When enabled, causes particles to always render relative to the emitter position, moving along with it. Otherwise, once emitted, particles won't follow the emitter, and will render relative to the scene origin.
Non-relative mode is useful for simulating something like a smoke coming from a moving object, while relative mode things like jet flame that have to stick to its emission source.

rebuildOnChange.haxe_doc:
Should group rebuild on parameters change.
Note that some parameters take immediate effect on the existing particles, and some would force rebuild regardless of this setting.
Parameters that take immediate effect: `speedIncr`, `gravity`, `gravityAngle`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`, `fadePower`, `rotAuto`, `rotInit`, `incrX`, `incrY`, `emitLoop` and `blendMode`
Parameters that will always force rebuild: `enable`, `sortMode`, `isRelative`, `texture`, `frameCount`, `frameDivisionX`, `frameDivisionY` and `nparts`
Parameters that newer cause rebuild: `blendMode`, `colorGradient` and `animationRepeat`

rebuild.haxe_doc: Reset current state of particle group and re-emit all particles.

save.haxe_doc: Saves the particle group configuration into a `Dynamic` object.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new particle group instance. @param p The parent Particles instance. Group does not automatically adds itself to the Particles.

class.haxe_doc: An emitter of a single particle group. Part of `Particles` simulation system.

onEnd.haxe_doc: Sent when all particle groups stopped playback. Restarts all groups by default.

save.haxe_doc: Saves Particles settings and returns an object that can be saved into a file and then loaded with a `Particles.load` method.

removeGroup.haxe_doc: Removes the group from the Particles.

getGroup.haxe_doc: Returns a group with a specified name or `null` if none found.

getGroups.haxe_doc: Returns an Iterator of particle groups within Particles.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Particles instance. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Particles adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A 2D particle system with wide range of customizability.
The Particles instance can contain multiple `ParticleGroup` instances - each of which works independently from one another.
To simplify designing of the particles [HIDE](https://github.com/HeapsIO/hide/) contains a dedicated 2D particle editor and stores the particle data in a JSON format, which then can be loaded with the `Particles.load` method: ```haxe var part = new h2d.Particles(); part.load(haxe.Json.parse(hxd.Res.my_parts_file.entry.getText()), hxd.Res.my_parts_file.entry.path); ```

STRICT.haxe_doc: If set, a missing texture or buffer parameter throws an error.

fillIntParam.haxe_doc: Writes the bits of an integer at the float position in the buffer.

fillRec.haxe_doc: Writes a value of the given shader type at the float position in the buffer, and returns the number of floats written.

get.haxe_doc: Returns the current context.

getType.haxe_doc: Returns the current context if it is an instance of the class, or `null`.

onContextChange.haxe_doc: Called when another context becomes the current one while one is set.

elapsedTime.haxe_doc: The time elapsed since the previous frame, in seconds.

textures.haxe_doc: The cache of the temporary render target textures.

globals.haxe_doc: The values of the global shader variables.

shaderBuffers.haxe_doc: The buffers receiving the shader globals and parameters.

setCurrent.haxe_doc: Makes this context the current one.

clearCurrent.haxe_doc: Clears the current context. Throws if this context is not the current one.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the temporary textures.

getParamValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value of a parameter of the shaders (or of a per object global). Throws if it is `null`, unless `opt` is set.

fillGlobals.haxe_doc: Writes the globals used by the shader in the buffers.

fillParams.haxe_doc: Writes the parameters, textures and buffers of the shaders in the buffers.

class.haxe_doc: The base class of the 2D and 3D render contexts (`h2d.RenderContext`, `h3d.scene.RenderContext`): time, globals, temporary textures, and the filling of the shader buffers.

globalAlpha.haxe_doc: Current transparency value used for rendering objects. Automatically managed by `Object`.

buffer.haxe_doc: Temporary vertex buffer used to emit Tiles when `RenderContext.BUFFERING` is on. Otherwise it's `null`. Internal usage only.

bufPos.haxe_doc: Current temporary buffer position. Internal usage only.

scene.haxe_doc: The 2D scene attached to this RenderContext instance.

defaultSmooth.haxe_doc: Internal usage Determines texture filtering method (Linear or Nearest). Not recommended to use - assign `Scene.defaultSmooth` instead.

killAlpha.haxe_doc: When enabled, pixels with alpha value below 0.001 will be discarded.

front2back.haxe_doc: When enabled, causes `Object` to render its children in reverse order.

onBeginDraw.haxe_doc: Sent before Drawable is rendered. Drawable won't be rendered if callback returns `false`.

onEnterFilter.haxe_doc: Sent before filter begins rendering. Filter (and it's object tree) won't be rendered if callback returns `false`.

onLeaveFilter.haxe_doc: Send after filter has been rendered.

tmpBounds.haxe_doc: Internal usage Used to calculate filter rendering bounds.

currentCamera.haxe_doc: The camera instance that is currently being rendered, if present, `null` otherwise.

hasBuffering.haxe_doc: Tells if tile buffering is enabled.

begin.haxe_doc: Internal usage Prepares RenderContext to begin rendering a new frame.

allocTarget.haxe_doc: Allocated a cached render target Texture with specified name, filter mode and current `Scene.width` and `Scene.height`. @returns Either precached Texture under same name or newly allocated one.

clear.haxe_doc: Clears current render target with specified color.

end.haxe_doc: Internal usage Performers cleanup after frame is rendered.

pushCamera.haxe_doc: Internal usage Applies Camera `cam` transform to current viewport and pushes it onto the camera stack. Should call `RenderContext.popCamera` when rendering is complete.

popCamera.haxe_doc: Internal usage Restores previous viewport state prior to camera rendering, removing it from the camera stack.

pushFilter.haxe_doc: Internal usage Prepares to render Filter and pushes provided Object onto filter stack. @returns true if filter is allowed to render, false otherwise (see `RenderContext.onEnterFilter`)

setFilterScale.haxe_doc: Internal usage Sets the current filter texture resolution scale factor.

popFilter.haxe_doc: Internal usage Finalizes Filter rendering and removes top-most Object from filter stack.

pushTargets.haxe_doc: Pushes an array of render targets onto target stack.

popTarget.haxe_doc: Pops current render target from the target stack. If last texture was removed from the stack, will restore the primary render buffer as a render target.

pushRenderZone.haxe_doc:
Sets rectangular render zone area, saving previous render zone settings. To respect previous render zone area, use `RenderContext.clipRenderZone` method.
`RenderContext.popRenderZone` should be called afterwards to clear render zone stack.

getCurrentRenderZone.haxe_doc: Returns the current render zone in `bounds` (or new bounds), or `null` if there is none.

clipRenderZone.haxe_doc: Pushes new render zone with respect to the old render zone settings by clipping new and old render zones, pushing the intersection area result. Used so that any call to the clipRenderZone respects the already set zone, and can't render outside of it.

drawScene.haxe_doc: Renders the assigned Scene. Same as `s2d.drawRec(s2d.renderer)`.

flush.haxe_doc: Flushes buffered tile data if one present.

beforeDraw.haxe_doc: Internal usage Should be called before performing a new draw call in order to sync shader data and other parameters.

beginDrawBatchState.haxe_doc: Prepares rendering with BatchState. Each state draw should be preceded with `swapTexture` call.

swapTexture.haxe_doc: Swap current active texture and prepares for next drawcall.

beginDrawObject.haxe_doc: Prepares rendering of the Drawable object with specified texture. @returns true if rendering is prepared, false otherwise (see `RenderContext.onBeginDraw`)

beginDrawBatch.haxe_doc: Begins buffered Tile render of the Drawable object. @returns true if rendering is prepared, false otherwise (see `RenderContext.onBeginDraw`)

new.haxe_doc: Create a new RenderContext and attach it to specified Scene. @param scene The scene which RenderContext will render.

class.haxe_doc:
A 2D scene renderer.
Passed during `Object.sync` and `Object.drawRec` and can be accessed directly via `Scene.renderer`.

tile.haxe_doc: The reference tile used as a Texture source to draw.

rangeMin.haxe_doc: If set, only tiles indexed above or equal to `rangeMin` will be drawn.

rangeMax.haxe_doc: If set, only tiles indexed below `rangeMax` will be drawn.

clear.haxe_doc: Clears all TileGroup contents and disposes allocated GPU memory.

invalidate.haxe_doc: When new data is added, it's not automatically flushed to the GPU memory if it was already allocated (when TileGroup is either rendered or received `Object.sync` call), in which case call `invalidate()` to force a refresh of the GPU data.

count.haxe_doc: Returns the number of tiles added to the group.

setDefaultColor.haxe_doc: Sets the default tinting color when adding new Tiles.

class.haxe_doc:
A static Tile batch renderer.
TileGroup follows an upload-once policy and does not allow modification of the already added geometry. To add new geometry it's mandatory to call `TileGroup.invalidate`. In case existing geometry has to be modified - entire group have to be cleared with `TileGroup.clear` and repopulated from ground up.
Usage note: While TileGroup allows for multiple unique textures, each texture swap causes a new drawcall, and due to that it's recommended to minimize the amount of used textures per TileGroup instance, ideally limiting to only one texture.

borderLeft.haxe_doc: The width of the left border in pixels.

borderRight.haxe_doc: The width of the right border in pixels.

borderTop.haxe_doc: The height of the top border in pixels.

borderBottom.haxe_doc: The height of the bottom border in pixels.

borderWidth.haxe_doc: Set the width of left and right borders altogether.

borderHeight.haxe_doc: Set the height of top and bottom borders altogether.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the bitmap. Setting to values less than `borderLeft + borderRight` leads to undefined results.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the bitmap. Setting to values less than `borderTop + borderBottom` leads to undefined results.

tileBorders.haxe_doc: When enabled, borders will be repeated along the edges instead of stretching to match the desired dimensions.

tileCenter.haxe_doc: When enabled, center will be repeated along the edges instead of stretching to match the desired dimensions.

ignoreScale.haxe_doc:
When enabled, the borders will ignore the final scale of the `h2d.ScaleGrid` to be rendered pixel perfect. This does not change the values of `borderLeft`, `borderRight`, `borderTop` or `borderBottom`.
Center tile is always stretched.

borderScale.haxe_doc: Scale factor applied to borders only. If combined with `ignoreScale`, becomes an absolute scale independent from the scene scale.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple 9-slice bitmap renderer.
Enables rendering of the Tile as a stretchable surface with unscaled corners, stretched center and either stretched or tiled borders. Set `ScaleGrid.width` and `ScaleGrid.height` to resize the ScaleGrid.

Left.haxe_doc: Anchor Scene viewport horizontally to the left side of the window. When passed to `verticalAlign` it will be treated as Center.

Right.haxe_doc: Anchor Scene viewport horizontally to the right side of the window. When passed to `verticalAlign` it will be treated as Center.

Center.haxe_doc: Anchor to the center of the window.

Top.haxe_doc: Anchor Scene viewport vertically to the top of the window. When passed to `horizontalAlign` it will be treated as Center.

Bottom.haxe_doc: Anchor Scene viewport vertically to the bottom of the window. When passed to `horizontalAlign` it will be treated as Center.

enum.haxe_doc: Viewport alignment when scaling mode supports it. See `ScaleMode`.

Resize.haxe_doc: Matches scene size to window size. `width` and `height` of Scene will match window size. Default scaling mode.

Zoom.haxe_doc:
Upscales/downscales the Scene internal viewport according to `level` and matches Scene size to `ceil(window size / level)`.
With `800x600` window, `Zoom(2)` will result in the `400x300` Scene size upscaled to fill the entire window.

enum.haxe_doc:
Scaling mode of the 2D Scene.
Set via `Scene.scaleMode`.
See ScaleMode2D sample for usage showcase.

setEvents.haxe_doc: Called when the scene is added to or removed (with `null`) from a `SceneEvents`.

handleEvent.haxe_doc: Returns the next interactive under the event position after `last` (or the first one if `last` is `null`), and sets the event position relative to it.

dispatchEvent.haxe_doc: Sends the event to the interactive, with its position relative to it.

dispatchListeners.haxe_doc: Sends the event to the event listeners of the scene, when no interactive handled it.

isInteractiveVisible.haxe_doc: Tells if the interactive is visible in the scene.

class.haxe_doc: A scene which can receive events from `SceneEvents`, such as `h2d.Scene` and `h3d.scene.Scene`.

render.haxe_doc: Renders the content to the current render target.

class.haxe_doc: Something which can be rendered by the engine, such as a `h3d.scene.Scene` or a `h2d.Scene` (see `hxd.App`).

width.haxe_doc: The current width (in pixels) of the scene. Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

height.haxe_doc: The current height (in pixels) of the scene. Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

viewportA.haxe_doc: Viewport horizontal scale transform value. Converts from scene space to screen space of [0, 2] range.

viewportD.haxe_doc: Viewport vertical scale transform value. Converts from scene space to screen space of [0, 2] range.

viewportX.haxe_doc: Horizontal viewport offset relative to top-left corner of the window. Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes. Offset is in screen-space coordinates: [-1, 1] where 0 is center of the window.

viewportY.haxe_doc: Vertical viewport offset relative to top-left corner of the window. Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes. Offset is in screen-space coordinates: [-1, 1] where 0 is center of the window.

offsetX.haxe_doc: Horizontal viewport offset relative to top-left corner of the window in pixels. Assigned if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

offsetY.haxe_doc: Vertical viewport offset relative to top-left corner of the window in pixels. Assigned if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

viewportScaleX.haxe_doc:
Horizontal scale of a scene when rendering to the screen.
Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

viewportScaleY.haxe_doc:
Vertical scale of a scene when rendering to the screen.
Can change if the screen gets resized or `scaleMode` changes.

mouseX.haxe_doc: The current mouse X coordinates (in pixels) relative to the current `Scene.interactiveCamera`.

mouseY.haxe_doc: The current mouse Y coordinates (in pixels) relative to the current `Scene.interactiveCamera`.

m.e: "zoom is deprecated, use scaleMode = Zoom(v) instead"

zoom.haxe_doc: The zoom factor of the scene, allows to set a fixed x2, x4 etc. zoom for pixel art When setting a zoom > 0, the scene resize will be automatically managed.

scaleMode.haxe_doc:
Scene scaling mode.
Important thing to keep in mind - Scene does not clip rendering to it's scaled size and graphics can render outside of it. However `RenderContext.drawTile` (and consecutively `Object.emitTile`) does check for those bounds and will clip out tiles that are outside of the scene bounds.

cameras.haxe_doc:
List of all cameras attached to the Scene. Should contain at least one camera to render (created by default).
Override `h2d.Camera.layerVisible` method to filter out specific layers from camera rendering.
To add or remove cameras use `Scene.addCamera` and `Scene.removeCamera` methods.

camera.haxe_doc: Alias to the first camera in the camera list: `cameras[0]`

interactiveCamera.haxe_doc:
Camera instance that handles the scene events.
Due to Heaps structure, only one Camera can work with the Interactives. Contrary to rendering, event handling does not check if layer is visible for the camera or not.
Should never be null. When set, if Camera does not belong to the Scene, it will be added with `Scene.addCamera`. Would cause an exception when trying to remove current interactive camera from the list.

defaultSmooth.haxe_doc: Controls the default value for `h2d.Drawable.smooth`. Default: `false`

renderer.haxe_doc: The current Scene renderer. Can be customized.

interactiveDirty.haxe_doc: Set when `interactive` is no longer guaranteed to be in front-to-back order, either because targets were added/removed or because the object tree was reordered. The list is rebuilt lazily by `Scene.checkInteractives` on the next event query.

m.e: "zoom is deprecated, use scaleMode = Zoom(v) instead"
"zoom is deprecated, use scaleMode = Zoom(v) instead"

removeCamera.haxe_doc: Removes the Camera from the Scene camera list. Attempting to remove current `Scene.interactiveCamera` would cause an exception.

m.e: "setFixedSize is deprecated, use scaleMode = Stretch(w, h) instead"

setFixedSize.haxe_doc: Set the fixed size for the scene, will prevent automatic scene resizing when screen size changes.

checkResize.haxe_doc: Recalculates the scene viewport parameters based on `scaleMode`.

getInteractive.haxe_doc: Returns the topmost visible Interactive at the specified coordinates.

addEventListener.haxe_doc: Add an event listener that will capture all events that were not caught by an `h2d.Interactive`

removeEventListener.haxe_doc: Remove a previously added event listener, returns false it was not part of the event listeners.

checkInteractives.haxe_doc: Rebuilds the event target list in front-to-back order if it was invalidated.

dispose.haxe_doc:
Dispose the scene and all its children, freeing used GPU memory.
If Scene was allocated, causes `Object.onRemove` on all Scene objects.

setElapsedTime.haxe_doc: Internal usage Before `Scene.render` or `Scene.sync` are called, allows to set how much time has elapsed (in seconds) since the last frame in order to update scene animations. This is managed automatically by hxd.App.

syncOnly.haxe_doc: Synchronize the scene without rendering, updating all objects and animations by the given amount of time, in seconds.

render.haxe_doc: Internal usage Render the scene on the screen.

mark.haxe_doc: Called at each step of the scene rendering (`"s2d sync"`, `"s2d draw"`, `"vsync"`), for profiling.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new 2D scene. A default 2D scene is already available in `hxd.App.s2d`.

class.haxe_doc: The root class for a 2D scene. All root objects are added to it before being drawn on screen.

friction.haxe_doc: The velocity friction. When not `1`, multiplies velocity by `pow(friction, dt * 60)`.

gravity.haxe_doc: The gravity applied to vertical velocity in pixels per second.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple `BatchElement` that provides primitive simulation of velocity, friction and gravity.
Parent `SpriteBatch` should have `SpriteBatch.hasUpdate` set to `true` in order for BasicElement to work properly.

tile.haxe_doc: The Tile used as a base Texture to draw contents with.

hasRotationScale.haxe_doc:
Enables usage of rotation and scaling of SpriteBatch elements at the cost of extra calculus.
Makes use of `BatchElement.scaleX`, `BatchElement.scaleY` and `BatchElement.rotation`.

hasUpdate.haxe_doc: Enables usage of `update` method in SpriteBatch elements.

clear.haxe_doc:
Removes all elements from the SpriteBatch.
Usage note: Does not clear the `BatchElement.batch` nor `next`/`prev` variables on the child elements.

alloc.haxe_doc: Creates a new BatchElement and returns it. Shortcut to `add(new BatchElement(t))` @param t The Tile element will render.

isEmpty.haxe_doc: Checks if SpriteBatch contains any elements.

getElements.haxe_doc:
Returns an Iterator of all SpriteBatch elements.
Adding or removing the elements will affect the Iterator results.

class.haxe_doc:
An active batched tile renderer.
Compared to `TileGroup` which is expected to be used as a static geometry, SpriteBatch uploads GPU buffer each frame by collecting data from added `BatchElement` instance. Due to that, dynamically removing and adding new geometry is fairly simple.
Usage note: While SpriteBatch allows for multiple unique textures, each texture swap causes a new drawcall, and due to that it's recommended to minimize the amount of used textures per SpriteBatch instance, ideally limiting to only one texture.

Left.haxe_doc: Aligns the text to the left edge.

Right.haxe_doc:
Aligns the text to the right edge.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), right edge is considered the smallest of the two.
Otherwise edge is at the `0` coordinate of the Text instance.
See Text sample for showcase.

Center.haxe_doc:
Centers the text alignment.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), center is calculated from 0 to the smallest of the two.
Otherwise text is centered around `0` coordinate of the Text instance.
See Text sample for showcase.

MultilineRight.haxe_doc:
With respect to Text constraints, aligns the text to the right edge of the longest line width.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), right edge is calculated as the smallest value of the `maxWidth`, constrained width and longest line width (after word-wrap from constraints).
Otherwise uses longest line width as the right edge.
See Text sample for showcase.

MultilineCenter.haxe_doc:
Centers the text with respect to Text constraints with the longest line width.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), center is calculated from the to the smallest value of the `maxWidth`, constrained width and longest line width (after word-wrap from constraints).
Otherwise calculates center from 0 to the longest line width.
See Text sample for showcase.

enum.haxe_doc: `Text` alignment rules.

fromBitmap.haxe_doc: Creates a new Texture from provided BitmapData and returns a Tile representing it.

fromTexture.haxe_doc: Create new Tile from provided Texture instance.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Creates new POT Texture from Pixels and returns a Tile representing it.

dx.haxe_doc: Visual offset of the Tile along the X axis during rendering.

dy.haxe_doc: Visual offset of the Tile along the Y axis during rendering.

x.haxe_doc:
Horizontal position of the Tile on the Texture.
Cannot be modified directly, use `Tile.setPosition` instead.

y.haxe_doc:
Vertical position of the Tile on the Texture.
Cannot be modified directly, use `Tile.setPosition` instead.

width.haxe_doc:
Width of the Tile. Not guaranteed to represent real width of the Tile on texture. (see `Tile.scaleToSize`)
Cannot be modified directly, use `Tile.setSize` instead.

height.haxe_doc:
Height of the Tile. Not guaranteed to represent real height of the Tile on texture. (see `Tile.scaleToSize`)
Cannot be modified directly, use `Tile.setSize` instead.

xFlip.haxe_doc: The flip state of the Tile. @see `Tile.flipX`

yFlip.haxe_doc: The flip state of the Tile. @see `Tile.flipY`

ix.haxe_doc: An integer horizontal position of the Tile on the Texture. Alias to `Math.floor(tile.x)`.

iy.haxe_doc: An integer vertical position of the Tile on the Texture. Alias to `Math.floor(tile.y)`.

iwidth.haxe_doc: An integer width of the Tile. Alias to `Math.ceil(tile.width + tile.x) - tile.ix`.

iheight.haxe_doc: An integer height of the Tile. Alias to `Math.ceil(tile.height + tile.y) - tile.iy`.

isDisposed.haxe_doc: Checks if Tile or underlying Texture were disposed.

switchTexture.haxe_doc:
Changes this Tile underlying texture to one used in the specified Tile.
If Tile was scaled, new uv will cover new width and height instead of the original unscaled one.
@param t The Tile used as a source of the Texture instance.
It's possible to switch texture by referring the Texture instance directly, by using access hacks: ```haxe @:privateAccess tile.setTexture(myTextureInstance); ```

center.haxe_doc:
Returns a new Tile with shifting origin point (`dx` and `dy`) to the tile center.
To modify this Tile origin point, use `Tile.setCenterRatio`.

setCenterRatio.haxe_doc: Sets `dx` / `dy` as origin point dictated by `px` / `py` with a default being center.

flipX.haxe_doc: Flips the Tile horizontally. Note that `dx` is flipped as well.

flipY.haxe_doc: Flips the Tile vertically. Note that `dy` is flipped as well.

setPosition.haxe_doc: Set the Tile position in the texture to the specified coordinate.

setSize.haxe_doc: Set the Tile size in the texture to the specified dimensions.

scaleToSize.haxe_doc:
Rescales the Tile to be of the set width and height, but without affecting the uv coordinates.
Using this method allows to upscale/downscale Tiles, but creates a mismatch between the tile uv and width/height values. Due to that, using any methods that modify the uv value will cause the new uv to treat scaled width and height as true dimensions and can lead to unexpected results if not accounted for.

scrollDiscrete.haxe_doc: Scrolls the texture position by specified amount.

dispose.haxe_doc: Disposes of the Tile and its underlying Texture. Note that if Texture is used by other Tile instances, it will cause them to point at a disposed texture and can lead to errors.

clone.haxe_doc: Create a copy of this Tile instance.

class.haxe_doc:
A core 2D rendering component representing a region of an underlying `h3d.mat.Texture`.
