slice.haxe_doc: For texture arrays: if positive, binds only the layer `slice - 1` as a 2D texture (DirectX 12).

layerCount.haxe_doc: The number of layers: 6 for cube textures, the number of layers of texture arrays, the depth of 3D textures, 1 otherwise.

lodBias.haxe_doc: A bias added to the mip level selected when sampling, from -15 to 16: positive values select less detailed levels.

mipLevels.haxe_doc: The number of mip levels (1 if the texture is not `MipMapped`).

anisotropicMaxLevel.haxe_doc: The maximum level of anisotropic filtering (1 to 16).

startingMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level sampled: levels before it are ignored.

residentMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level allocated on the GPU : mip levels before it are not allocated, and the texture is sampled starting at this level.

isPlaceholder.haxe_doc: A 1x1 texture is allocated while the texture is loading (see hxd.res.Image)

realloc.haxe_doc: If this callback is set, the texture can be re-allocated when the 3D context has been lost or when it's been free because of lack of memory.

depthBuffer.haxe_doc: When the texture is used as render target, tells which depth buffer will be used. If set to null, depth testing is disabled.

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocates the GPU memory of the texture if it is not allocated.

isSRGB.haxe_doc: Tells if the format stores sRGB colors.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a GPU copy of the texture (same size, format and main flags).

preventAutoDispose.haxe_doc: In case we run out of GPU memory, textures that hasn't been used for a long time will be disposed. Calling this will make this texture not considered for auto disposal.

waitLoad.haxe_doc: Some textures might take some time to load. You can check flags.has(Loading) or add a waitLoad callback which will get called either immediately if the texture is already loaded or when loading is complete.

setName.haxe_doc: Sets the texture name, used for debugging.

isDisposed.haxe_doc: Tells if the GPU memory is released and cannot be restored with `realloc`.

resize.haxe_doc: Changes the texture size. The content is lost.

clearF.haxe_doc: Fills a render target with the given float color. @param layer The layer to clear, or `-1` for all layers.

setResidentMip.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the mip levels more detailed than `mip` (texture streaming). Returns `false` if the driver does not support it. Not supported for render targets and depth textures.

uploadBitmap.haxe_doc: Uploads the pixels of a bitmap to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size.

uploadPixels.haxe_doc: Uploads pixels to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size. Uploading the level 0 of the last layer of a `MipMapped` texture generates the mip levels, unless `ManualMipMapGen` is set.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the texture.

hasStencil.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format with a stencil.

isDepth.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format.

getHandle.haxe_doc: Returns the bindless handle of the texture (requires a driver supporting bindless textures).

capturePixels.haxe_doc: Downloads the current texture data from the GPU. Beware, this is a very slow operation that shouldn't be done during rendering.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a 3D texture of `w` x `h` x `d` pixels.

class.haxe_doc: A 3D (volume) texture of `width` x `height` x `depth` pixels.

defaultArrayTexture.haxe_doc: Returns a shared 1x1 texture array with a single dark grey layer, used when a texture array is missing.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a texture array of `layers` layers of `w` x `h` pixels.

class.haxe_doc: A texture array: several 2D textures (layers) of the same size and format, sampled with a layer index in shaders.

texture.haxe_doc: The texture referenced by the handle.

class.haxe_doc: A bindless handle of a texture: an identifier allowing shaders to access the texture without binding it. Requires a driver supporting bindless textures. Created by the driver.

type.haxe_doc: The type of the saved data.

hide.haxe_doc: Extra data saved by the editor.

typedef.haxe_doc: The serialized form of a `GpuParticles` (see `GpuParticles.save`).

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Particles are sorted back-to-front every frame based on their current position.

enum.haxe_doc: How the particles of a `GpuPartGroup` are sorted.

Point.haxe_doc: A single Point, emit in all directions

Cone.haxe_doc: A cone, parametrized with emitAngle and emitDistance

CameraBounds.haxe_doc: Same as VolumeBounds, but in Camera space, not world space.

Disc.haxe_doc: A disc, emit in one direction

enum.haxe_doc: The shape the particles of a `GpuPartGroup` are emitted from.

x.haxe_doc: The current X position (see `updatePos`).

y.haxe_doc: The current Y position.

time.haxe_doc: The time offset of the particle in its life cycle.

life.haxe_doc: The life duration of the particles, in seconds.

initX.haxe_doc: The initial X offset of the quad (size and rotation).

initY.haxe_doc: The initial Y offset of the quad.

deltaX.haxe_doc: The X variation of the quad offset over time (size increase and rotation).

deltaY.haxe_doc: The Y variation of the quad offset over time.

next.haxe_doc: The next particle of the list.

updatePos.haxe_doc: Computes the CPU position at `time` (used for sorting and bounds).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a particle.

class.haxe_doc: The initial state of a particle of a `GpuPartGroup`, computed on the CPU and uploaded once. The particle is then animated on the GPU.

amount.haxe_doc: A multiplier of the number of particles, from `0` to `1`.

emitLoop.haxe_doc: If `true`, particles are emitted again when they die; otherwise each particle lives once.

emitMode.haxe_doc: The shape the particles are emitted from.

emitStartDist.haxe_doc: The minimum distance from the emitter at which particles appear.

emitDist.haxe_doc: The size of the emission area, added to `emitStartDist`.

emitAngle.haxe_doc: The opening of the emission cone, in radians (negative values emit backwards).

emitSync.haxe_doc: How synchronized the particle births are, from `0` (spread over their life) to `1` (all born at once).

emitDelay.haxe_doc: The delay before the first particles appear, in seconds.

emitOnBorder.haxe_doc: Emits on the border of the disc only (`Disc` mode).

clipBounds.haxe_doc: Wraps the particles in the volume bounds (always enabled in `CameraBounds` mode).

transform3D.haxe_doc: Orients the particle quads in 3D instead of facing the camera.

sizeRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the size (fraction of `size`).

life.haxe_doc: The life duration of the particles, in seconds.

lifeRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the life (fraction of `life`).

speedRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the speed (fraction of `speed`).

gravity.haxe_doc: The gravity applied to the particles.

rotInit.haxe_doc: The random initial rotation, as a fraction of a half turn.

rotSpeedRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the rotation speed.

fadeIn.haxe_doc: The fraction of the life during which the particles fade in.

fadeOut.haxe_doc: The fraction of the life after which the particles fade out.

fadePower.haxe_doc: The exponent of the fade curves.

frameCount.haxe_doc: The number of animation frames in the texture (`0` for all the cells).

frameDivisionX.haxe_doc: The number of animation cells horizontally in the texture.

frameDivisionY.haxe_doc: The number of animation cells vertically in the texture.

animationRepeat.haxe_doc: The number of times the animation plays during a particle life (`0` uses a random fixed frame per particle).

colorGradient.haxe_doc: A texture giving the color over the life (horizontally) and per particle (vertically).

isRelative.haxe_doc: If `true`, the particles move with the emitter instead of staying in world space.

attachToCam.haxe_doc: Places the emitter in front of the camera, at `distanceToCam`.

distanceToCam.haxe_doc: The distance from the camera when `attachToCam` is set.

syncParams.haxe_doc: Updates the shader parameters from the settings.

getMaterialProps.haxe_doc: Returns the material properties for the current material setup.

save.haxe_doc: Returns the settings of the group as a serializable object.

load.haxe_doc: Loads the settings of the group saved with the given format version.

updateBounds.haxe_doc: Adds the bounds of the particles to `bounds`.

emitPart.haxe_doc: Computes the initial state of the particle `pt`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a group of the particles `parent`.

class.haxe_doc: A group of GPU particles sharing the same settings and material, part of a `GpuParticles`. Changing most settings rebuilds the particles.

primitive.haxe_doc: The primitive of the mesh: the list of vertexes and indices necessary to display the mesh.

material.haxe_doc: The material of the mesh: the properties used to display it (texture, color, shaders, etc.)

inheritLod.haxe_doc: When enabled, the lod level is inherited by children objects.

blendshapeInstance.haxe_doc: Instance of the blendshape of the mesh: the list of weights for the different shapes

forcedLod.haxe_doc: Allow user to force a specific lod index. If set to -1, forced lod will be ignored.

getMeshMaterials.haxe_doc: Return all materials for the current object.

getLodIndex.haxe_doc: Returns the level of detail currently used to draw this mesh: `forcedLod` if set (not `-1`), otherwise the LOD selected by the primitive from the screen ratio computed during the last frame.

setBlendshapeWeight.haxe_doc: Sets the weight of the blend shape (morph target) `name`. The primitive must be a `h3d.prim.HMDModel` with blend shapes.

setBlendshapeWeights.haxe_doc: Sets the weights of all the blend shapes at once, in the order returned by `getBlenshapeNames`.

getBlenshapeNames.haxe_doc: Returns the names of the blend shapes of the primitive, or an empty array if it has none.

hasBlendshapes.haxe_doc: Tells if the primitive of this mesh has blend shapes (morph targets).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new mesh with given primitive, material and parent object. If material is not specified, a new default material is created for the current renderer.

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.Mesh is the base class for all 3D objects displayed on screen. Unlike Object base class, all properties of Mesh only apply to the current object and are not inherited by its children.

materials.haxe_doc: The materials, indexed by primitive material group. `null` entries are not drawn. `Mesh.material` refers to the first one.

class.haxe_doc:
A `Mesh` using several materials, one per material group of its primitive.
The primitive must split its indexes per material (for instance a `h3d.prim.HMDModel` loaded from a model with several materials): each material `i` is drawn with the indexes of group `i`.

XY_UV_RGBA.haxe_doc: 2D position, UV and color: the format of `h2d` vertices.

fromID.haxe_doc: Returns the format with the given `uid`, or `null`.

make.haxe_doc: Returns the unique format for the list of inputs, creating it if needed.

float32to16.haxe_doc: Converts a float to the bits of a 16 bits float.

float16to32.haxe_doc: Converts the bits of a 16 bits float to a float.

float32toS8.haxe_doc: Converts a float in the `[-1, 1]` range to a signed 8 bits value.

floatS8to32.haxe_doc: Converts a signed 8 bits value to a float in the `[-1, 1]` range.

float32toU8.haxe_doc: Converts a float in the `[0, 1]` range to an unsigned 8 bits value.

floatU8to32.haxe_doc: Converts an unsigned 8 bits value to a float in the `[0, 1]` range.

uid.haxe_doc: The unique identifier of the format.

stride.haxe_doc: The number of 32 bits components of a vertex, ignoring the precision.

strideBytes.haxe_doc: The size of a vertex in bytes.

hasLowPrecision.haxe_doc: Tells if an input has a precision lower than `F32`.

getInput.haxe_doc: Returns the input of the given name, or `null`.

getCompressed.haxe_doc: Returns a format with lower precisions for the known inputs (data, color, position, normal and uv), raising some of them back to fill the alignment padding.

calculateInputOffset.haxe_doc: Returns the offset in bytes of the input in a vertex. Throws if it is not found.

hasInput.haxe_doc: Tells if the format has an input of the given name, and of the given type if set.

append.haxe_doc: Returns the format with an input added at the end.

pop.haxe_doc: Returns the format without its last input.

isSubSet.haxe_doc: Tells if the inputs of this format are the first inputs of `fmt`.

resolveMapping.haxe_doc: Returns where to find each input of `target` in this format. Throws if one is missing.

getInputs.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator on the inputs.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a description of the inputs.

class.haxe_doc: The vertex layout of a `h3d.Buffer`: the list of its inputs. Formats are unique: use `BufferFormat.make` to get the format for a list of inputs, or one of the predefined formats. Each input is aligned to 4 bytes.

U8.haxe_doc: Unsigned 8 bits, normalized to the `[0, 1]` range.

S8.haxe_doc: Signed 8 bits, normalized to the `[-1, 1]` range.

getSize.haxe_doc: Returns the size in bytes of a component.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the integer value of the precision.

fromInt.haxe_doc: Returns the precision of the given integer value.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the name of the precision.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the input, matching the shader input name (such as `"position"`).

precision.haxe_doc: The storage precision of the input.

getBytesSize.haxe_doc: Returns the size of the input in bytes (without alignment).

equals.haxe_doc: Tells if the input has the same name, type and precision as `b`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an input.

class.haxe_doc: An input (vertex attribute) of a `BufferFormat`: its name, type and precision.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a texture coordinate.

class.haxe_doc: A texture coordinate, used by `Polygon`.

PFORMAT.expr: hxd.BufferFormat.make([{ name : "position", type : DVec3 }, { name : "normal", type : DVec3 }, { name : "uv", type : DVec2 }, { name : "time", type : DFloat }, { name : "life", type : DFloat }, { name : "init", type : DVec2 }, { name : "delta", type : DVec2 }])

m.e: hxd.BufferFormat.make([{ name : "position", type : DVec3 }, { name : "normal", type : DVec3 }, { name : "uv", type : DVec2 }, { name : "time", type : DFloat }, { name : "life", type : DFloat }, { name : "init", type : DVec2 }, { name : "delta", type : DVec2 }])

seed.haxe_doc: The random seed of the particles.

volumeBounds.haxe_doc: The emission volume in `VolumeBounds` and `CameraBounds` modes.

currentTime.haxe_doc: The current time of the particle system, in seconds.

duration.haxe_doc: The duration of the effect, in seconds, computed from the groups (`0` if a group loops).

bounds.haxe_doc: The bounds of the particles, used for culling.

amount.haxe_doc: Tells how much percent of the particles to display. This can be used to progressively display a particle effect. This can also be done per group in GpuPartGroup.progress

uploadedCount.haxe_doc: Tells how many particles were uploaded to GPU last frame (for performance tuning).

count.haxe_doc: Tells how many particles are live actually

onEnd.haxe_doc: Called when `currentTime` reaches `duration`. By default restarts the effect.

save.haxe_doc: Returns the settings of all the groups as a serializable object.

load.haxe_doc: Loads the groups from saved settings.

getGroups.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator on the groups.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty particle system.

class.haxe_doc: A particle system animated on the GPU: the initial state of each particle is computed once, then the shader computes its position, size and color over time. Supports very large numbers of particles. Made of one or several `GpuPartGroup`. Usually edited in Hide and loaded with `load`.

run.haxe_doc: Renders a screen shader to `output` with a temporary pass.

pass.haxe_doc: The material pass holding the render states (no culling, no depth test by default) and the shaders.

primitive.haxe_doc: The primitive drawn, the full screen quad by default.

addShader.haxe_doc: Adds a shader to the pass.

removeShader.haxe_doc: Removes a shader from the pass.

getShader.haxe_doc: Returns the first shader of class `cl`, or `null`.

render.haxe_doc: Renders the full screen quad to the current target.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the resources of the pass.

radius.haxe_doc: How far in pixels the blur will go.

gain.haxe_doc: How much the blur increases or decreases the color amount (default = 1)

linear.haxe_doc: Set linear blur instead of gaussian (default = 0).

quality.haxe_doc: Adjust how much quality/speed tradeoff we want (default = 1)

additive.haxe_doc: If `true`, the blurred result is added to the output instead of replacing it.

getKernelSize.haxe_doc: Returns the number of samples of each pass.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a blur. See `radius`, `gain`, `linear` and `quality`.

class.haxe_doc:
A separable blur: a horizontal then a vertical pass, gaussian by default. Works with 2D and cube textures.
```haxe var blur = new h3d.pass.Blur(5); blur.apply(ctx, texture); // blurs texture in place ```

onShaderError.haxe_doc: If set, called when the driver fails to select the shader of an object (instead of throwing the error); the object is then skipped.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the pass, matching the material pass names it draws (such as `"default"` or `"shadow"`).

setContext.haxe_doc: Sets the render context used by the next `draw`. Done by the renderer.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the resources of the pass.

draw.haxe_doc: Draws the object passes to the current target. @param sort A function sorting the passes before drawing them (by material by default).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a pass. @param output The values written to the render targets (`output.color` by default).

class.haxe_doc: A render pass of a renderer: draws a list of object passes (`PassList`) to the current render target, linking each object shaders with the output shader of the pass (which writes the given values, such as `output.color`, to the targets).

enabled.haxe_doc: Enables the shadows of the light.

mode.haxe_doc: How the shadows are computed (`None` by default). Not all lights support all modes.

size.haxe_doc: The size of the shadow map texture, in pixels.

shader.haxe_doc: The shader applying the shadows to the lit objects.

blur.haxe_doc: The blur applied to the shadow map (used by soft shadow techniques).

samplingKind.haxe_doc: How the shadow map is sampled.

power.haxe_doc: The sharpness of the exponential shadows (`ESM`).

bias.haxe_doc: The depth bias subtracted when comparing depths, to avoid shadow acne.

pcfScale.haxe_doc: The radius of the `PCF` sampling, in pixels.

getShadowView.haxe_doc: Returns the view matrix of the shadow camera.

getShadowProj.haxe_doc: Returns the projection matrix of the shadow camera.

getShadowViewProj.haxe_doc: Returns the view-projection matrix of the shadow camera.

getShadowTex.haxe_doc: Returns the shadow map texture of the last frame.

loadStaticData.haxe_doc: Loads baked static shadow data. Returns `false` if not supported or invalid.

saveStaticData.haxe_doc: Returns the static shadow data to bake, or `null`.

computeStatic.haxe_doc: Renders the static shadows with the given shadow casters.

hasStaticShadow.haxe_doc: Tells if the mode uses static shadows (`Static` or `Mixed`).

needStaticUpdate.haxe_doc: * Triggers update of static part of shadows (if any).

new.haxe_doc: Creates the shadow map of `light`.
Creates the shadow map of `light`.

class.haxe_doc: Base class of the omnidirectional shadow maps: the shadows are rendered in the 6 faces of a cube texture around the light.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the shadow map of `light`.

class.haxe_doc: The shadow map of a `h3d.scene.pbr.CapsuleLight`: a cube shadow map rendered from the light center.

slopeBias.haxe_doc: The slope scaled depth bias of the cascade.

depthBias.haxe_doc: The constant depth bias multiplier of the cascade.

typedef.haxe_doc: The depth bias settings of a cascade.

scale.haxe_doc: The scale from the shared shadow space to the cascade (W stores the far distance of the cascade).

orthoBounds.haxe_doc: The orthographic bounds of the cascade.

offset.haxe_doc: The offset from the shared shadow space to the cascade.

typedef.haxe_doc: The shadow camera of a cascade.

cascadeViewProj.haxe_doc: The view-projection matrix shared by the cascades.

params.haxe_doc: The depth bias settings of each cascade.

distributionPower.haxe_doc: How the distances of the cascades after the first one are distributed: `1` is linear, higher values give more resolution to the near cascades.

minPixelSize.haxe_doc: The minimum size, in shadow map pixels, of an object to be drawn in the cascades after the first one.

firstCascadeSize.haxe_doc: The distance from the camera covered by the first cascade.

castingMaxDist.haxe_doc: If positive, how far beyond the cascade bounds (towards the light) shadow casters are drawn. Otherwise `maxDist` or the camera far plane is used.

transitionFraction.haxe_doc: The fraction of each cascade blended with the next one, to hide the transitions (`0` to disable).

highPrecision.haxe_doc: Uses a 32-bit depth buffer instead of a 16-bit one when rendering the cascades.

maxDist.haxe_doc: Clamp the zFar of the frustum of the camera for bounds calculation

calcCascadeMatrices.haxe_doc: Computes the shadow camera of each cascade from the current camera.

getCascadeView.haxe_doc: Returns the view matrix of the cascade `i`.

getCascadeProj.haxe_doc: Returns the projection matrix of the cascade `i`.

getCascadeViewProj.haxe_doc: Returns the view-projection matrix of the cascade `i`.

getCascadeOffset.haxe_doc: Returns the offset from the shared shadow space to the cascade `i`.

getCascadeScale.haxe_doc: Returns the scale from the shared shadow space to the cascade `i`.

customCullPasses.haxe_doc: Removes from `passes` the shadow casters which do not need to be drawn in the cascade `i`: by default, the objects smaller than `minSize` in the cascades after the first one. Can be replaced for custom culling.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the cascaded shadow map of `light`.

class.haxe_doc:
Cascaded shadow maps of a directional light: the view frustum is split in `cascade` ranges of distance, each with its own shadow map, so that near shadows get more resolution than far ones. Used by `h3d.scene.pbr.DirLight` with `cascade = true`.
The first cascade covers `firstCascadeSize` units from the camera, the others share the remaining distance up to `maxDist` (or the camera far plane), distributed by `distributionPower`.
Base class of the full screen shaders used with `h3d.pass.ScreenFx`: it provides the `calculatedUV` of each pixel of the screen quad. Extend it and write a `fragment` function.

dispose.haxe_doc: See `h3d.impl.RendererFX.dispose`.

Screen space reflections for the PBR renderer: reflections are found by marching rays in the depth buffer, after the forward passes. Add it to the renderer effects:
```haxe s3d.renderer.effects.push(new h3d.pass.SSR()); ```

Dynamic.haxe_doc: The shadows are rendered every frame.

abstract.haxe_doc: How the shadow map is sampled when drawing the lit objects.

begin.haxe_doc: Call begin() before starting to add vertexes/indexes to the primitive. The count value is the number of vertexes you will add, it will automatically flush() if it doesn't fit into the current buffer.

clear.haxe_doc: Removes all the geometry.

addSub.haxe_doc: Adds a buffer to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation. The buffer can have more stride than the BigPrimitive, but not less. It is assumed that the buffer contains [X,Y,Z,NX,NY,NZ,U,V,R,G,B] (depending on his stride) so the different offsets are applied to the corresponding components. If hasTangent=true, we have [TX,TY,TZ] just after normal. However if the stride is 5, we assume [X,Y,Z,U,V] If mat is not null, it overrides dx, dy, dz, rotation, scale

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the mouse/keyboard camera controllers. Add a controller to the scene to drive `Scene.camera`: it listens to the scene events and moves the camera smoothly towards the wanted position every frame.
The camera position is expressed in spherical coordinates around `target`: `distance`, `theta` (horizontal angle) and `phi` (vertical angle, from the Z axis). Use `set` to change them and `loadFromCamera` to start from the current camera. See `OrbitCameraController` and `FPSCameraController`.

zNear.haxe_doc: The camera near plane distance, applied every frame.

zFar.haxe_doc: The camera far plane distance, applied every frame.

class.haxe_doc:
A `MeshBatch` using GPU driven rendering: the level of detail selection and the frustum culling of each instance can be computed by a compute shader (see `enableGpuLod` and `enableGpuCulling`), and the instances are drawn with indirect draw calls.
Requires compute shaders and indirect draws: not available on JavaScript and DirectX 11 (`hldx` without `dx12`).

setupDebugMaterial.haxe_doc: Sets up the materials of the debug object displayed by `showDebug`: semi transparent, without shadows, and in wireframe when the driver supports it. Can be replaced to customize the debug display.

shape.haxe_doc: The collision shape tested against the mouse ray, relative to this interactive transform (or in world space if `isAbsoluteShape` is set).

preciseShape.haxe_doc: If several interactive conflicts, the preciseShape (if defined) can be used to distinguish between the two.

priority.haxe_doc: In case of conflicting shapes, usually the one in front of the camera is prioritized, unless you set an higher priority.

cursor.haxe_doc: Cursor used when the Interactive is under the mouse cursor (`Button` by default).

cancelEvents.haxe_doc: Set the default `cancel` mode (see `hxd.Event`), default to false.

propagateEvents.haxe_doc: Set the default `propagate` mode (see `hxd.Event`), default to false.

enableRightButton.haxe_doc: When enabled, interacting with secondary mouse buttons (right button/wheel) will cause `onPush`, `onClick`, `onRelease` and `onReleaseOutside` callbacks. Otherwise those callbacks will only be triggered with primary mouse button (left button).

allowMultiClick.haxe_doc: When enabled, allows to receive several onClick events the same frame.

bestMatch.haxe_doc: Is it required to find the best hit point in a complex mesh or any hit possible point will be enough (default = false, faster).

showDebug.haxe_doc: When set, will display the debug object of the shape (using makeDebugObj)

isAbsoluteShape.haxe_doc: * Tells if our shapes are in absolute space (for example ObjectCollider) or relative to the interactive transform.

emittedLastFrame.haxe_doc: Set to `true` when the interactive was emitted (visible and not culled) during the last rendered frame.

getPoint.haxe_doc: Returns the world position where `ray` (in world space) hits the shape, or `null` if it does not hit it. @param bestMatch If `true`, finds the nearest hit point on complex shapes instead of any hit point (slower).

preventClick.haxe_doc: This can be called during or after a push event in order to prevent the release from triggering a click.

focus.haxe_doc: Sets focus on this `Interactive`. If Interactive was not already focused and it receives focus - `onFocus` event is sent. Interactive won't become focused if during `onFocus` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes focus from interactive if it's focused. If Interactive is currently focused - `onFocusLost` event will be sent. Interactive won't lose focus if during `onFocusLost` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

isOver.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently hovered by the mouse.

hasFocus.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently focused.

onOver.haxe_doc: Sent when mouse enters Interactive hitbox area. `event.propagate` and `event.cancel` are ignored during `onOver`. Propagation can be set with `onMove` event, as well as cancelling `onMove` will prevent `onOver`.

onOut.haxe_doc: Sent when mouse exits Interactive hitbox area. `event.propagate` and `event.cancel` are ignored during `onOut`.

onPush.haxe_doc: Sent when Interactive is pressed by user.

onRelease.haxe_doc: Sent on multiple conditions. A. Always sent if user releases mouse while it is inside Interactive hitbox area. This happends regardless if that Interactive was pressed prior or not. B. Sent before `onReleaseOutside` if this Interactive was pressed, but released outside it's bounds. For first case `event.kind` will be `ERelease`, for second case - `EReleaseOutside`. See `onClick` and `onReleaseOutside` functions for separate events that trigger only when user interacts with this particular Interactive.

onReleaseOutside.haxe_doc: Sent when user presses Interactive, moves mouse outside and releases it. This event fired only on Interactive that user pressed, but released mouse after moving it outside of Interactive hitbox area.

onClick.haxe_doc: Sent when Interactive is clicked by user. This event fired only on Interactive that user pressed and released when mouse is inside Interactive hitbox area.

onMove.haxe_doc:
Sent when user moves within the Interactive hitbox area. See `Interactive.onCheck` for event when user does not move the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onWheel.haxe_doc: Sent when user scrolls mouse wheel above the Interactive. Wheel delta can be obtained through the `Event.wheelDelta`.

onFocus.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive receives focus during `Interactive.focus` call.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from becoming focused.

onFocusLost.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive lost focus either via `Interactive.blur` call or when user clicks on another Interactive/outside this Interactive hitbox area.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from losing focus.

onKeyUp.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user unpressed a keyboard key. Unpressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onKeyDown.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user pressed a keyboard key. Pressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onCheck.haxe_doc:
Sent every frame when user hovers an Interactive but does not move the mouse. See `Interactive.onMove` for event when user moves the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onTextInput.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user inputs text. Character added can be accessed through `Event.charCode`.

class.haxe_doc:
A 3D object receiving mouse, touch and keyboard events through a collision shape.
The `Scene` casts a ray from the cursor through the camera and sends the events to the interactives whose `shape` is hit, nearest first (see `Scene.rayCastEventTargets` and `priority`).
The shape is expressed in the interactive local space. `Object.getCollider()` returns a world space snapshot of an object shape, so such an interactive is added at the scene root (it will not follow the object if it moves). To follow a moving object, add the interactive as its child with a shape in the object local space (for instance a `h3d.col.Sphere` or `h3d.col.Bounds`), or keep it at the scene root with a `h3d.col.ObjectCollider(obj, localShape)`, which applies the current object transform to its shape.
```haxe var mesh = new h3d.scene.Mesh(prim, s3d); var i = new h3d.scene.Interactive(mesh.getCollider(), s3d); // world space shape, at the scene root i.onClick = function(e) trace("clicked at local position " + e.relX + "," + e.relY + "," + e.relZ); ```

color.haxe_doc: The color of the light. The base implementation returns a new zero vector and ignores assignments: subclasses map it to their shader parameter.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class for all 3D lights.
A light is a regular scene `Object`: it is positioned and oriented through its transform and emits itself to the `RenderContext` at render time so that the renderer's `LightSystem` can apply it to the lit objects. Do not instantiate it directly: use the implementations of the active renderer, such as `h3d.scene.fwd.PointLight` / `h3d.scene.fwd.DirLight` (forward renderer) or `h3d.scene.pbr.PointLight` / `h3d.scene.pbr.SpotLight` / `h3d.scene.pbr.DirLight` (PBR renderer).

drawPasses.haxe_doc: Number of additional draw passes performed by the light system during the last frame (used for statistics).

shadowLight.haxe_doc: The light used to cast the main shadow. If `null` (or disposed), `initLights` selects the first light which returns a non-null `Light.getShadowDirection`.

initGlobals.haxe_doc: Called by the renderer to declare the shader globals required by this light system.

initLights.haxe_doc: Called once per frame by the renderer before drawing, with the list of lights emitted in `ctx.lights`. Selects the `shadowLight` if needed.

computeLight.haxe_doc: Returns the shader list used to draw `obj`, with the light shaders affecting it prepended. The base implementation returns `shaders` unchanged.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU resources allocated by this light system.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty light system.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the lighting setup used by a `Renderer`.
Every frame, the renderer calls `initLights` with the lights emitted during the scene sync, then `computeLight` for each drawn object to add the light shaders it needs. This base implementation does no lighting: see `h3d.scene.fwd.LightSystem` and `h3d.scene.pbr.LightSystem`.

EnableResizeDown.haxe_doc: Shrinks the instance buffers when much fewer instances are emitted.

EnableGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: The per instance parameters can be written by compute shaders. See `MeshBatch.enableGpuUpdate`.

EnableStorageBuffer.haxe_doc: The per instance parameters are stored in a storage buffer. See `MeshBatch.enableStorageBuffer`.

HasPrimitiveOffset.haxe_doc: Internal: instances store an offset in the primitive (used with sub meshes).

EnableCpuLod.haxe_doc: The level of detail is chosen per instance on the CPU. See `MeshBatch.enableCpuLod`.

ForceGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: The per instance parameters are only written by compute shaders. See `MeshBatch.forceGpuUpdate`.

EnableSubMesh.haxe_doc: Instances draw parts of the primitive. See `MeshBatch.enableSubMesh`.

EnablePerInstanceTexture.haxe_doc: Instances can use different textures (bindless). See `MeshBatch.enablePerInstanceTexture`.

enum.haxe_doc: Options of a `MeshBatch`, set with its `enable*` methods.

typedef.haxe_doc: The indirect draw commands of one material, built on the CPU when using sub meshes.

paramsCount.haxe_doc: The number of 4-floats vectors of parameters per instance.

maxInstance.haxe_doc: The maximum number of instances per buffer.

matIndex.haxe_doc: The index of the material of the batch this pass belongs to.

indirectCallBuffers.haxe_doc: The indirect draw commands, one per buffer.

buffers.haxe_doc: The GPU buffers storing the per instance parameters.

bufferFormat.haxe_doc: The format of the per instance data.

textureHandles.haxe_doc: The bindless texture handles used by the instances (with `enablePerInstanceTexture`).

data.haxe_doc: The per instance parameters filled on the CPU before upload.

params.haxe_doc: The shader parameters copied for each instance.

shader.haxe_doc: The generated shader reading the per instance parameters.

shaders.haxe_doc: The shaders whose parameters are stored per instance.

next.haxe_doc: The next pass in the list.

clean.haxe_doc: Releases the buffers and removes the generated shader from the pass.

new.haxe_doc: Creates empty pass data.

class.haxe_doc: The instance data of one material pass of a `MeshBatch`.

subParts.haxe_doc: The index ranges of the sub mesh, one per material.

bounds.haxe_doc: The local bounds of the sub mesh.

lodCount.haxe_doc: The number of levels of detail of the sub mesh.

lodConfig.haxe_doc: The screen ratios at which each level of detail is selected.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty sub mesh.

class.haxe_doc: A part of the primitive of a `MeshBatch` which can be drawn by an instance (see `MeshBatch.primitiveSubMeshes`).

indexStart.haxe_doc: The first index of the range.

indexCount.haxe_doc: The number of indexes of the range.

lodIndexStart.haxe_doc: The first index of the range for each level of detail.

lodIndexCount.haxe_doc: The number of indexes of the range for each level of detail.

matIndex.haxe_doc: The index of the material drawing this range.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty index range.

class.haxe_doc: An index range of the primitive, for one material and its levels of detail.

abstract.haxe_doc: Bit flags storing the boolean state of an `Object`. Most of them are exposed as properties of `Object` (for instance `FVisible` is `Object.visible`): prefer using these properties.

FPosChanged.haxe_doc: The transform changed and `absPos` must be recomputed. See `Object.posChanged`.

FAllocated.haxe_doc: The object is part of an allocated scene. See `Object.allocated`.

FFixedPositionSynced.haxe_doc: Internal: the absolute position of a `fixedPosition` object has been computed once.

FInSync.haxe_doc: Internal: the object is currently running its `sync`.

FPosChangedInSync.haxe_doc: Internal: the transform was modified during `sync`, so `absPos` must be recomputed right after it.

_new.haxe_doc: Creates flags from their integer value.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the integer value of the flags.

has.haxe_doc: Tells if the flag `f` is set.

set.haxe_doc: Sets or clears the flag `f` and returns `b`.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the list of the flags set, separated by ` | `.

FPosChanged.haxe_doc: The transform changed and `absPos` must be recomputed. See `Object.posChanged`.

FAllocated.haxe_doc: The object is part of an allocated scene. See `Object.allocated`.

FFixedPositionSynced.haxe_doc: Internal: the absolute position of a `fixedPosition` object has been computed once.

FInSync.haxe_doc: Internal: the object is currently running its `sync`.

FPosChangedInSync.haxe_doc: Internal: the transform was modified during `sync`, so `absPos` must be recomputed right after it.

_new.haxe_doc: Creates flags from their integer value.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the integer value of the flags.

has.haxe_doc: Tells if the flag `f` is set.

set.haxe_doc: Sets or clears the flag `f` and returns `b`.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the list of the flags set, separated by ` | `.

frustum.haxe_doc: The frustum used to cull the objects of this view.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a view with the given index.

class.haxe_doc: A rendering view: the frustum used to cull objects for the current view (see `RenderContext.currentView`). Renderers drawing several views (for instance shadow cascades) change it temporarily.

camera.haxe_doc: The camera used for the current frame: a copy of `Scene.camera` made in `start`. Use `setCamera` to change it.

drawPass.haxe_doc: The pass currently being drawn, set by the render passes before calling `Object.draw`.

pbrLightPass.haxe_doc: The material pass used by the PBR lights to emit their light volumes. Set by `h3d.scene.pbr.Renderer`.

computingStatic.haxe_doc: `true` while computing static data, such as static shadow maps (see `Scene.computeStatic`).

computeVelocity.haxe_doc: When set, objects keep their previous frame transform so that a velocity buffer can be rendered (used by temporal effects such as TAA or motion blur). Reset to `false` at the end of each frame.

enableTranslucency.haxe_doc: Enables the translucency output of the PBR renderer (an additional G-buffer texture used by translucent materials).

useReverseDepth.haxe_doc: Uses a reversed depth buffer (1 near, 0 far), which improves depth precision. Applied to the camera in `setCamera`.

renderResolutionWidth.haxe_doc: The width of the rendering, in pixels. Set to the engine width in `start`, see `setRenderResolution`.

renderResolutionHeight.haxe_doc: The height of the rendering, in pixels. Set to the engine height in `start`, see `setRenderResolution`.

lightSystem.haxe_doc: The light system of the scene, used by the render passes to add the light shaders.

extraShaders.haxe_doc: Shaders added to every object drawn by the render passes, in addition to their material shaders.

visibleFlag.haxe_doc: `false` while syncing the children of an invisible or culled object. Objects use it to skip work, such as updating animations, unless `Object.alwaysSyncAnimation` is set.

debugCulling.haxe_doc: Debug flag set by `h3d.impl.Benchmark`. It is not read by Heaps itself and can be used by custom objects to display culling information.

wasContextLost.haxe_doc: `true` during the first frame rendered after the GPU context was lost and restored (see `Scene.onContextLost`).

cullingCollider.haxe_doc: The culling collider inherited from the parent objects during sync (see `Object.cullingCollider`).

forcedScreenRatio.haxe_doc: If not negative, the screen ratio used by meshes to select their level of detail instead of computing it. Set by a `Mesh` with `inheritLod` so that its children use the same level of detail. Reset at the beginning of each frame.

meshLodScale.haxe_doc: A multiplier applied to the screen ratio of meshes when selecting their level of detail: lower values select lower details sooner.

hzb.haxe_doc: The hierarchical depth buffer (HZB) built by the PBR renderer, used for GPU occlusion culling.

numViews.haxe_doc: The number of views rendered in the current frame. Reset to 1 in `start`.

currentView.haxe_doc: The view currently rendered. Its frustum is the camera frustum, unless a pass renders from another view.

prevCamera.haxe_doc: The camera of the previous frame, used to compute velocities.

prevWorldDelta.haxe_doc: If set, the world origin offset between the previous and current frame, used by temporal effects when the world is rebased. Reset at the end of each frame.

setCamera.haxe_doc: Copies `cam` into `camera` and updates the camera shader globals. The previous camera is kept in `prevCamera`.

setRenderResolution.haxe_doc: Sets the rendering resolution and the `global.pixelSize` shader global.

updateNumViews.haxe_doc: Sets the number of views rendered in the current frame.

setCurrentView.haxe_doc: Sets the view currently rendered and its culling frustum.

setupTarget.haxe_doc: Updates the `camera.projFlip` global according to the current render target: needed on drivers using bottom-left texture coordinates when rendering to a texture.

start.haxe_doc: Starts a new frame: resets the emitted passes and lights, advances `time` and `frame`, and copies the scene camera. Called by `Scene.render`.

nextPass.haxe_doc: Resets the shader list cache before rendering the next pass.

getGlobal.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the shader global `name` (for instance `"global.time"`).

setGlobal.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the shader global `name`.

emitPass.haxe_doc: Emits a single material pass for object `obj` and returns the allocated pass object.

allocShaderList.haxe_doc: Returns a shader list node from the frame cache (to avoid allocations), holding `s` followed by `next`.

computeList.haxe_doc: Sets the list of compute shaders to run with the next `computeDispatch` called without shader.

memoryBarrier.haxe_doc: Inserts a GPU memory barrier, so that the writes of the previous compute dispatches are visible to the next ones.

emitLight.haxe_doc: Adds a light to the lights of the current frame. Called by `Light.emit`.

getCameraFrustumBuffer.haxe_doc: Returns a GPU buffer containing the 6 planes of the camera frustum (left, right, top, bottom, far, near), uploaded once per frame. Used for GPU culling.

getDepthClearValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value to clear the depth buffer with: `0` with reverse depth, `1` otherwise.

selectTextureHandles.haxe_doc: Binds bindless texture handles for the next draws (requires a driver supporting them).

selectBufferHandles.haxe_doc: Binds bindless buffer handles for the next draws (requires a driver supporting them).

uploadParams.haxe_doc: Uploads the shader parameters of the current `drawPass`. Call it after changing shader parameters inside `Object.draw`.

done.haxe_doc: Ends the frame: recycles the emitted passes and stores the camera matrices for the next frame. Called by `Scene.render`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the render context of a scene. Done by the `Scene` itself.

class.haxe_doc:
The per-frame state of a 3D `Scene` rendering, shared by the scene objects, the `Renderer` and the render passes.
Each frame, `Scene.render` calls `start`, syncs the objects (which `emit` the passes of their materials and their lights), hands the emitted passes to the renderer and calls `done`. It also holds the shader globals (`camera.*`, `global.*`), which can be read and changed with `getGlobal` and `setGlobal`. Accessible from objects in `Object.sync`, `Object.emit` and `Object.draw`, and from the scene as `s3d.ctx`.

passes.haxe_doc: The object passes to draw for this pass name.

rendered.haxe_doc: Set to `true` when the renderer retrieved these passes. In debug builds, the scene traces a warning for passes left unrendered (see `Scene.checkPasses`).

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty pass list.

class.haxe_doc: The list of draw passes emitted for one pass name (such as `"default"`, `"alpha"` or `"shadow"`) during a frame, handed to the `Renderer` by the `Scene`.

LightProbe.haxe_doc: Rendering for light probe baking: only diffuse lighting is computed and the environment is used as sky.

enum.haxe_doc: The rendering mode of a `Renderer`.

effects.haxe_doc: The renderer effects (post processes and render hooks) applied in order during the frame. See `h3d.impl.RendererFX`.

renderMode.haxe_doc: The rendering mode. `LightProbe` is used while baking light probes: the PBR renderer then only renders the diffuse lighting and uses the environment map as sky.

shadows.haxe_doc: Enables shadow casting. When `false`, the shadow passes are not drawn.

getEffect.haxe_doc: Returns the first effect of `effects` which is an instance of `cl`, or `null` if there is none.

dispose.haxe_doc: Disposes the render passes, effects and light system resources of this renderer.

addShader.haxe_doc: Inject a post process shader for the current frame. Shaders are reset after each render.

getPass.haxe_doc: Returns the first render pass which is an instance of `c`, or `null` if there is none.

getPassByName.haxe_doc: Returns the render pass named `name`, or `null` if there is none.

start.haxe_doc: Called by the `Scene` at the beginning of the frame, before objects are synchronized and emitted.

startEffects.haxe_doc: Calls `RendererFX.start` on each enabled effect. Called by the `Scene` right after `start`.

process.haxe_doc: Renders the frame from the draw passes emitted by the scene objects. Called by `Scene.render`. Calls `computeStatic` instead of `render` when `RenderContext.computingStatic` is set (see `Scene.computeStatic`).

computeDispatch.haxe_doc: Dispatches a compute shader with the given number of work groups. Requires a driver supporting compute shaders.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the renderer and initializes its properties with `getDefaultProps()`.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the scene renderers.
Each frame, the `Scene` syncs its objects, sorts the emitted draw passes by pass name into `PassObjects` and calls `process`. The renderer then decides in which order and to which render targets each pass name is drawn, and applies the post-processing `effects`. This class only provides the helpers: the concrete renderers are `h3d.scene.fwd.Renderer` (forward, the default) and `h3d.scene.pbr.Renderer` (physically based). The active renderer is created by `h3d.mat.MaterialSetup.current`.

lightSystem.haxe_doc: The scene light system. Can be customized.

renderer.haxe_doc: The scene renderer. Can be customized.

scenePosition.haxe_doc: The scene position. Mainly used for subscenes that aren't fullscreen.

interactiveOffset.haxe_doc: Adjust the position of the ray used to handle interactives.

addEventListener.haxe_doc: Add an event listener that will capture all events not caught by an h2d.Interactive

removeEventListener.haxe_doc: Remove a previously added event listener, return false it was not part of our event listeners.

syncEventTargets.haxe_doc: Updates the physics shapes of the interactives (only with `-D hlphysics`, otherwise does nothing). Called automatically before ray casts, at most once per frame.

rayCastEventTargets.haxe_doc: Returns the visible interactives hit by the ray `r` (in world space), sorted from the nearest to the farthest. Only the interactives with the highest `Interactive.priority` among the hits are returned. `Interactive.hitPoint` is updated with the local hit position; `distance` is the distance from the camera.

dispose.haxe_doc: Free the GPU memory for this Scene and its children

setElapsedTime.haxe_doc: Before render() or sync() are called, allow to set how much time has elapsed (in seconds) since the last frame in order to update scene animations. This is managed automatically by hxd.App

syncOnly.haxe_doc: Synchronize the scene without rendering, updating all objects and animations by the given amount of time, in seconds.

computeStatic.haxe_doc: Perform a rendering with `RendererContext.computingStatic=true`, allowing the computation of static shadow maps, etc.

onContextLost.haxe_doc: Automatically called when the 3D context is lost

render.haxe_doc: Render the scene on screen. Internal usage only.

mark.haxe_doc: Called during rendering at the beginning of each named step (forwards to the renderer). Can be overridden for profiling.

setOutputTarget.haxe_doc: Temporarily overrides the output render target. This is useful for picture-in-picture rendering, where the output render target has a different size from the window. `tex` must have a matching depthBuffer attached. Call `setOutputTarget()` after `render()` has been called.

getRenderCamera.haxe_doc: Returns the camera of the render context: a copy of `camera` made at the start of each frame, with the render settings applied (such as reverse depth).

new.haxe_doc: Create a new scene. A default 3D scene is already available in `hxd.App.s3d`

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.Scene is the root class for a 3D scene. All root objects are added to it before being drawn on screen.

skin.haxe_doc: The skin this joint belongs to.

index.haxe_doc: The index of the joint in `h3d.anim.Skin.allJoints`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an object following the joint `j` of `skin`.

class.haxe_doc:
A temporary object representing a joint (bone) of a `Skin`, returned by `Skin.getObjectByName`.
Its absolute position follows the joint, which allows attaching objects to bones or reading their position. It is not part of the scene tree: it is recreated by each `getObjectByName` call.

currentRelPos.haxe_doc: The current transform of the joint relative to its parent, written by animations. `null` uses the default pose.

currentAbsPos.haxe_doc: The absolute transform of the joint computed during the last joints sync.

additivePose.haxe_doc: An optional transform applied on top of the animated pose (see `Skin.setJointRelPosition` with `additive`).

sync.haxe_doc: Computes the absolute transform of the joint and its skinning matrix. @param syncDyn `true` when a dynamic joint simulation step must be performed.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the state of a joint.

class.haxe_doc: The runtime state of a joint of a `Skin` (one per joint of the skin data).

curTargetWorld.haxe_doc: The current simulated world transform of the joint.

initData.haxe_doc: Initializes the simulation from the current joint position.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the state of a dynamic joint.

class.haxe_doc: The runtime state of a dynamic joint (`h3d.anim.Skin.DynamicJoint`): a joint simulated as a spring following its animated position, for hair, cloth or other secondary motion. The simulation runs at the fixed time step `Skin.FIXED_DT`.

FIXED_DT.haxe_doc: The fixed time step, in seconds, of the dynamic joints simulation.

MIN_SHADER_BONES.haxe_doc: The minimum number of bones allocated in the skinning shader (the actual size is the next power of two of the number of bones, which limits the number of shader variants).

MAX_SHADER_BONES.haxe_doc: The maximum number of bones per skinning draw. Skins with more bones must be split per material (see `h3d.anim.Skin.splitJoints`).

accumulator.haxe_doc: The time accumulated for the dynamic joints simulation, consumed by steps of `FIXED_DT`.

showJoints.haxe_doc: Displays the skeleton joints and bones with lines (debug).

enableRetargeting.haxe_doc: When enabled, joints flagged for retargeting keep their bind pose translation instead of the animated one, which allows playing an animation made for a skeleton with different proportions.

prevEnableRetargeting.haxe_doc: The value of `enableRetargeting` at the last joints sync.

getCurrentSkeletonBounds.haxe_doc: Returns the bounds of the current positions of the bound joints, in world space.

getSkinData.haxe_doc: Returns the skin data: the skeleton and the skinned primitive.

getJointRelPosition.haxe_doc: Returns the current transform of joint `name` relative to its parent, or `null` if the joint does not exist. @param additive If `true`, returns the additive pose of the joint instead (or `null` if none).

setSkinData.haxe_doc: Sets the skin data (skeleton and skinned primitive) and reallocates the joint states. @param shaderInit If `true`, (re)creates the skinning shader of the materials.

class.haxe_doc:
A skinned mesh: a mesh deformed by a skeleton of joints (bones), driven by skeletal animations.
Skins are created when loading a model with a skeleton (see `hxd.res.Model.toHmd` and `h3d.prim.ModelCache`), and animated with `Object.playAnimation`. The skinning is performed on the GPU by `h3d.shader.Skin`. Use `getObjectByName` with a joint name to get an object following that joint.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a skin using the skin data and materials of `subSkin`, posed by the skeleton of `baseSkin`.

class.haxe_doc:
A skin following the skeleton of another skin: the joints with the same name copy the pose of `baseSkin`.
Used for separate skinned parts sharing a skeleton, such as clothes or equipment on a character. Animations bound to the hierarchy are not applied to it, but animations played directly on it are (for instance facial animations on top of the body animation).

duration.haxe_doc: The time, in seconds, a point stays in the trail.

angle.haxe_doc: The orientation of the strip width, in radians: at `0` the strip extends along the local Y axis of the object, other values rotate it around the local X axis.

sizeStart.haxe_doc: The width of the strip at the head of the trail (most recent point).

sizeEnd.haxe_doc: The width of the strip at the tail of the trail (oldest point).

movementMin.haxe_doc: Movements smaller than this distance do not add width to the trail (the strip collapses while the object stays still).

movementMax.haxe_doc: Movements larger than this distance are split into several points, interpolated with a curve.

smoothness.haxe_doc: The curvature of the interpolation between points, from `0` (straight segments) to `1`.

materialData.haxe_doc: The material properties per `h3d.mat.MaterialSetup` name, saved with `save`. See `getMaterialProps`.

texture.haxe_doc: The texture applied to the strip: its U coordinate goes along the trail (`0` at the head, `1` at the tail) and its V coordinate across the strip.

getMaterialProps.haxe_doc: Returns the material properties for the current `h3d.mat.MaterialSetup`, creating them from the setup defaults for `"trail3D"` if needed.

clear.haxe_doc: Removes all the points of the trail.

save.haxe_doc: Returns the trail parameters as a serializable object (the texture is stored by its resource path).

load.haxe_doc: Loads the parameters returned by `save`. The texture is loaded from the resources, or replaced by a pink texture if not found.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a trail.

class.haxe_doc:
A ribbon following the movements of the object, such as a sword or projectile trail.
Every frame the trail records the absolute position and orientation of the object, and draws a strip through the recorded points that fades after `duration` seconds. Move the object (or its parent) to draw. The strip is drawn in world space.

transform.haxe_doc: The world transform of the instance.

optimized.haxe_doc: `true` for instances added with `World.add` (only position, uniform scale and Z rotation), which are merged faster.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an instance of `model` with transform `mat`.

class.haxe_doc: A model instance placed in a `World` chunk.

cx.haxe_doc: The X index of the chunk.

cy.haxe_doc: The Y index of the chunk.

x.haxe_doc: The X world position of the chunk.

y.haxe_doc: The Y world position of the chunk.

root.haxe_doc: The object containing the meshes of the chunk.

buffers.haxe_doc: The meshes of the chunk, one per material (indexed by `WorldMaterial.bits`).

bounds.haxe_doc: The world bounds of the elements of the chunk, used for culling.

initialized.haxe_doc: `true` when the meshes of the chunk are built.

lastFrame.haxe_doc: The last frame the chunk was visible, used to release the least recently seen chunks first.

elements.haxe_doc: The model instances of the chunk.

dispose.haxe_doc: Removes the chunk meshes from the scene.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty chunk at the given indexes.

class.haxe_doc: A square area of a `World`, of `World.chunkSize` units. The meshes of a chunk are built when it becomes visible and released by the garbage collection of the `World`.

bits.haxe_doc: A key combining the material settings, computed by `updateBits`. Geometries with the same bits are merged.

t.haxe_doc: The diffuse texture area in the big texture.

spec.haxe_doc: The specular texture area, if `World.enableSpecular` is set.

normal.haxe_doc: The normal map area, if `World.enableNormalMaps` is set.

mat.haxe_doc: The source material of the model.

blend.haxe_doc: The blend mode (`Alpha` by default, `None` for jpg textures).

killAlpha.haxe_doc: If set, pixels with an alpha below this threshold are discarded.

emissive.haxe_doc: If set, the emissive intensity of the material.

stencil.haxe_doc: If set, the stencil reference value written by the material.

name.haxe_doc: The material name, used as mesh name.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the material (the texture areas are shared).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a material with lights and shadows enabled.

class.haxe_doc: A material of a `World` model: the geometries sharing the same material bits are merged in the same mesh. Textures are packed in shared big textures (`h3d.mat.BigTexture`).

startVertex.haxe_doc: The first vertex of the part in the model buffer.

startIndex.haxe_doc: The first index of the part in the model index buffer.

vertexCount.haxe_doc: The number of vertexes of the part.

indexCount.haxe_doc: The number of indexes of the part.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a geometry using material `m`.

class.haxe_doc: A part of a `WorldModel` using one material.

enum.haxe_doc: Geometry optimizations available for `WorldModel.optimize`.

geometries.haxe_doc: The parts of the model, one per material.

bounds.haxe_doc: The local bounds of the model.

optimize.haxe_doc: Reorders the geometry with the given algorithm.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty model for resource `r`.

class.haxe_doc: A model loaded by `World.loadModel`: its geometry is kept on the CPU to be merged into the chunks.

chunkSize.haxe_doc: The size of a chunk, in world units.

enableSpecular.haxe_doc: For each texture loaded, will call resolveSpecularTexture and have separate spec texture.

enableNormalMaps.haxe_doc: For each texture loaded, will call resolveNormalMap and have separate normal texture.

specularInAlpha.haxe_doc: When enableSpecular=true, will store the specular value in the alpha channel instead of a different texture. This will erase alpha value of transparent textures, so should only be used if specular is only on opaque models.

wrap.haxe_doc: The wrap mode of the big textures.

garbage.haxe_doc: Releases the meshes of the least recently visible chunk, which are rebuilt when it becomes visible again.

done.haxe_doc: Finalizes the big textures. Call it after loading all the models.

loadModel.haxe_doc: Loads a model and its textures so that it can be added to the world. @param filter If set, only the parts of the model for which it returns `true` are loaded.

dispose.haxe_doc: Dispose the World instance. Note: Only chunked world objects will be disposed. Any objects added to World object will be disposed when World is removed from scene or scene is disposed.

onContextLost.haxe_doc: Releases the meshes of all the chunks after the GPU context was lost. They are rebuilt when visible.

addTransform.haxe_doc: Adds an instance of `model` with any world transform (slower to merge than `add`).

getWorldBounds.haxe_doc: Returns the bounds of all the instances of the world. @param b An optional bounds to add the result to.

priority.haxe_doc: When an object is lit by more lights than `LightSystem.maxLightsPerObject`, lights with a higher priority are kept first, then the nearest ones.

enableSpecular.haxe_doc: Enables the specular highlights of this light. Not supported by all lights (throws when enabled on those).

class.haxe_doc: Base class of the lights of the forward renderer (`h3d.scene.fwd.Renderer`, the default renderer). See `DirLight` and `PointLight`.

maxLightsPerObject.haxe_doc: The maximum number of lights applied to an object. When there are more lights, the lights with the highest `Light.priority` are kept first, then the lights nearest to the object (or to the camera target for objects with `Object.lightCameraCenter`).

perPixelLighting.haxe_doc: Computes the lighting per pixel. If `false`, it is computed per vertex (faster, less precise).

ambientLight.haxe_doc: The ambient light color, added to all the lit objects (`0.5, 0.5, 0.5` by default). Modify its components.

additiveLighting.haxe_doc: In the additive lighting model (by default), the lights are added after the ambient. In the new non additive ligthning model, the lights will be modulated against the ambient, so an ambient of 1 will reduce lights intensities to 0.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the light system.

class.haxe_doc: The light system of the forward renderer: each object is drawn with the ambient light and up to `maxLightsPerObject` lights shaders.

params.haxe_doc: The attenuation coefficients: `x` constant, `y` linear and `z` quadratic.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a point light.

class.haxe_doc:
A point light of the forward renderer, shining in all directions from its position.
Its intensity at distance `d` is divided by `params.x + params.y * d + params.z * d²`. The light is culled when this attenuated intensity falls below 1/128 outside of the camera view.

enableSky.haxe_doc: If `true`, the depth texture is cleared to zero instead of the maximum depth.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the depth pass.

class.haxe_doc: Renders the objects having a `"depth"` pass into the `depthMap` shader global (a packed depth texture).

new.haxe_doc: Creates the normal pass.

class.haxe_doc: Renders the objects having a `"normal"` pass into the `normalMap` shader global (a packed normal texture).

shadow.haxe_doc: The shadow map of the shadow light (1024x1024 pixels).

new.haxe_doc: Creates the renderer.

class.haxe_doc:
The forward renderer, used by default (see `h3d.mat.MaterialSetup`).
Objects are drawn directly to the output with their lights (see `LightSystem`), in this order: the `"shadow"`, `"depth"` and `"normal"` passes to their textures if used, then the `"default"`, `"alpha"` (sorted back to front) and `"additive"` passes.

power.haxe_doc: The light power. The intensity is `power * power` (scaled by 100 for point and capsule lights).

shadows.haxe_doc: The shadow map of the light. Shadows are disabled by default: set `shadows.mode` to enable them.

isMainLight.haxe_doc: If `true`, the light color, power, position, direction and shadow map are exposed to the shaders as the `mainLight*` globals (`mainLightColor`, `mainLightPower`, `mainLightPos`, `mainLightDir`, `mainLightShadowMap`, `mainLightViewProj`).

occlusionFactor.haxe_doc: How much the material ambient occlusion attenuates this light, from `0` (not at all) to `1` (fully).

enableForward.haxe_doc: If `true`, the light also lights the objects drawn in the forward passes (`"forward"` and `"forwardAlpha"`), such as transparent objects.

getIntensity.haxe_doc: Returns the light intensity, computed from `power`.

inFrustum.haxe_doc: Tells if the light volume intersects `frustum`. Lights outside of the camera frustum are not drawn.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the lights of the PBR renderer (`h3d.scene.pbr.Renderer`).
Lights with a volume (point, spot, capsule, rectangle) are drawn as their volume in the lighting pass, so they only cost for the pixels they cover. Each light owns its `shadows` map. See `DirLight`, `PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `CapsuleLight` and `RectangleLight`.

radius.haxe_doc: The radius of the light source.

length.haxe_doc: The length of the light segment, along the X axis.

zNear.haxe_doc: The near plane distance of the shadow map cameras.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a capsule light with a range of 10.

class.haxe_doc: A capsule shaped light of the PBR renderer (a segment of `length` along the X axis, with a `radius`), such as a neon tube, up to `range`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a decal using the given volume primitive and material.

class.haxe_doc: A projected decal for the PBR renderer: a box volume (usually a unit cube) whose material uses a `h3d.shader.pbr.VolumeDecal` shader to project a texture on the surfaces inside the box.

A directional light of the PBR renderer, such as the sun: its rays are parallel and it lights the whole scene.
The light direction is the X axis of the object (see `Object.setDirection`).
Base shader of the environment lighting precomputations (importance sampling helpers).
Computes the diffuse irradiance and the prefiltered specular cube maps of an `Environment`.
Computes the BRDF lookup texture shared by all environments (see `Environment.getDefaultLUT`).
Converts an equirectangular (panorama) texture into the faces of a cube map.
Converts a cube map into an equirectangular (panorama) texture.

getDefaultLUT.haxe_doc: Returns the BRDF lookup texture, computing it the first time.

getDefault.haxe_doc: Returns the default environment embedded in Heaps, with precomputed textures.

sampleBits.haxe_doc: The number of samples used by `compute` is `2^sampleBits`.

diffSize.haxe_doc: The size of the diffuse irradiance cube map faces.

specSize.haxe_doc: The size of the specular cube map faces.

specLevels.haxe_doc: The number of mip levels of the specular cube map used for the roughness levels. Computed by `compute`.

ignoredSpecLevels.haxe_doc: The number of smallest mip levels of the specular cube map not used for roughness levels.

hdrMax.haxe_doc: The maximum color value of the source texture used by `compute`, which limits the fireflies caused by very bright pixels.

source.haxe_doc: The source texture: a cube map or an equirectangular (2:1) panorama.

env.haxe_doc: The source as a cube map, converted from `source` on first access if needed.

lut.haxe_doc: The BRDF lookup texture, shared by all environments.

diffuse.haxe_doc: The diffuse irradiance cube map, computed by `compute`.

specular.haxe_doc: The prefiltered specular cube map, with one mip level per roughness level, computed by `compute`.

power.haxe_doc: The intensity of the environment lighting is `power * power`. With `0` the environment does not light the scene.

rotation.haxe_doc: The rotation of the environment around the Z axis, in radians.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the textures of the environment.

compute.haxe_doc: Computes the `diffuse` and `specular` lighting textures from the source. This is expensive: do it once, at load time.

defaultForwardShader.haxe_doc: The forward lighting shader added to the forward objects which do not already have one.

shadowHandles.haxe_doc: The bindless handles of the shadow maps used in the frame.

tightShadowSamplers.haxe_doc: If `true` (default on JavaScript), the forward shader declares only the shadow samplers used by the current lights instead of the maximum count. This saves texture units but compiles more shader variants. Ignored with bindless.

clusterMaxDistance.haxe_doc: If positive, the distance covered by the clusters; farther objects use the last depth slice. Otherwise the clusters cover the camera range up to `zFar`.

enableClustering.haxe_doc: Enables the light clustering when compute shaders are supported.

enableClusterHZB.haxe_doc: Uses the hierarchical depth buffer to skip the clusters and lights hidden by the opaque geometry.

setBuffers.haxe_doc: Copies the light buffer and counts of the frame to a custom forward shader `s`.

sortLights.haxe_doc: Returns the lights of the frame enabled for the forward passes (see `Light.enableForward`) and inside the camera frustum, sorted with the directional lights first, then by distance to the camera target.

fillLights.haxe_doc: Writes `lights` into the light buffer, within the buffer size and shadow limits. @param shadows If `false`, the lights are written without their shadows.

sync.haxe_doc: Updates the light buffer and the clusters for the current frame. Called by the PBR renderer before the forward passes.

createClusterDebug.haxe_doc: Debug: draws the clusters of the last frame as lines, colored by their number of lights. Returns `null` if no clusters were built.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU buffers.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the light buffer.

class.haxe_doc:
Packs the lights of the frame in a GPU buffer read by the forward shader (`h3d.shader.pbr.DefaultForward`), so that the objects drawn in the forward passes (such as transparent objects) are lit by the PBR lights.
When compute shaders are available, the lights can be sorted into a grid of clusters covering the camera view (16x9 tiles and 24 depth slices), so that each pixel only evaluates the lights affecting its cluster. A limited number of lights of each kind can cast shadows in the forward passes.

lightBuffer.haxe_doc: The buffer of lights used by the forward passes.

forwardMode.haxe_doc: `true` while the renderer draws the forward passes.

lightingShaders.haxe_doc: Additional shaders applied with each light in the lighting pass.

drawShadows.haxe_doc: Draws the shadow map of `light` with the given shadow casters.

drawScreenLights.haxe_doc: Draws the lights without volume (such as directional lights) as full screen passes. @param shadows If `false`, the shadows of these lights are ignored.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the light system.

class.haxe_doc: The light system of the PBR renderer. Lights are applied in a deferred lighting pass, except for the objects drawn in the forward passes, which read the lights from `lightBuffer`.

size.haxe_doc: The radius of the light source: closer than this distance, the light has its full intensity.

zNear.haxe_doc: The near plane distance of the shadow map cameras.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a point light with a range of 10.

class.haxe_doc: A point light of the PBR renderer, shining in all directions from its position up to `range`. Its shadows use a cube shadow map (`h3d.pass.PointShadowMap`).

width.haxe_doc: The width of the rectangle (along the Y axis).

height.haxe_doc: The height of the rectangle (along the Z axis).

verticalAngle.haxe_doc: The vertical opening angle of the emitted light, in degrees.

horizontalAngle.haxe_doc: The horizontal opening angle of the emitted light, in degrees.

range.haxe_doc: The maximum distance reached by the light.

fallOff.haxe_doc: The half angle, in degrees, inside which the light has its full intensity: it fades out up to half of `verticalAngle` / `horizontalAngle`.

getSpread.haxe_doc: Returns how far the light spreads sideways at `range` for an opening `angle` in degrees (capped to 179).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a rectangle light with a range of 10.

class.haxe_doc: A rectangular area light of the PBR renderer, such as a window or a screen. The rectangle is in the YZ plane of the object and shines along its X axis, up to `range`.

abstract.haxe_doc: What the PBR renderer displays: the lit scene or a debug view.

Performance.haxe_doc: Displays the lighting cost of each pixel as a heat map.
Displays the lighting cost of each pixel as a heat map.

abstract.haxe_doc: What the PBR renderer displays where no object is drawn.

Hide.haxe_doc: Nothing (the background stays black, or transparent with `Renderer.enableTransparency`).

Specular.haxe_doc: The specular lighting cube map of the environment (debug).

Irrad.haxe_doc: The diffuse irradiance cube map of the environment.

Hide.haxe_doc: Nothing (the background stays black, or transparent with `Renderer.enableTransparency`).

Specular.haxe_doc: The specular lighting cube map of the environment (debug).

Irrad.haxe_doc: The diffuse irradiance cube map of the environment.

abstract.haxe_doc: The tone mapping operators converting the HDR lighting to displayable colors.

Linear.haxe_doc: No tone mapping: colors are clamped.

Reinhard.haxe_doc: Reinhard operator: compresses the high values smoothly.

Filmic.haxe_doc: Filmic curve, configured by the `a` to `e` properties of `RenderProps` (ACES approximation by default).

KhronosNeutral.haxe_doc: Khronos PBR Neutral operator, which preserves the hue and saturation of the base colors.

Linear.haxe_doc: No tone mapping: colors are clamped.

Reinhard.haxe_doc: Reinhard operator: compresses the high values smoothly.

Filmic.haxe_doc: Filmic curve, configured by the `a` to `e` properties of `RenderProps` (ACES approximation by default).

KhronosNeutral.haxe_doc: Khronos PBR Neutral operator, which preserves the hue and saturation of the base colors.

skyColor.haxe_doc: The color of the sky, for the `CustomColor` sky mode.

occlusion.haxe_doc: The ambient occlusion strength is `occlusion * occlusion`.

forceDirectDiscard.haxe_doc: Discards the pixels not lit by the direct lights (default `false`).

exposure.haxe_doc: The exposure: colors are multiplied by `exp(exposure)` before tone mapping.

emissive.haxe_doc: The emissive intensity multiplier is `emissive * emissive`.

e.haxe_doc: The `e` factor of the `Filmic` tone mapping curve.

d.haxe_doc: The `d` factor of the `Filmic` tone mapping curve.

c.haxe_doc: The `c` factor of the `Filmic` tone mapping curve.

b.haxe_doc: The `b` factor of the `Filmic` tone mapping curve.

a.haxe_doc: The `a` factor of the `Filmic` tone mapping curve `(x * (a * x + b)) / (x * (c * x + d) + e)`.

typedef.haxe_doc: The properties of the PBR renderer (see `hxd.impl.AnyProps.props`), usually edited in Hide. Call `refreshProps()` after modifying them.

class.haxe_doc: Copies a depth channel texture to the output color.

Value.haxe_doc: The value of a variable of the given name.

PackNormal.haxe_doc: A normal packed in a color.

PackFloat.haxe_doc: A float packed in a color.

enum.haxe_doc: An output value of a link shader (see `Cache.getLinkShader`).
A vector component, for swizzling.

LIGHTMAP_STENCIL.haxe_doc: The stencil bit marking the pixels already lit by a volumetric light map, so that the environment lighting skips them.

toneMode.haxe_doc: The tone mapping operator, set from `RenderProps.tone` by `refreshProps`.

displayMode.haxe_doc: The display mode, set from `RenderProps.mode` by `refreshProps`.

updateHZB.haxe_doc: Builds the hierarchical depth buffer of the current depth into `RenderContext.hzb`, used for GPU occlusion culling. @param max If `true`, each mip level keeps the farthest depth of the pixels it covers (conservative for occlusion).

getPbrDepth.haxe_doc: Returns the depth texture of the renderer.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the renderer. It is usually created by `h3d.mat.PbrMaterialSetup`. @param env The environment, see `env`.

spotLightPrim.haxe_doc: Returns the pyramid primitive used to draw the light volume (shared, cached by the engine).

enum.haxe_doc: Elements return by `CallStack` methods.

callStack.haxe_doc: Return the call stack elements, or an empty array if not available.

exceptionStack.haxe_doc:
Return the exception stack : this is the stack elements between the place the last exception was thrown and the place it was caught, or an empty array if not available. Set `fullStack` parameter to true in order to return the full exception stack.
May not work if catch type was a derivative from `haxe.Exception`.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a representation of the stack as a printable string.

subtract.haxe_doc: Returns a range of entries of current stack from the beginning to the the common part of this and `stack`.
