abstract.haxe_doc:
This type unifies with any function type.
It is intended to be used as a type parameter constraint. If used as a real type, the underlying type will be `Dynamic`.

This type unifies with an enum instance if all constructors of the enum require no arguments.
It is intended to be used as a type parameter constraint. If used as a real type, the underlying type will be `Dynamic`.

This type unifies with anything but `Void`.
It is intended to be used as a type parameter constraint. If used as a real type, the underlying type will be `Dynamic`.

This type unifies with any instance of classes that have a constructor which
* is `public` and * unifies with the type used for type parameter `T`.
If a type parameter `A` is assigned to a type parameter `B` which is constrained to `Constructible<T>`, A must be explicitly constrained to `Constructible<T>` as well.
It is intended to be used as a type parameter constraint. If used as a real type, the underlying type will be `Dynamic`.

DynamicAccess is an abstract type for working with anonymous structures that are intended to hold collections of objects by the string key.
For example, these types of structures are often created from JSON.
Basically, it wraps `Reflect` calls in a `Map`-like interface.

acquire.haxe_doc: The current thread acquire the mutex or wait if not available. The same thread can acquire several times the same mutex but must release it as many times it has been acquired.

tryAcquire.haxe_doc: Try to acquire the mutex, returns true if acquire or false if it's already locked by another thread.

release.haxe_doc: Release a mutex that has been acquired by the current thread. The behavior is undefined if the current thread does not own the mutex.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a mutex.

class.haxe_doc: Creates a mutex, which can be used to acquire a temporary lock to access some ressource. The main difference with a lock is that a mutex must always be released by the owner thread.

repeat.haxe_doc: Schedule event for execution every `intervalMs` milliseconds in current loop.

cancel.haxe_doc: Prevent execution of a previously scheduled event in current loop.

promise.haxe_doc: Notify this loop about an upcoming event. This makes the thread stay alive and wait for as many events as the number of times `.promise()` was called. These events should be added via `.runPromised()`.

progress.haxe_doc:
Executes all pending events.
The returned time stamps can be used with `Sys.time()` for calculations.
Depending on a target platform this method may be non-reentrant. It must not be called from event callbacks.

loop.haxe_doc:
Execute all pending events. Wait and execute as many events as the number of times `promise()` was called. Runs until all repeating events are cancelled and no more events are expected.
Depending on a target platform this method may be non-reentrant. It must not be called from event callbacks.

class.haxe_doc: An event loop implementation used for `sys.thread.Thread`

run.haxe_doc: Start the main loop. Depending on the platform, this can return immediately or will only return when the application exits.

class.haxe_doc: If `haxe.MainLoop` is kept from DCE, then we will insert an `haxe.EntryPoint.run()` call just at then end of `main()`. This class can be redefined by custom frameworks so they can handle their own main loop logic.

abstract.haxe_doc:
A typed interface for bit flags. This is not a real object, only a typed interface for an actual Int. Each flag can be tested/set with the corresponding enum instance. Up to 32 flags can be stored that way.
Enum constructor indices are preserved from Haxe syntax, so the first declared is index 0, the next index 1 etc. The methods are optimized if the enum instance is passed directly, e.g. as `has(EnumCtor)`. Otherwise `Type.enumIndex()` reflection is used.

getName.haxe_doc:
Returns the name of enum `e`, including its path.
If `e` is inside a package, the package structure is returned dot- separated, with another dot separating the enum name:
pack1.pack2.(...).packN.EnumName
If `e` is a sub-type of a Haxe module, that module is not part of the package structure.
If `e` has no package, the enum name is returned.
If `e` is `null`, the result is unspecified.
The enum name does not include any type parameters.

createByName.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of enum `e` by calling its constructor `constr` with arguments `params`.
If `e` or `constr` is `null`, or if enum `e` has no constructor named `constr`, or if the number of elements in `params` does not match the expected number of constructor arguments, or if any argument has an invalid type, the result is unspecified.

createByIndex.haxe_doc:
Creates an instance of enum `e` by calling its constructor number `index` with arguments `params`.
The constructor indices are preserved from Haxe syntax, so the first declared is index 0, the next index 1 etc.
If `e` or `index` is `null`, or if enum `e` has no constructor corresponding to index `index`, or if the number of elements in `params` does not match the expected number of constructor arguments, or if any argument has an invalid type, the result is unspecified.

createAll.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of all constructors of enum `e` that require no arguments.
This may return the empty Array `[]` if all constructors of `e` require arguments.
Otherwise an instance of `e` constructed through each of its non- argument constructors is returned, in the order of the constructor declaration.
If `e` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

getConstructors.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of the names of all constructors of enum `e`.
The order of the constructor names in the returned Array is preserved from the original syntax.
If `c` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
This class provides advanced methods on enums. It is ideally used with `using EnumTools` and then acts as an [extension](https://haxe.org/manual/lf-static-extension.html) to the `enum` types.
If the first argument to any of the methods is `null`, the result is unspecified.

equals.haxe_doc:
Recursively compares two enum instances `a` and `b` by value.
Unlike `a == b`, this function performs a deep equality check on the arguments of the constructors (if there are any).
If `a` or `b` are `null`, the result is unspecified.

getName.haxe_doc:
Returns the constructor name of enum instance `e`.
The result String does not contain any constructor arguments.
If `e` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

getParameters.haxe_doc:
Returns a list of the constructor arguments of enum instance `e`.
If `e` has no arguments, the result is `[]`.
Otherwise the result are the values that were used as arguments to `e`, in the order of their declaration.
If `e` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

getIndex.haxe_doc:
Returns the index of enum instance `e`.
This corresponds to the original syntactic position of `e`. The index of the first declared constructor is 0, the next one is 1 etc.
If `e` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
This class provides advanced methods on enum values. It is ideally used with `using EnumValueTools` and then acts as an [extension](https://haxe.org/manual/lf-static-extension.html) to the `EnumValue` types.
If the first argument to any of the methods is `null`, the result is unspecified.

stack.haxe_doc: The call stack at the moment of the exception creation.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns exception message.

new.haxe_doc:
Create a new Exception instance.
The `previous` argument could be used for exception chaining.
The `native` argument is for internal usage only. There is no need to provide `native` argument manually and no need to keep it upon extending `haxe.Exception` unless you know what you're doing.

abstract.haxe_doc: Int32 provides a 32-bit integer with consistent overflow behavior across all platforms.

formatOutput.haxe_doc: Format the output of `trace` before printing it.

class.haxe_doc: Log primarily provides the `trace()` method, which is invoked upon a call to `trace()` in Haxe code.

isBlocking.haxe_doc: Tells if the event can lock the process from exiting (default:true)

stop.haxe_doc: Stop the event from firing anymore.

add.haxe_doc: Add a pending event to be run into the main loop.

tick.haxe_doc: Run the pending events. Return the time for next event.

class.haxe_doc: Do not use manually.

typedef.haxe_doc:
`PosInfos` is a magic type which can be used to generate position information into the output for debugging use.
If a function has a final optional argument of this type, i.e. `(..., ?pos:haxe.PosInfos)`, each call to that function which does not assign a value to that argument has its position added as call argument.
This can be used to track positions of calls in e.g. a unit testing framework.

USE_CACHE.haxe_doc:
If the values you are serializing can contain circular references or objects repetitions, you should set `USE_CACHE` to true to prevent infinite loops.
This may also reduce the size of serialization Strings at the expense of performance.
This value can be changed for individual instances of `Serializer` by setting their `useCache` field.

USE_ENUM_INDEX.haxe_doc:
Use constructor indexes for enums instead of names.
This may reduce the size of serialization Strings, but makes them less suited for long-term storage: If constructors are removed or added from the enum, the indices may no longer match.
This value can be changed for individual instances of `Serializer` by setting their `useEnumIndex` field.

run.haxe_doc:
Serializes `v` and returns the String representation.
This is a convenience function for creating a new instance of Serializer, serialize `v` into it and obtain the result through a call to `toString()`.

useCache.haxe_doc:
The individual cache setting for `this` Serializer instance.
See `USE_CACHE` for a complete description.

useEnumIndex.haxe_doc:
The individual enum index setting for `this` Serializer instance.
See `USE_ENUM_INDEX` for a complete description.

toString.haxe_doc:
Return the String representation of `this` Serializer.
The exact format specification can be found here: https://haxe.org/manual/serialization/format

serialize.haxe_doc:
Serializes `v`.
All haxe-defined values and objects with the exception of functions can be serialized. Serialization of external/native objects is not guaranteed to work.
The values of `this.useCache` and `this.useEnumIndex` may affect serialization output.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Serializer instance.
Subsequent calls to `this.serialize` will append values to the internal buffer of this String. Once complete, the contents can be retrieved through a call to `this.toString`.
Each `Serializer` instance maintains its own cache if `this.useCache` is `true`.

class.haxe_doc:
The Serializer class can be used to encode values and objects into a `String`, from which the `Unserializer` class can recreate the original representation.
This class can be used in two ways:
- create a `new Serializer()` instance, call its `serialize()` method with any argument and finally retrieve the String representation from `toString()` - call `Serializer.run()` to obtain the serialized representation of a single argument
Serialization is guaranteed to work for all haxe-defined classes, but may or may not work for instances of external/native classes.
The specification of the serialization format can be found here: <https://haxe.org/manual/std-serialization-format.html>

delay.haxe_doc:
Invokes `f` after `time_ms` milliseconds.
This is a convenience function for creating a new Timer instance with `time_ms` as argument, binding its `run()` method to `f` and then stopping `this` Timer upon the first invocation.
If `f` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

stop.haxe_doc:
Stops `this` Timer.
After calling this method, no additional invocations of `this.run` will occur.
It is not possible to restart `this` Timer once stopped.

run.haxe_doc:
This method is invoked repeatedly on `this` Timer.
It can be overridden in a subclass, or rebound directly to a custom function:
```haxe var timer = new haxe.Timer(1000); // 1000ms delay timer.run = function() { ... } ```
Once bound, it can still be rebound to different functions until `this` Timer is stopped through a call to `this.stop`.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new timer that will run every `time_ms` milliseconds.
After creating the Timer instance, it calls `this.run` repeatedly, with delays of `time_ms` milliseconds, until `this.stop` is called.
The first invocation occurs after `time_ms` milliseconds, not immediately.
The accuracy of this may be platform-dependent.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Timer` class allows you to create asynchronous timers on platforms that support events.
The intended usage is to create an instance of the `Timer` class with a given interval, set its `run()` method to a custom function to be invoked and eventually call `stop()` to stop the `Timer`.
Note that a running `Timer` may or may not prevent the program to exit automatically when `main()` returns.
It is also possible to extend this class and override its `run()` method in the child class.
Notice for threaded targets: `Timer` instances require threads they were created in to run with Haxe's event loops. Main thread of a Haxe program always contains an event loop. For other cases use `sys.thread.Thread.createWithEventLoop` and `sys.thread.Thread.runWithEventLoop` methods.

DEFAULT_RESOLVER.haxe_doc:
This value can be set to use custom type resolvers.
A type resolver finds a `Class` or `Enum` instance from a given `String`. By default, the Haxe `Type` Api is used.
A type resolver must provide two methods:
1. `resolveClass(name:String):Class<Dynamic>` is called to determine a `Class` from a class name 2. `resolveEnum(name:String):Enum<Dynamic>` is called to determine an `Enum` from an enum name
This value is applied when a new `Unserializer` instance is created. Changing it afterwards has no effect on previously created instances.

run.haxe_doc:
Unserializes `v` and returns the according value.
This is a convenience function for creating a new instance of Unserializer with `v` as buffer and calling its `unserialize()` method once.

unserialize.haxe_doc:
Unserializes the next part of `this` Unserializer instance and returns the according value.
This function may call `this.resolver.resolveClass` to determine a Class from a String, and `this.resolver.resolveEnum` to determine an Enum from a String.
If `this` Unserializer instance contains no more or invalid data, an exception is thrown.
This operation may fail on structurally valid data if a type cannot be resolved or if a field cannot be set. This can happen when unserializing Strings that were serialized on a different Haxe target, in which the serialization side has to make sure not to include platform-specific data.
Classes are created from `Type.createEmptyInstance`, which means their constructors are not called.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Unserializer instance, with its internal buffer initialized to `buf`.
This does not parse `buf` immediately. It is parsed only when calls to `this.unserialize` are made.
Each Unserializer instance maintains its own cache.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Unserializer` class is the complement to the `Serializer` class. It parses a serialization `String` and creates objects from the contained data.
This class can be used in two ways:
- create a `new Unserializer()` instance with a given serialization String, then call its `unserialize()` method until all values are extracted - call `Unserializer.run()` to unserialize a single value from a given String
The specification of the serialization format can be found here: <https://haxe.org/manual/serialization/format>

An exception containing arbitrary value.
This class is automatically used for throwing values, which don't extend `haxe.Exception` or native exception type. For example: ```haxe throw "Terrible error"; ``` will be compiled to ```haxe throw new ValueException("Terrible error"); ```

alloc.haxe_doc: Returns a new `Bytes` instance with the given `length`. The values of the bytes are not initialized and may not be zero.

ofString.haxe_doc: Returns the `Bytes` representation of the given `String`, using the specified encoding (UTF-8 by default).

get.haxe_doc: Returns the byte at index `pos`.

set.haxe_doc: Stores the given byte `v` at the given position `pos`.

fill.haxe_doc: Sets `len` consecutive bytes starting from index `pos` of `this` instance to `value`.

sub.haxe_doc: Returns a new `Bytes` instance that contains a copy of `len` bytes of `this` instance, starting at index `pos`.

getDouble.haxe_doc: Returns the IEEE double-precision value at the given position `pos` (in little-endian encoding). Result is unspecified if `pos` is outside the bounds.

getFloat.haxe_doc: Returns the IEEE single-precision value at the given position `pos` (in little-endian encoding). Result is unspecified if `pos` is outside the bounds.

setFloat.haxe_doc: Stores the given IEEE single-precision value `v` at the given position `pos` in little-endian encoding. Result is unspecified if writing outside of bounds.

getInt32.haxe_doc: Returns the 32-bit integer at the given position `pos` (in little-endian encoding).

getInt64.haxe_doc: Returns the 64-bit integer at the given position `pos` (in little-endian encoding).

setInt32.haxe_doc: Stores the given 32-bit integer `v` at the given position `pos` (in little-endian encoding).

getString.haxe_doc: Returns the `len`-bytes long string stored at the given position `pos`, interpreted with the given `encoding` (UTF-8 by default).

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a `String` representation of the bytes interpreted as UTF-8.

toHex.haxe_doc: Returns a hexadecimal `String` representation of the bytes of `this` instance.

RawNative.haxe_doc: Output the string the way the platform represent it in memory. This is the most efficient but is platform-specific

sort.haxe_doc:
Sorts Array `a` according to the comparison function `cmp`, where `cmp(x,y)` returns 0 if `x == y`, a positive Int if `x > y` and a negative Int if `x < y`.
This operation modifies Array `a` in place.
This operation is stable: The order of equal elements is preserved.
If `a` or `cmp` are null, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc: ArraySort provides a stable implementation of merge sort through its `sort` method. It should be used instead of `Array.sort` in cases where the order of equal elements has to be retained on all targets.

set.haxe_doc:

If `key` is already bound to a value, that binding disappears.
If `key` is null, the result is unspecified.

get.haxe_doc:

If `key` is not bound to any value, `null` is returned.
If `key` is null, the result is unspecified.

keys.haxe_doc:
Iterates over the keys of `this` BalancedTree.
This operation is performed in-order.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new BalancedTree, which is initially empty.

class.haxe_doc:
BalancedTree allows key-value mapping with arbitrary keys, as long as they can be ordered. By default, `Reflect.compare` is used in the `compare` method, which can be overridden in subclasses.
Operations have a logarithmic average and worst-case cost.
Iteration over keys and values, using `keys` and `iterator` respectively, are in-order.
A tree node of `haxe.ds.BalancedTree`.

EnumValueMap allows mapping of enum value keys to arbitrary values.
Keys are compared by value and recursively over their parameters. If any parameter is not an enum value, `Reflect.compare` is used to compare them.

Otherwise, false is returned.

class.haxe_doc:
A linked-list of elements. The list is composed of element container objects that are chained together. It is optimized so that adding or removing an element does not imply copying the whole list content every time.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-List.html

abstract.haxe_doc:
Map allows key to value mapping for arbitrary value types, and many key types.
This is a multi-type abstract, it is instantiated as one of its specialization types depending on its type parameters.
A Map can be instantiated without explicit type parameters. Type inference will then determine the type parameters from the usage.
Maps can also be created with `[key1 => value1, key2 => value2]` syntax.
Map is an abstract type, it is not available at runtime.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-Map.html

_new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Map.
This becomes a constructor call to one of the specialization types in the output. The rules for that are as follows:
1. if `K` is a `String`, `haxe.ds.StringMap` is used 2. if `K` is an `Int`, `haxe.ds.IntMap` is used 3. if `K` is an `EnumValue`, `haxe.ds.EnumValueMap` is used 4. if `K` is any other class or structure, `haxe.ds.ObjectMap` is used 5. if `K` is any other type, it causes a compile-time error
(Cpp) Map does not use weak keys on `ObjectMap` by default.

ObjectMap allows mapping of object keys to arbitrary values.

See `Map` for documentation details.
@see https://haxe.org/manual/std-Map.html

abstract.haxe_doc:
`ReadOnlyArray` is an abstract over an ordinary `Array` which only exposes APIs that don't modify the instance, hence "read-only".
Note that this doesn't necessarily mean that the instance is *immutable*. Other code holding a reference to the underlying `Array` can still modify it, and the reference can be obtained with a `cast`.

If `length` is less than or equal to 0, the result is unspecified.

print.haxe_doc:
Encodes `o`'s value and returns the resulting JSON string.
If `replacer` is given and is not null, it is used to retrieve actual object to be encoded. The `replacer` function takes two parameters, the key and the value being encoded. Initial key value is an empty string.
If `space` is given and is not null, the result will be pretty-printed. Successive levels will be indented by this string.

getBytes.haxe_doc: Returns either a copy or a reference of the current bytes. Once called, the buffer should no longer be used.

bigEndian.haxe_doc:
Endianness (word byte order) used when reading numbers.
If `true`, big-endian is used, otherwise `little-endian` is used.

readBytes.haxe_doc:
Read `len` bytes and write them into `s` to the position specified by `pos`.
Returns the actual length of read data that can be smaller than `len`.
See `readFullBytes` that tries to read the exact amount of specified bytes.

close.haxe_doc:
Close the input source.
Behaviour while reading after calling this method is unspecified.

readAll.haxe_doc:
Read and return all available data.
The `bufsize` optional argument specifies the size of chunks by which data is read. Its default value is target-specific.

readFullBytes.haxe_doc:
Read `len` bytes and write them into `s` to the position specified by `pos`.
Unlike `readBytes`, this method tries to read the exact `len` amount of bytes.

readUntil.haxe_doc:
Read a string until a character code specified by `end` is occurred.
The final character is not included in the resulting string.

readLine.haxe_doc:
Read a line of text separated by CR and/or LF bytes.
The CR/LF characters are not included in the resulting string.

readFloat.haxe_doc:
Read a 32-bit floating point number.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readDouble.haxe_doc:
Read a 64-bit double-precision floating point number.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readInt16.haxe_doc:
Read a 16-bit signed integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readUInt16.haxe_doc:
Read a 16-bit unsigned integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readUInt24.haxe_doc:
Read a 24-bit unsigned integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readInt32.haxe_doc:
Read a 32-bit signed integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

readString.haxe_doc: Read and `len` bytes as a string.

class.haxe_doc:
An Input is an abstract reader. See other classes in the `haxe.io` package for several possible implementations.
All functions which read data throw `Eof` when the end of the stream is reached.

bigEndian.haxe_doc:
Endianness (word byte order) used when writing numbers.
If `true`, big-endian is used, otherwise `little-endian` is used.

writeBytes.haxe_doc:
Write `len` bytes from `s` starting by position specified by `pos`.
Returns the actual length of written data that can differ from `len`.
See `writeFullBytes` that tries to write the exact amount of specified bytes.

close.haxe_doc:
Close the output.
Behaviour while writing after calling this method is unspecified.

writeFullBytes.haxe_doc:
Write `len` bytes from `s` starting by position specified by `pos`.
Unlike `writeBytes`, this method tries to write the exact `len` amount of bytes.

writeFloat.haxe_doc:
Write `x` as 32-bit floating point number.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

writeDouble.haxe_doc:
Write `x` as 64-bit double-precision floating point number.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

writeInt16.haxe_doc:
Write `x` as 16-bit signed integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

writeUInt16.haxe_doc:
Write `x` as 16-bit unsigned integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

writeInt32.haxe_doc:
Write `x` as 32-bit signed integer.
Endianness is specified by the `bigEndian` property.

writeInput.haxe_doc:
Read all available data from `i` and write it.
The `bufsize` optional argument specifies the size of chunks by which data is read and written. Its default value is 4096.

class.haxe_doc: An Output is an abstract write. A specific output implementation will only have to override the `writeByte` and maybe the `write`, `flush` and `close` methods. See `File.write` and `String.write` for two ways of creating an Output.

getBytes.haxe_doc:

class.haxe_doc: This exception is raised when reading while data is no longer available in the `haxe.io.Input`.

Blocked.haxe_doc: The IO is set into nonblocking mode and some data cannot be read or written

Overflow.haxe_doc: An integer value is outside its allowed range

OutsideBounds.haxe_doc: An operation on Bytes is outside of its valid range

enum.haxe_doc: The possible IO errors that can occur

directory.haxe_doc:
Returns the directory of `path`.
If the directory is `null`, the empty String `""` is returned.
If `path` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

withExtension.haxe_doc:
Returns a String representation of `path` where the extension is `ext`.
If `path` has no extension, `ext` is added as extension.
If `path` or `ext` are `null`, the result is unspecified.

join.haxe_doc:
Joins all paths in `paths` together.
If `paths` is empty, the empty String `""` is returned. Otherwise the paths are joined with a slash between them.
If `paths` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

normalize.haxe_doc:
Normalize a given `path` (e.g. turn `'/usr/local/../lib'` into `'/usr/lib'`).
Also replaces backslashes `\` with slashes `/` and afterwards turns multiple slashes into a single one.
If `path` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

addTrailingSlash.haxe_doc:
Adds a trailing slash to `path`, if it does not have one already.
If the last slash in `path` is a backslash, a backslash is appended to `path`.
If the last slash in `path` is a slash, or if no slash is found, a slash is appended to `path`. In particular, this applies to the empty String `""`.
If `path` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

removeTrailingSlashes.haxe_doc:
Removes trailing slashes from `path`.
If `path` does not end with a `/` or `\`, `path` is returned unchanged.
Otherwise the substring of `path` excluding the trailing slashes or backslashes is returned.
If `path` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

isAbsolute.haxe_doc: Returns `true` if the path is an absolute path, and `false` otherwise.

dir.haxe_doc:
The directory.
This is the leading part of the path that is not part of the file name and the extension.
Does not end with a `/` or `\` separator.
If the path has no directory, the value is `null`.

file.haxe_doc:
The file name.
This is the part of the part between the directory and the extension.
If there is no file name, e.g. for `".htaccess"` or `"/dir/"`, the value is the empty String `""`.

ext.haxe_doc:
The file extension.
It is separated from the file name by a dot. This dot is not part of the extension.
If the path has no extension, the value is `null`.

backslash.haxe_doc: `true` if the last directory separator is a backslash, `false` otherwise.

toString.haxe_doc:
Returns a String representation of `this` path.
If `this.backslash` is `true`, backslash is used as directory separator, otherwise slash is used. This only affects the separator between `this.dir` and `this.file`.
If `this.directory` or `this.extension` is `null`, their representation is the empty String `""`.

new.haxe_doc:

Path information can be retrieved by accessing the `dir`, `file` and `ext` properties.

class.haxe_doc:

remove.haxe_doc:
Removes all `name` metadata entries from the origin of `this` MetaAccess.
This method might clear several metadata entries of the same name.
If a `Metadata` array is obtained through a call to `get`, a subsequent call to `remove` has no effect on that array.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

has.haxe_doc:
Tells if the origin of `this` MetaAccess has a `name` metadata entry.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

get.haxe_doc:
Return the wrapped `Metadata` array.
Modifying this array has no effect on the origin of `this` MetaAccess. The `add` and `remove` methods can be used for that.

extract.haxe_doc:
Extract metadata entries by given `name`.
If there's no metadata with such name, empty array `[]` is returned.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

add.haxe_doc:
Adds the metadata specified by `name`, `params` and `pos` to the origin of `this` MetaAccess.
Metadata names are not unique during compilation, so this method never overwrites a previous metadata.
If a `Metadata` array is obtained through a call to `get`, a subsequent call to `add` has no effect on that array.
If any argument is null, compilation fails with an error.

diffPrefab.haxe_doc: Same as diffObject, but handles `type` and `children` fields as a special case : children is serialized as an object with prefabName: diffPrefab(prefab) and if original.type != modified.type, the whole modified object is copied as is (because we consider that changing the type of a prefab in a diff means the prefab was destroyed then re-created)

diffObject.haxe_doc: Returns the difference between two dynamic objects

diffArray.haxe_doc: Returns the difference between two arrays. If the arrays are found to be different, a full copy of modified will be returned as a Set()

apply.haxe_doc:
Modifies `target` dynamic so `apply(a, diffPrefab(a, b)) == b`
`apply` is meant to be used on serialized prefab data, with diffs generated by `diffPrefab`. Like in diffPrefab, the `children` field of the root and of each prefab in a children diff is handled with the prefab children diff semantics. Other object fields are merged as generated by diffObject, including their own `children` fields (for example the `overrides` of a nested Reference).
For performance reasons, `apply` doesn't copy the values it takes from `diff` : objects and arrays from `diff` are directly referenced in the result, and `diff` itself can be modified during the process (for example, `@index` fields are consumed). If you need to keep `diff` intact (e.g. to apply it several times), pass `deepCopy(diff)` instead.
The root of `diff` must contain a `#v` field set to DIFF_VERSION (diffPrefab sets it). If you craft a diff by hand, add it : a diff without `#v` (or with `#v` == 0) is applied with the original apply code, which is only kept to load diffs saved before versioning as they were.

applyObject.haxe_doc: Merges the fields of `diff` into `target`, as generated by `diffObject`. Unlike `apply`, a change of the `type` field is not considered as a prefab replacement. `children` is handled as prefab children only if `isPrefab` is set

applyV0.haxe_doc: Original apply code, used for diffs without `#v`. Don't fix the bugs in this function : it must give the same result as when these diffs were saved

class.haxe_doc:
Utility class to get the difference between two dynamics
There are two main functions : diff and apply, and they are reciprocal diff(A,B) = D apply(A,D) = B
the diff has a special support for prefab if the diffPrefab function is used : the children array is handled as a special case, and prefabs that change type are fully serialized in the diff instead of just the delta
Special fields prefixed by an @ can appear in the diff, they are as follow :
@removed : an array of keys name that are present in A but were removed in B @index : in the prefab children data, indicate that this child has changed index between the A.children and B.children array
The root of a diffPrefab result also contains a `#v` field, set to DIFF_VERSION

instanceParams.haxe_doc: The definitions of the particle parameters (`@:instParam` fields). Generated by `EmitterMacros`.

PARAMS.haxe_doc: All the parameter definitions, by name. Generated by `EmitterMacros`.

lifeTime.haxe_doc: The lifetime of the particles, in seconds.

lifeTimeRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the lifetime, in seconds: between `-lifeTimeRand` and `lifeTimeRand` is added.

subEmitterKind.haxe_doc: When this emitter is spawned, as a sub emitter of a parent emitter.

speedFactor.haxe_doc: The speed of the time of the emitter.

warmUpTime.haxe_doc: The time simulated when the emitter starts, in seconds.

delay.haxe_doc: The delay before the emitter starts, in seconds.

seedGroup.haxe_doc: Combined with the random seed: emitters with the same group and seed get the same random values.

alignLockAxis.haxe_doc: The axis locked by the `Axis` align mode.

simulationSpace.haxe_doc: The space in which the particles are simulated.

particleScaling.haxe_doc: Whether the particles are scaled with the parents of the emitter.

followRotation.haxe_doc: The particles follow the rotation of the emitter.

m.e: { t : PBool, disp : "Apply mesh transform", group : "Properties" }

applyMeshTransform.haxe_doc: Applies the transform of the particle template mesh.

emitDuration.haxe_doc: The duration of the emission, in seconds (`Duration` and `BurstDuration`).

m.e: { t : PInt(0, 100), disp : "Rate", animate : true, group : "Emit Params" }

emitRate.haxe_doc: The number of particles emitted per second.

m.e: { t : PInt(0, 100), disp : "Rate Min", animate : true, group : "Emit Params" }
{ t : PInt(0, 100), disp : "Rate Max", animate : true, group : "Emit Params" }
{ t : PFloat(0.01, 5.0), disp : "Rate Change Time", group : "Emit Params" }

emitRateChangeDelay.haxe_doc: The time between rate changes (`InfinityRandom`), in seconds.

burstDelay.haxe_doc: The time between bursts, in seconds.

m.e: { t : PInt(1, 10), disp : "Particle Count", animate : true, group : "Emit Params" }

burstParticleCount.haxe_doc: The number of particles of a burst.

maxCount.haxe_doc: The maximum number of particles alive.

emitShape.haxe_doc: The shape in which the particles are emitted.

m.e: { t : PFloat(0, 360.0), disp : "Angle", animate : true, group : "Emit Shape" }

emitAngle.haxe_doc: The angle of the cone shape, in degrees.

emitRad1.haxe_doc: The first radius of the shape.

emitRad2.haxe_doc: The second radius of the shape.

emitSurface.haxe_doc: Emits on the surface of the shape only.

emitOrientation.haxe_doc: The initial orientation of the particles.

useRandomColor.haxe_doc: Gives the particles a random color between `randomColor1` and `randomColor2`.

useRandomGradient.haxe_doc: Gives the particles a random color of `randomGradient`.

randomColor1.haxe_doc: The first random color, as `[r, g, b, a]`.

randomColor2.haxe_doc: The second random color, as `[r, g, b, a]`.

randomGradient.haxe_doc: The gradient of the random colors.

class.haxe_doc: A particle of an `Emitter2DObject`.

batch.haxe_doc: The sprite batch rendering the particles.

instDef.haxe_doc: The values of the particle parameters.

lifeTime.haxe_doc: The lifetime of the particles, in seconds.

lifeTimeRand.haxe_doc: The random variation of the lifetime, in seconds: between `-lifeTimeRand` and `lifeTimeRand` is added.

speedFactor.haxe_doc: The speed of the time of the emitter.

warmUpTime.haxe_doc: The time simulated when the emitter starts, in seconds.

delay.haxe_doc: The delay before the emitter starts, in seconds.

emitOrientation.haxe_doc: The initial orientation of the particles.

emitType.haxe_doc: When the particles are emitted (`InfinityRandom` is not supported).

burstParticleCount.haxe_doc: The number of particles of a burst.

burstDelay.haxe_doc: The time between bursts, in seconds.

emitDuration.haxe_doc: The duration of the emission, in seconds (`Duration` and `BurstDuration`).

emitRate.haxe_doc: The number of particles emitted per second.

emitRateChangeDelay.haxe_doc: The time between rate changes (not used).

emitScale.haxe_doc: The factor of the emit rate, between `0` and `1`.

maxCount.haxe_doc: The maximum number of particles alive.

startSpeed.haxe_doc: The initial speed, in the space of the emitter.

startWorldSpeed.haxe_doc: The initial speed, in world space.

emitShape.haxe_doc: The shape in which the particles are emitted.

emitRadius.haxe_doc: The radius of the circle shape.

emitAngle1.haxe_doc: The start angle of the circle shape, in degrees.

emitAngle2.haxe_doc: The end angle of the circle shape, in degrees.

emitWidth.haxe_doc: The width of the rectangle shape.

emitHeight.haxe_doc: The height of the rectangle shape.

emitSurface.haxe_doc: Emits on the border of the shape only.

color.haxe_doc: The color of the particles (`Color` sprite).

texture.haxe_doc: The path of the texture (`Texture` sprite).

spriteSheet.haxe_doc: The path of the sprite sheet texture, or `null`.

frameCount.haxe_doc: The number of frames of the sprite sheet.

frameDivisionX.haxe_doc: The number of columns of the sprite sheet.

frameDivisionY.haxe_doc: The number of rows of the sprite sheet.

animationSpeed.haxe_doc: The speed of the sprite sheet animation.

animationUseSourceUVs.haxe_doc: Uses the texture coordinates of the tile in each frame.

animationBlendBetweenFrames.haxe_doc: Blends the consecutive frames of the animation.

useRandomColor.haxe_doc: Gives the particles a random color between `randomColor1` and `randomColor2` (`Color` sprite).

useRandomGradient.haxe_doc: Gives the particles a random color of `randomGradient` (`Color` sprite).

randomGradient.haxe_doc: The gradient of the random colors.

invTransform.haxe_doc: The inverse transform of the emitter.

init.haxe_doc: Generates the random values (`randSlots` per particle) and sets up the sprite sheet.

setTime.haxe_doc: Sets the time of the emitter, simulating the particles (restarting when the time goes back).

new.haxe_doc: Creates the object.

InvLerp.haxe_doc: `invLerp(v, a, b)`: the position of `v` between `a` and `b`, clamped to `[0, 1]`.

TextureLod.haxe_doc: `tex.getLod(uv, lod)`: samples a mip level of a texture.

Texel.haxe_doc: `tex.fetch(pos)`: reads a texel at integer coordinates.

Pack.haxe_doc: `pack(v)`: packs a float in `[0, 1]` into a color.

PackNormal.haxe_doc: `packNormal(n)`: packs a normal into a color.

UnpackNormal.haxe_doc: `unpackNormal(c)`: the normal from the XY of a normal map color.

ScreenToUv.haxe_doc: `screenToUv(p)`: converts screen coordinates (`[-1, 1]`, Y up) to texture coordinates.

UvToScreen.haxe_doc: `uvToScreen(uv)`: converts texture coordinates to screen coordinates.

ChannelReadLod.haxe_doc: `channel.getLod(uv, lod)`: reads a mip level of a `TChannel`.

ChannelTextureSize.haxe_doc: `channel.size()`: the size of the texture of a `TChannel`.

Trace.haxe_doc: `trace(...)`: prints its arguments when the shader is evaluated (debug).

FragCoord.haxe_doc: `fragCoord`: the window coordinates of the pixel.

FrontFacing.haxe_doc: `frontFacing`: tells if the face is front facing.

Barycentrics.haxe_doc: `barycentrics`: the barycentric coordinates of the pixel in its triangle (DirectX 12).

VertexAt.haxe_doc: `vertexAt(v, index)`: the value of an input at a vertex of the triangle (DirectX 12).

SetLayout.haxe_doc: `setLayout(x, y, z)`: the size of a work group of a compute shader.

ImageStore.haxe_doc: `tex.store(pos, color)`: writes a texel of a read-write texture.

ComputeVar_GlobalInvocation.haxe_doc: `computeVar.globalInvocation`: the index of the invocation of a compute shader.

ComputeVar_LocalInvocation.haxe_doc: `computeVar.localInvocation`: the index of the invocation in its work group.

ComputeVar_WorkGroup.haxe_doc: `computeVar.workGroup`: the index of the work group.

ComputeVar_LocalInvocationIndex.haxe_doc: `computeVar.localInvocationIndex`: the flattened index of the invocation in its work group.

AtomicAdd.haxe_doc: `atomicAdd(buf, index, data)`: adds to an element of a buffer and returns its previous value.

GroupMemoryBarrier.haxe_doc: `groupMemoryBarrier()`: synchronizes the memory accesses of a work group.

UnpackSnorm4x8.haxe_doc: `unpackSnorm4x8(x)`: four signed normalized bytes to a vector.

UnpackUnorm4x8.haxe_doc: `unpackUnorm4x8(x)`: four unsigned normalized bytes to a vector.

TexelLod.haxe_doc: `tex.fetchLod(pos, lod)`: reads a texel of a mip level at integer coordinates.

ResolveSampler.haxe_doc: `resolveSampler(handle, tex)`: sets a texture from a bindless handle.

ResolveBuffer.haxe_doc: `resolveBuffer(handle, buf)`: sets a buffer from a bindless handle.

FindLSB.haxe_doc: `findLSB(x)`: the index of the least significant bit set.

FindMSB.haxe_doc: `findMSB(x)`: the index of the most significant bit set.

AtomicAnd.haxe_doc: `atomicAnd(buf, index, data)`: combines an element of a buffer with a bitwise and, and returns its previous value.

AtomicOr.haxe_doc: `atomicOr(buf, index, data)`: combines an element of a buffer with a bitwise or, and returns its previous value.

AZERTY_EQUALS.haxe_doc: The key of the `=` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_COMMA.haxe_doc: The key of the `,` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_SEMICOLON.haxe_doc: The key of the `;` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_COLON.haxe_doc: The key of the `:` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_MODULO.haxe_doc: The key of the `ù` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_PARENT_CLOSE.haxe_doc: The key of the `)` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_MULTIPLY.haxe_doc: The key of the `*` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_POWER.haxe_doc: The key of the `^` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_SQUARED.haxe_doc: The key of the `²` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_EXCLAM.haxe_doc: The key of the `!` character on AZERTY keyboards.

NUMBER_0.haxe_doc: The 0 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_1.haxe_doc: The 1 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_2.haxe_doc: The 2 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_3.haxe_doc: The 3 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_4.haxe_doc: The 4 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_5.haxe_doc: The 5 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_6.haxe_doc: The 6 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_7.haxe_doc: The 7 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_8.haxe_doc: The 8 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_9.haxe_doc: The 9 key of the main keyboard.

NUMPAD_0.haxe_doc: The 0 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_1.haxe_doc: The 1 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_2.haxe_doc: The 2 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_3.haxe_doc: The 3 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_4.haxe_doc: The 4 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_5.haxe_doc: The 5 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_6.haxe_doc: The 6 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_7.haxe_doc: The 7 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_8.haxe_doc: The 8 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_9.haxe_doc: The 9 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_MULT.haxe_doc: The `*` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_ADD.haxe_doc: The `+` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_ENTER.haxe_doc: The Enter key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_SUB.haxe_doc: The `-` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_DOT.haxe_doc: The `.` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_DIV.haxe_doc: The `/` key of the numeric keypad.

MOUSE_WHEEL_UP.haxe_doc: * Mouse wheel does not have an off signal, and should be checked only through `isPressed` method. * Note that there may be multiple wheel scrolls between 2 frames, and to receive more accurate * results, it is recommended to directly listen to wheel events which also provide OS-generated wheel delta value. * See `Interactive.onWheel` for per-interactive events. For scene-based see `Scene.addEventListener` * when event is `EWheel`. For global hook use `Window.addEventTarget` method.

MOUSE_WHEEL_DOWN.haxe_doc: * Mouse wheel does not have an off signal, and should be checked only through `isPressed` method. * Note that there may be multiple wheel scrolls between 2 frames, and to receive more accurate * results, it is recommended to directly listen to wheel events which also provide OS-generated wheel delta value. * See `Interactive.onWheel` for per-interactive events. For scene-based see `Scene.addEventListener` * when event is `EWheel`. For global hook use `Window.addEventTarget` method.

LOC_LEFT.haxe_doc: a bit that is set for left keys

LOC_RIGHT.haxe_doc: a bit that is set for right keys

ALLOW_KEY_REPEAT.haxe_doc: This enable the native key repeat behavior, and will report several times isPressed() in case a key is kept pressed for a long time if this is allowed by the target platform.

isDown.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button is currently down.

getFrame.haxe_doc: Returns the frame number used to timestamp the key events.

isPressed.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button was pressed since the last frame.

isReleased.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button was released since the last frame.

initialize.haxe_doc: Starts listening to the events of the window. Called by `hxd.App`.

dispose.haxe_doc: Stops listening to the events of the window and clears the key states.

getKeyName.haxe_doc: Returns a readable name for the key code, such as `"Escape"` or `"F1"`, or `null` if unknown.

class.haxe_doc: The key codes, and the state of the keyboard and mouse buttons, to poll in the update loop. Mouse buttons use the codes `0` to `6`, so they can be tested with the same functions as keys. For Shift, Ctrl and Alt, both the generic code (`SHIFT`) and the located code (`LSHIFT` or `RSHIFT`) are reported. `hxd.App` calls `initialize` automatically.

PI.haxe_doc: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

EPSILON.haxe_doc: A very small value (`1e-10`), used to compare floats.

EPSILON2.haxe_doc: The square of `EPSILON`, used to compare squared distances.

isFinite.haxe_doc: Tells if `v` is neither infinite nor `NaN`.

fmt.haxe_doc: Rounds `v` to 4 significant digits, and returns `0` for values under `1e-6`. Useful to print values.

exp.haxe_doc: Returns e raised to the power `f`.

logBase.haxe_doc: Returns the logarithm of `f` in the given base.

floor.haxe_doc: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to `f`.

ffloor.haxe_doc: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to `f`, as a `Float`.

ceil.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to `f`.

round.haxe_doc: Returns `f` rounded to the nearest integer.

fround.haxe_doc: Returns `f` rounded to the nearest integer, as a `Float`.

clamp.haxe_doc: Returns `f` limited to the `[min, max]` range (`[0, 1]` by default).

cos.haxe_doc: Returns the cosine of the angle `f`, in radians.

sin.haxe_doc: Returns the sine of the angle `f`, in radians.

tan.haxe_doc: Returns the tangent of the angle `f`, in radians.

acos.haxe_doc: Returns the arc cosine of `f`, in radians.

asin.haxe_doc: Returns the arc sine of `f`, in radians.

atan.haxe_doc: Returns the arc tangent of `f`, in radians.

atan2.haxe_doc: Returns the angle of the vector `(dx, dy)`, in radians in the `[-PI, PI]` range.

iabs.haxe_doc: Returns the absolute value of the integer `i`.

imax.haxe_doc: Returns the greatest of the integers `a` and `b`.

imin.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest of the integers `a` and `b`.

iclamp.haxe_doc: Returns the integer `v` limited to the `[min, max]` range.

lerp.haxe_doc: Linear interpolation between two values. When k is 0 a is returned, when it's 1, b is returned.

inverseLerp.haxe_doc: Returns a value between 0 and 1, that determines where val lies between a and b.

ease.haxe_doc: Similar to linear interpolation (k is between [0,1]), but can be controled with easing parameter. When easing is 0 it's linear.

lerpTime.haxe_doc: Same as lerp but is scaled based on current FPS, using current elapsed time in seconds.

bitCount.haxe_doc: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in `v`.

isPOT.haxe_doc: Tells if `v` is a power of two (also true for `0`).

nextPOT.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest power of two greater than or equal to `v`.

distanceSq.haxe_doc: Returns the squared length of the vector `(dx, dy, dz)`.

distance.haxe_doc: Returns the length of the vector `(dx, dy, dz)`.

angle.haxe_doc: Wraps an angle into the `]-PI, PI]` range. Can be used to measure the direction between two angles : if Math.angle(A-B) < 0 go left else go right.

angleLerp.haxe_doc: Interpolates from angle `a` to angle `b` by `k`, using the shortest way around the circle.

angleMove.haxe_doc: Move angle a towards angle b with a max increment. Return the new angle.

valueMove.haxe_doc: Move a value towards the given target using the max increment. Return the new value.

shuffle.haxe_doc: Shuffles the array in place, using `Std.random`.

random.haxe_doc: Returns a random float between `0` (included) and `max` (excluded).

srand.haxe_doc: Returns a signed random between -max and max (both included).

b2f.haxe_doc: * takes an int , masks it and devide so that it safely maps 0...255 to 0...1.0 * @paramv an int between 0 and 255 will be masked * @return a float between( 0 and 1)

f2b.haxe_doc: * takes a float , clamps it and multipy so that it safely maps 0...1 to 0...255.0 * @param f a float * @return an int [0...255]

umod.haxe_doc: * returns the modulo but always positive

ufmod.haxe_doc: * returns the modulo but always positive

class.haxe_doc: Math helpers, inlined where possible: most functions call `std.Math`, with `Int` and `Float` variants and game-oriented additions (angles, interpolation, random).

ranalogY.haxe_doc: The axis of the right stick, vertical.

ranalogX.haxe_doc: The axis of the right stick, horizontal.

ranalogClick.haxe_doc: The click of the right stick (R3).

dpadUp.haxe_doc: The up button of the directional pad.

dpadRight.haxe_doc: The right button of the directional pad.

dpadLeft.haxe_doc: The left button of the directional pad.

dpadDown.haxe_doc: The down button of the directional pad.

analogY.haxe_doc: The axis of the left stick, vertical.

analogX.haxe_doc: The axis of the left stick, horizontal.

analogClick.haxe_doc: The click of the left stick (L3).

typedef.haxe_doc: The mapping of the buttons and axes of a game pad: each field is the index of the button or axis in `Pad.buttons` and `Pad.values`. `names` gives a display name for each index.

CONFIG_SDL.expr: { analogX : 0, analogY : 1, ranalogX : 2, ranalogY : 3, A : 6, B : 7, X : 8, Y : 9, LB : 15, RB : 16, LT : 4, RT : 5, back : 10, start : 12, analogClick : 13, ranalogClick : 14, dpadUp : 17, dpadDown : 18, dpadLeft : 19, dpadRight : 20, names : ["LX", "LY", "RX", "RY", "LT", "RT", "A", "B", "X", "Y", "Back", null, "Start", "LCLK", "RCLK", "LB", "RB", "DUp", "DDown", "DLeft", "DRight"] }

CONFIG_SDL.haxe_doc: Works with both DualShock and XBox controllers

ANALOG_BUTTON_THRESHOLDS.haxe_doc: The values at which an analog input (trigger or axis) is considered as pressed and released in `buttons`.

DEFAULT_CONFIG.haxe_doc: The default configuration for the current platform.

createDummy.haxe_doc: Creates a new dummy unconnected game pad, which can be used instead of checking for null everytime. Use wait() to get real physical game pad access.

wait.haxe_doc: Wait until a gamepad gets connected. On some platforms, this might require the user to press a button until it activates

connected.haxe_doc: Tells if the pad is connected. It is `false` for a dummy pad and after a disconnection.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the pad, as reported by the system.

index.haxe_doc: The index of the pad, or `-1` for a dummy pad.

config.haxe_doc: The mapping of the buttons and axes, used to read `buttons` and `values` by name, as in `pad.isDown(pad.config.A)`.

xAxis.haxe_doc: The X axis of the left stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

yAxis.haxe_doc: The Y axis of the left stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

rxAxis.haxe_doc: The X axis of the right stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

ryAxis.haxe_doc: The Y axis of the right stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

axisDeadZone.haxe_doc: The radius around the center under which the sticks report `0`.

buttons.haxe_doc: The state of each button, indexed as in `config`.

values.haxe_doc: The value of each button (`0` to `1`) or axis (`-1` to `1`), indexed as in `config`.

prevValues.haxe_doc: The values of the previous frame.

onDisconnect.haxe_doc: Called when the pad is disconnected.

isDown.haxe_doc: Tells if the button is down.

isPressed.haxe_doc: Tells if the button was pressed since the previous frame.

isReleased.haxe_doc: Tells if the button was released since the previous frame.

reset.haxe_doc: Resets all buttons and axes to their released state.

rumble.haxe_doc: Makes the pad vibrate with the given `strength` (`0` to `1`) for `time_s` seconds, if supported.

class.haxe_doc: A game pad (controller). Use `Pad.wait` to be notified of connected pads, and read `buttons`, `values` and the axes every frame. `Pad.createDummy` returns an unconnected pad that can be used before a real one is connected.

ReadOnly.haxe_doc: The bytes are shared and must not be modified: they are copied before the first change.

AlphaPremultiplied.haxe_doc: The colors are premultiplied by the alpha.

enum.haxe_doc: Flags of a `Pixels`.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `ARGB` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `ARGB` in place.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `ARGB` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `R32F` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel in the X component of `v` (or of a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel to the X component of `v`.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `R32F` in place.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel in the X component of `v` (or of a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel to the X component of `v`.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `R32F` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `RGBA32F` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the 4 values of the pixel in `v` (or in a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the 4 values of the pixel.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `RGBA32F` in place.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the 4 values of the pixel in `v` (or in a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the 4 values of the pixel.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `RGBA32F` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: A color channel.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the channel.

fromInt.haxe_doc: Returns the channel of the given index.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the channel.

fromInt.haxe_doc: Returns the channel of the given index.

switchEndian.haxe_doc: Reverses the order of the 4 bytes of `v`.

switchBR.haxe_doc: Swaps the first and third bytes of `v` (converts between `0xAARRGGBB` and `0xAABBGGRR`).

calcDataSize.haxe_doc: Returns the size in bytes of an image of the given size and format.

calcStride.haxe_doc: Returns the size in bytes of a row of pixels (of a row of 4x4 blocks for compressed formats).

isFloatFormat.haxe_doc: Tells if the format stores float values (16 or 32 bits floats).

getChannelOffset.haxe_doc: Returns the byte offset for the requested channel (0=R,1=G,2=B,3=A) Returns -1 if the channel is not found

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocates an image of the given size and format, filled with zeros.

toDDSLayers.haxe_doc: Build DDS texture bytes from an array of pixels : - can contain a single image - can contain multiple layers (set isCubeMap = true if it's a cubemap) - can contain single or multiple layers with mipmaps (auto detected with diffences in size)

bytes.haxe_doc: The data of the image, starting at `offset`.

format.haxe_doc: The format of the pixels. Use `convert` to change it.

width.haxe_doc: The width in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height in pixels.

dataSize.haxe_doc: The size of the image data in bytes.

offset.haxe_doc: The position of the image data in `bytes`.

sub.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of a rectangle of the image. Throws if it is outside the image.

blit.haxe_doc: Copies a rectangle of `src` at the given position. `src` is converted to the format of this image first.

clear.haxe_doc: Fills the image with the color, in `0xAARRGGBB` format. The bits set in `preserveMask` keep their current value. Only supported for 4 bytes formats (`BGRA`, `RGBA`, `ARGB`), unless all the bytes of the color are equal.

toVector.haxe_doc: Returns the colors of the pixels in `0xAARRGGBB` format. Only supported for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`.

makeSquare.haxe_doc: Extends the image to power of two dimensions, filling the new pixels with zeros. Returns a new image if `copy` is set, or modifies this one.

flipY.haxe_doc: Flips the image vertically, in place.

convert.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to the `target` format, in place. Throws if the conversion is not supported.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel in `0xAARRGGBB` format (for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`), or its raw value (for `R8` and `RG8`).

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel in `0xAARRGGBB` format (for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`), or its raw value (for `R8` and `RG8`).

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel as floats in `v` (or in a new vector). 8 and 16 bits channels are returned in the `[0, 1]` range.

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel from floats. 8 and 16 bits channels take values in the `[0, 1]` range.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the bytes of the image.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a description of the size and format of the image.

toPNG.haxe_doc: Encodes the image as a PNG file with the given compression level. Images not in `ARGB` or `R8` format are converted to `BGRA` first.

toDDS.haxe_doc: Encodes the image as a DDS file (see `toDDSLayers`).

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the image.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an image using the given bytes, without copying them. See `alloc` to allocate new bytes.

class.haxe_doc: An image in CPU memory: its bytes, size and `PixelFormat`. It is used to load, convert and save images, and to upload data to a `h3d.mat.Texture`.

hash.haxe_doc: Returns a well distributed hash of the integer `n` (Murmur3 mixing), useful as a stateless random value.

create.haxe_doc: Create a randomized hxd.Rand (using a Std.random number as seed)

init.haxe_doc: Initialize the random generator with a seed.

random.haxe_doc: Return a random integer between 0 and n (excluded).

rand.haxe_doc: Return a random float between 0.0 and 1.0 (excluded)

srand.haxe_doc: Return a random float between -scale and +scale (excluded)

new.haxe_doc: Create a random generator with a seed.

class.haxe_doc: `hxd.Rand` is a seeded random number generator, that allows to get always the same results starting from a given seed.

enablePhysicalMouse.haxe_doc: * enablePhysicalMouse : enable mouse movements of system mouse, set it to false anse use setMousePos instead to manually set mouse position

mouseCheckMove.haxe_doc: * enable/disable per frame check of elements under mouse (default:true)

defaultCursor.haxe_doc: * Default cursor when there is no Interactive present under cursor.

setMousePos.haxe_doc: Sets the mouse position, used when `enablePhysicalMouse` is disabled.

addScene.haxe_doc: Adds a scene, at the end of the list or at `index`. The scenes receive events in list order.

dispose.haxe_doc: Stops listening to the window events.

focus.haxe_doc: Gives the focus to the interactive, which then receives the key, text and wheel events. The interactive can refuse it by cancelling the `EFocus` event.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes the focus from the current interactive. It can refuse it by cancelling the `EFocusLost` event.

checkEvents.haxe_doc: Dispatches the pending events. Called every frame by `hxd.App`.

startCapture.haxe_doc: Sends all the following events to `f` until `stopCapture` is called, such as for a drag operation. `onCancel` is called when the capture stops. If `touchId` is set, only the events of this touch are captured.

getFocus.haxe_doc: Returns the interactive which has the focus.

updateCursor.haxe_doc: Updates the displayed cursor after the cursor of the interactive changed.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an event dispatcher listening to the window (the current one by default).

class.haxe_doc: Dispatches the window input events to the interactives of one or more scenes. It handles the focus, the over/out events, the mouse capture and the cursor. `hxd.App` creates one as `sevents`, with `s2d` and `s3d` added.

enum.haxe_doc: The kind of platform the application runs on (see `System.platform`).

IsTouch.haxe_doc: The main input is a touch screen.

IsWindowed.haxe_doc: The application runs in a window that can be resized or moved.

IsMobile.haxe_doc: The application runs on a mobile device.

enum.haxe_doc: Boolean system properties, queried with `System.getValue`.

Unknown.haxe_doc: The layout could not be detected.

enum.haxe_doc: The detected keyboard layout (see `System.getKeyboardLayout`).

class.haxe_doc: Use `sys.io.File.write` to create a `FileOutput`.

getMonitors.haxe_doc: Returns the list of the connected monitors.

getInstance.haxe_doc: Returns the current window (on JS, it is created for the `#webgl` canvas if needed).

hasWindow.haxe_doc: Tells if at least one window is open.

id.haxe_doc: The identifier of the native window (only set with the `multidriver` define).

x.haxe_doc: The X position of the window on the screen (of the canvas in the page on JS).

y.haxe_doc: The Y position of the window on the screen (of the canvas in the page on JS).

width.haxe_doc: The width of the drawable area in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the drawable area in pixels.

mouseX.haxe_doc: The X position of the mouse, relative to the window.

mouseY.haxe_doc: The Y position of the mouse, relative to the window.

mouseLock.haxe_doc: Tells if the mouse is locked. Deprecated: use `mouseMode = AbsoluteUnbound(true)`.

mouseClip.haxe_doc: If set, will restrain the mouse cursor within the window boundaries.

mouseMode.haxe_doc:
Set the mouse movement input handling mode.
@see `hxd.impl.MouseMode` for more details on each mode.

monitor.haxe_doc: The index of the monitor used in fullscreen and borderless modes, or `null` to use the current monitor.

framerate.haxe_doc: The refresh rate to use when changing the resolution in fullscreen mode, or `null` to keep the current one.

vsync.haxe_doc: Tells if the rendering is synchronized with the screen refresh. It can't be disabled on JS.

isFocused.haxe_doc: Tells if the window has the focus.

displayScale.haxe_doc: Get the preferred scaling ratio for high dpi displays for this window

title.haxe_doc: The title of the window (of the page on JS).

displayMode.haxe_doc: The display mode of the window: windowed, borderless or fullscreen. On JS, any mode other than `Windowed` requests the browser fullscreen.

currentMonitorIndex.haxe_doc: The index of the monitor containing the window.

onClose.haxe_doc: Called when the user asks to close the window. Return `false` to keep it open.

onMove.haxe_doc: Called when the window is moved.

onMouseModeChange.haxe_doc: Called when `mouseMode` changes, including when only the parameters of the mode change. Returns a mouse mode to use instead of `to`, or `null` to keep it.

event.haxe_doc: Sends an event to all the event targets.

addEventTarget.haxe_doc: Adds a function called for every input event of the window.

addResizeEvent.haxe_doc: Adds a function called when the window is resized.

resize.haxe_doc: Resizes the window (not supported on JS). In fullscreen mode, it also changes the screen resolution to the closest available one.

setPosition.haxe_doc: Moves the window on the screen (not supported on JS).

addDragAndDropTarget.haxe_doc: Adds a function called when files are dropped on the window.

setCursorPos.haxe_doc: Moves the mouse cursor, relative to the window. If `emitEvent` is set, an `EMove` event is sent. On JS, the browser can't move the cursor: it is only allowed in relative mouse modes, and sets the mouse position.

captureMouseEvents.haxe_doc: Enables or disables the mouse capture: while enabled, the window keeps receiving mouse events when the cursor leaves it.

setFullScreen.haxe_doc: Enables or disables fullscreen mode. Deprecated: use `displayMode`.

setIcon.haxe_doc: Sets the icon of the window (not supported on JS).

isMaximized.haxe_doc: Tells if the window is maximized.

getCurrentDisplaySetting.haxe_doc: Returns the current display setting of the monitor (the first one by default). On DirectX, if `registry` is set, returns the default setting instead of the one changed by the application.

getDisplaySettings.haxe_doc: Returns the display settings available on the monitor (`monitor` by default), keeping only the ones of at least 720 pixels high and 60 Hz (or 30 Hz) when there are any.

setCurrent.haxe_doc: Makes this window the current one, returned by `getInstance`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a window. On HashLink: with the given title and size; flags: `fixed` disables resizing, `hidden` creates it hidden, `background` (DirectX) creates it without activating it. The main window is created by `hxd.System.createWindow`. On JS: for the given canvas, or for the `#webgl` canvas of the page. If `globalEvents` is set (or the canvas has the `globalEvents="1"` attribute), events are captured on the whole page instead of only the canvas.

class.haxe_doc: The application window, which receives the input events and resize notifications. On JS, it is a canvas of the page. Use `Window.getInstance()` to get the current window. Each target has its own implementation (`Window.hl.hx`, `Window.js.hx`).

Absolute.haxe_doc: Default mouse movement mode. Causes `EMove` events in window coordinates.

wantedFPS.haxe_doc: The FPS on which "tmod" have values are based on. Can be freely configured if your gameplay runs at a different speed. Default : 60

maxDeltaTime.haxe_doc: The maximum amount of time between two frames (in seconds). If the time exceed this amount, Timer will consider these lags are to be ignored. Default : 0.5

smoothFactor.haxe_doc: The smoothing done between frames. A smoothing of 0 gives "real time" values, higher values will smooth the results for tmod/dt/fps over frames using the formula dt = lerp(elapsedTime, dt, smoothFactor) Default : 0 on HashLink, 0.95 on other platforms

lastTimeStamp.haxe_doc: The last timestamp in which update() function was called.

elapsedTime.haxe_doc: The amount of time (unsmoothed) that was spent since the last frame.

frameCount.haxe_doc: A frame counter, increases on each call to update()

tmod.haxe_doc: The smoothed frame modifier, based on wantedFPS. Its value is the same as dt/wantedFPS Allows to express movements in terms of pixels-per-frame-at-wantedFPS instead of per second.

update.haxe_doc: Update the timer calculus on each frame. This is automatically called by hxd.App

skip.haxe_doc: After some loading / long processing, call skip() in order to prevent it from impacting your smoothed values.

reset.haxe_doc: Similar as skip() but also reset dt to default value. Can be used when starting a new game if you want to discard any previous measurement.

class.haxe_doc: The Timer class acts as a global time measurement that can be accessed from various parts of the engine. These three values are representation of the same underlying calculus: tmod, dt, fps

width.haxe_doc: The width of the screen in pixels (of the page on JS: the body width multiplied by the device pixel ratio).

height.haxe_doc: The height of the screen in pixels (of the page on JS: the body height multiplied by the device pixel ratio).

lang.haxe_doc: The language code of the user, such as `"en"`.

platform.haxe_doc: The platform the application runs on.

screenDPI.haxe_doc: The resolution of the screen in dots per inch (currently always `72`).

setCursor.haxe_doc: Sets the current cursor. It can be replaced by a custom function, which should call `setNativeCursor` with the cursor to display.

allowTimeout.haxe_doc: Tells if the infinite loop check is enabled. Set it to `false` to temporarily disable it during long computations.

allowLCID.haxe_doc: If set, `lang` keeps the region code for the locales that need it (such as `"zh-TW"` for traditional Chinese).

getCurrentLoop.haxe_doc: Returns the function called every frame, set with `setLoop`.

setLoop.haxe_doc: Sets the function called every frame by the main loop.

createWindow.haxe_doc: Creates the main window. Its size and title can be set with the `-D windowSize=WIDTHxHEIGHT`, `-D windowTitle=...` and `-D windowFixed=1` defines. Can be replaced to customize the window.

start.haxe_doc: Initializes the system and calls the given function. On HashLink, the window is created with `createWindow` first, and the main loop then runs until the application exits. Called by `hxd.App`.

onReload.haxe_doc: onReload() is called when app hot reload is enabled with -D hot-reload and is also enabled when running hashlink. The later can be done by running `hl --hot-reload` or by setting hotReload:true in VSCode launch props.

reportError.haxe_doc: Called when an uncaught exception occurs in the main loop. By default, writes the error and its call stack to stderr, and on Windows also shows them in a dialog. Can be replaced to log or report errors.

setNativeCursor.haxe_doc: Sets the displayed cursor. Meant to be called by a custom `setCursor`: calling it outside of the automatic interactive cursor update leads to undefined behavior.

getClipboardText.haxe_doc: Returns the text in the system clipboard, or `null` if not supported. On JS, returns the last text set with `setClipboardText`, since the browser clipboard can't be read synchronously.

setClipboardText.haxe_doc: Sets the text in the system clipboard. Returns `false` if not supported.

getDeviceName.haxe_doc: Returns a description of the device, such as `"PC/"` followed by the graphics device name (`"Unknown"` on JS).

getDefaultFrameRate.haxe_doc: Returns the default frame rate of the platform.

getValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value of a system property.

exit.haxe_doc: Exits the application (does nothing on JS).

openURL.haxe_doc: Opens the URL in the default browser (in a new tab on JS).

_loc.haxe_doc: * Returns the locale including region code ()

getLocale.haxe_doc: Returns the locale of the user, including the region code (such as `"en-US"`), based on the system or browser language.

getKeyboardLayout.haxe_doc: Returns the detected keyboard layout, or `Unknown` if it can't be detected (always on JS). The value isn't reliable on SDL without a window.

onKeyboardLayoutChange.haxe_doc: Called when the keyboard layout changes.

timeoutTick.haxe_doc: Notifies the infinite loop check that the application is still running. Call it frequently during long computations, or disable `allowTimeout`.

class.haxe_doc: Platform-specific services: main loop, cursor, clipboard, locale, and screen information. Each target has its own implementation (`System.hl.hx`, `System.js.hx`).

typedef.haxe_doc: How the window is displayed (see `Window.displayMode`). On HashLink, it is the display mode type of the native library (SDL or DirectX) when one is used.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the monitor, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the monitor, in pixels.

typedef.haxe_doc: A monitor, as returned by `Window.getMonitors`.

width.haxe_doc: The width, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height, in pixels.

typedef.haxe_doc: A display mode of a monitor: resolution and refresh rate.

Intersection.haxe_doc: The regions inside both the subject and the clip.

Union.haxe_doc: The regions inside the subject or the clip.

Difference.haxe_doc: The regions inside the subject but not the clip.

Xor.haxe_doc: The regions inside the subject or the clip, but not both.

enum.haxe_doc: The boolean operation of `Clipper.execute`, between the subject and the clip polygons.

clear.haxe_doc: Clears the tree.

enum.haxe_doc: The kind of polygon tree nodes to output: any, open or closed paths.
The polygons kept in the result: all of them, only the outer polygons, or only the holes.

Orientation.haxe_doc: Tells if the polygon has a positive (counter clockwise) orientation.

polArea.haxe_doc: Returns the signed area of the polygon.

SimplifyPolygon.haxe_doc: Removes the self intersections of the polygon, and returns the resulting simple polygons.

SimplifyPolygons.haxe_doc: Removes the self intersections of the polygons, and returns the resulting simple polygons.

MinkowskiSums.haxe_doc: Returns the Minkowski sums of the pattern swept along the polygons.

MinkowskiDiff.haxe_doc: Returns the Minkowski difference of the polygons.

strictlySimple.haxe_doc: If set, the result polygons are strictly simple (no touching vertices).

reverseSolution.haxe_doc: If set, the orientation of the result polygons is reversed.

resultKind.haxe_doc: The polygons kept in the result.

execute.haxe_doc: Computes the boolean operation between the subject and clip polygons, with the filling rules, and returns the result polygons.

ExecuteTree.haxe_doc: Computes the boolean operation into a tree of the result polygons and their holes.

PointInPolygon.haxe_doc: Returns `1` if the point is inside the polygon, `0` if it is outside, and `-1` if it is on its boundary.

CleanPolygon.haxe_doc: Removes the vertices closer than `distance` to their neighbors, and the collinear vertices.

CleanPolygons.haxe_doc: Removes the vertices closer than `distance` to their neighbors, and the collinear vertices, from the polygons.

MinkowskiSum.haxe_doc: Returns the Minkowski sum of the pattern swept along the polygon.

PolyTreeToPaths.haxe_doc: Returns the polygons of the tree.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a clipper.

class.haxe_doc: Polygon clipping (Angus Johnson's Clipper library 5.1.6): intersection, union, difference and xor of polygons with integer coordinates. Add the subject and clip polygons with `addPolygon`, then call `execute`. Used by `h2d.col.IPolygon`.

ArcTolerance.haxe_doc: The maximum distance between a round join and its approximation.

MiterLimit.haxe_doc: The maximum distance of a mitered corner, as a multiple of the offset, before it is squared.

resultKind.haxe_doc: The polygons kept in the result.

clear.haxe_doc: Removes the polygons.

addPolygon.haxe_doc: Adds a polygon with the join and end types.

addPolygons.haxe_doc: Adds polygons with the join and end types.

execute.haxe_doc: Returns the polygons offset by `delta` (negative to shrink).

new.haxe_doc: Creates an offsetter.

class.haxe_doc: Offsets (grows or shrinks) polygons and paths. Add them with `addPolygon`, then call `execute`.

ClosedPol.haxe_doc: The paths are closed polygons: both sides are offset.

ClosedLine.haxe_doc: The paths are closed lines: offset as an outline.

OpenButt.haxe_doc: Open paths with ends squared off at the end points.

OpenSquare.haxe_doc: Open paths with ends squared off, extended by the offset.

enum.haxe_doc: How the ends of the paths are handled by `ClipperOffset`: closed polygons, closed lines, or open paths with butt, square or round ends.

Miter.haxe_doc: Mitered (sharp) corners, limited by the miter limit.

enum.haxe_doc: How the corners are joined by `ClipperOffset`: square, round or mitered.

EvenOdd.haxe_doc: Inside when the winding number is odd.

NonZero.haxe_doc: Inside when the winding number is not zero.

Positive.haxe_doc: Inside when the winding number is positive.

Negative.haxe_doc: Inside when the winding number is negative.

enum.haxe_doc: The filling rule deciding which regions are inside the polygons, from their winding numbers.
The role of a polygon added to `Clipper`: subject or clip.

steiner.haxe_doc: Tells if the vertex is a Steiner point.

joint.haxe_doc: The joint created for the node.

skin.haxe_doc: The skinned mesh node of the joint.

rootJoints.haxe_doc: The root joints of a skinned mesh node.

wasRemoved.haxe_doc: Set when the model was removed from the hierarchy (such as an optimized joint).

transPos.haxe_doc: The bind transform of a joint.

fromMatrix.haxe_doc: Sets the transform from a matrix.

toMatrix.haxe_doc: Returns the matrix of the transform (converted to left handed if `leftHand` is set).

toQuaternion.haxe_doc: Returns the rotation of the transform (converted to left handed if `leftHand` is set).

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty transform.

class.haxe_doc: The default transform of a FBX model: translation, scale, rotation and pre-rotation.

fileName.haxe_doc: The path of the FBX file.

version.haxe_doc: The FBX version that was decoded

keepJoints.haxe_doc: Allows to prevent some terminal unskinned joints to be removed, for instance if we want to track their position

skipObjects.haxe_doc: Allows to skip some objects from being processed as if they were not part of the FBX

fourBonesByVertex.haxe_doc: Use 4 bones of influence per vertex instead of 3

maxBonesPerSkin.haxe_doc: If there are too many bones, the model will be split in separate render passes.

unskinnedJointsAsObjects.haxe_doc: Consider unskinned joints to be simple objects

allowVertexColor.haxe_doc: If set, the vertex colors are imported.

normalizeScaleOrient.haxe_doc: Convert centimeters to meters and axis to Z-up (Maya FBX export)

highPrecision.haxe_doc: Keep high precision values. Might increase animation data size and compressed size.

legacyScaleAxisConversion.haxe_doc: Use the legacy system to convert scale and axis of FBX file

legacySkinImport.haxe_doc: Use the legacy system to import skinned mesh of FBX file

leftHandConvert.haxe_doc: Converts the data from right handed to left handed coordinates, by flipping the X axis.

getChilds.haxe_doc: Returns the children of the node (of the given node type if set).

getParents.haxe_doc: Returns the parents of the node (of the given node type if set).

getRoot.haxe_doc: Returns the root of the FBX data.

mergeModels.haxe_doc: Merges the geometries of the given models into the first one.

getAnimationNames.haxe_doc: Returns an array of names with all animations present in FBX file.

loadAnimation.haxe_doc: Loads the animation of the given name (the first one by default), from this library, another FBX data (`root`), or another library (`lib`) applied to this skeleton.

getAll.haxe_doc: Returns all the descendant nodes at the path.

getInts.haxe_doc: Returns the integer array of the node.

getFloats.haxe_doc: Returns the float array of the node (converting an integer array).
